fams.label: Painting
fams.test: a picture made by laying paint or ink on a movable flat support — paper, vellum, panel, canvas, cloth or silk. Wall painting fixed to a building is L.
key: 1. Small-format opaque watercolour or ink on paper or vellum, made for a book or an album? → A1.
2. Ink and colour with the brush on silk or paper in the East Asian formats (hanging scroll, handscroll, screen, album)? → A2.
3. A devotional image on a wooden panel in the icon tradition? → A3. A painting on cloth made to be hung or carried (thangka, pata, phad)? → A4.
4. Oil, tempera or acrylic on canvas or panel in the easel tradition and its modern and contemporary lineages? → A5.
5. A folk or popular painting named as its own tradition (reverse glass, coffeehouse painting, bark painting)? → A6.

subs.label: Manuscript & Album Painting
subs.axis: Axis: the painting tradition (a court and school lineage). Small-format pictures in opaque watercolour or ink on paper or vellum, made to illustrate a book or to be mounted in an album (miniature painting).

leaves.label: Arab Painting
leaves.defn: manuscript painting of the Arab lands from the 12th to the 15th century: illustrated scientific texts, the Maqamat of al-Hariri and Kalila wa Dimna, made in Baghdad, Mosul, Syria and Mamluk Egypt (al-Wasiti's 1237 Maqamat).
leaves.aliases: Arabic miniature; Baghdad school; Mesopotamian school

leaves.label: Persian Miniature
leaves.defn: Persian manuscript and album painting from the Mongol conquest to the 19th century, taught in court workshops whose schools are named after their centres (Herat, Tabriz, Qazvin, Isfahan, Shiraz, Bukhara); kinds are those schools and their masters (Bihzad, Sultan Muhammad, Riza-yi 'Abbasi).
leaves.see: A1-3 Ottoman Miniature; A1-4 Mughal Painting; I2-1 Persian Lacquer.
alias_rows: Shahnameh and Persian illustrated epics (see islamic_world.py)
Attributed to Safavid master Sultan Muhammad
Attributed to Muhammad Qasim, died Hegira 1070 / AD 1659/60 (miniature)

leaves.label: Ottoman Miniature
leaves.defn: painting of the Ottoman court workshop (nakkaşhane) for histories, festival books and albums, from Mehmed II to the 18th century (Matrakçı Nasuh's topographies, Nakkaş Osman's Hünername, Levni's Surname-i Vehbi).

leaves.label: Mughal Painting
leaves.defn: painting of the Mughal court atelier and its offshoots in South Asia, 16th–19th century: the Hamzanama and the illustrated histories of Akbar, Jahangir's portraits and natural history, and the sub-imperial and provincial schools (Lucknow, Murshidabad).
leaves.see: A1-5 Deccan Painting; A1-6 Company Painting.
alias_rows: Attributed to Manôhar and his studio

leaves.label: Deccan Painting
leaves.defn: painting of the Deccan sultanates (Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda) and of Hyderabad after them, 16th–19th century, with its lyrical colour and Persian, Turkman and Vijayanagara sources.

leaves.label: Company Painting
leaves.defn: paintings made by Indian artists for officials of the East India Company and other Europeans, 18th–19th century, in a hybrid of Mughal technique and European natural history and topography (Delhi, Lucknow, Patna, Murshidabad, Tanjore).

leaves.label: Rajput Painting
leaves.defn: Court painting of the Rajput kingdoms of Rajasthan and Central India, 16th–19th century, in schools named for their courts: Mewar Ragamala sets, Bundi and Kota hunting scenes, Kishangarh portraits of Radha, Jodhpur durbar paintings.

leaves.label: Pahari Painting
leaves.defn: Painting of the Hindu courts of the Punjab Hills, 17th–19th century, from the bold Basohli Rasamanjari to the lyrical Guler and Kangra Gita Govinda and Bhagavata Purana series of the family of Pandit Seu.

leaves.label: Jain Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: The Western Indian style of manuscript painting on palm leaf and then paper (11th–16th century), chiefly Jain scriptures with angular figures and projecting far eyes: Kalpasutra, Kalakacharyakatha, painted wooden covers (patli).
leaves.aliases: Western Indian style;Jain painting;Western Indian painting

leaves.label: Sikh Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in the Punjab under Sikh patronage, late 18th–19th century, in Pahari and Company-influenced idioms: portraits of Ranjit Singh and his court, Janamsakhi illustrations, Gurus series.

leaves.label: Assamese Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of Assam on sanchipat (agarwood-bark) folios, 16th–19th century, in sattriya and Ahom court styles: Hastividyarnava, illustrated Bhagavata.

leaves.label: Burmese Parabaik Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in watercolour on white parabaik (folding books of mulberry paper) by the royal and monastic painters of Konbaung Burma, 18th–19th century: court ceremonies and processions, Life of the Buddha, Jataka cycles, cosmologies.

leaves.label: Thai Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: Paintings in gouache and gold on khoi-paper folding books of Siam, late 17th–19th century, chiefly funerary chanting books: Phra Malai manuscripts, Traiphum cosmologies, Ten Great Jatakas.
leaves.aliases: samut khoi painting;Phra Malai manuscript painting

leaves.label: Nara-ehon
leaves.defn: Illustrated books and scrolls of tales painted in bright mineral colours by largely anonymous town painters of Kyoto, late 16th–18th century: Tales of Ise, Bunshō zōshi, otogi-zōshi booklets.
leaves.weak: Nara-ehon redirects to E-hon; anonymous workshop tradition, so built here rather than in the artist pass

leaves.label: Ethiopian Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Ethiopian Christian manuscripts on parchment, from the Aksumite-era gospel books to the Gondarine Marian miracle books: Garima Gospels evangelist portraits, Miracles of Mary (Täammərä Maryam) cycles, illustrated Psalters.

leaves.label: Byzantine Illuminated Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Painted miniatures in Greek manuscripts of the Byzantine empire, 4th–15th century, from late antique codices to the classicising Macedonian Renaissance and Palaiologan books: Vienna Dioscurides, Rossano Gospels, Paris Psalter, Menologion of Basil II.

leaves.label: Borgia Group
leaves.defn: The pre-Hispanic ritual and divinatory screenfold codices painted on deerskin in the Mixteca-Puebla style of central Mexico, 14th–early 16th century: Codex Borgia, Codex Laud, Codex Fejérváry-Mayer, Codex Cospi.
leaves.see: A1-18 Mixtec Codices;A1-19 Aztec Codices;C2-16 Maya Codices

leaves.label: Mixtec Codices
leaves.defn: Genealogical and historical screenfold codices painted on deerskin by Mixtec (Ñudzavui) tlacuiloque of Oaxaca, 14th–16th century: Codex Zouche-Nuttall, Codex Vindobonensis Mexicanus I, Codex Bodley, Codex Colombino.

leaves.label: Aztec Codices
leaves.defn: Pictorial manuscripts of the Nahua of central Mexico, from the few pre-Hispanic and early colonial ritual books to the colonial histories, tribute rolls and encyclopedias painted by indigenous tlacuiloque: Codex Borbonicus, Codex Mendoza, Florentine Codex, Codex Azcatitlan.

leaves.label: Armenian Manuscript Illumination
leaves.defn: Painting and ornament of Armenian Gospel books and service books from the 10th to the 18th century, taught in monastic schools named after their regions: Etchmiadzin Gospels, Mugni Gospels, Toros Roslin's Gospels, Glajor Gospels.
leaves.weak: enwiki Armenian manuscript illumination redirects to Armenian illuminated manuscripts; schools (Cilician, Vaspurakan, Glajor, Tatev, Crimean, New Julfa) are kinds; routed europe_folk_east rows attach here

subs.label: East Asian Ink & Colour Painting
subs.axis: Axis: school and lineage. Built at scale (Chinese, Japanese and Korean painting).

leaves.label: Gongbi
leaves.defn: The meticulous, finely outlined and coloured manner of Chinese court and academy painting from the Tang and Song: Emperor Huizong's Auspicious Cranes, Zhang Zeduan's Along the River during the Qingming Festival.

leaves.label: Northern Landscape Style
leaves.defn: The monumental landscape painting of the Five Dynasties and Northern Song: Fan Kuan's Travelers among Mountains and Streams, Guan Tong's Waiting for the Ferry.

leaves.label: Literati Painting
leaves.defn: Scholar-amateur painting of China (wenrenhua) and its Korean and Japanese reflexes, valuing brushwork, poetry and calligraphy over likeness: Ni Zan's Rongxi Studio, Huang Gongwang's Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains, Dong Qichang's landscapes.
leaves.aliases: Southern School;wenrenhua;scholar painting;Chinese landscape painting;shanshui;Chinese scroll painting

leaves.label: Zhe School
leaves.defn: The professional Ming school of landscape continuing Southern Song Ma–Xia painting (15th–16th century): Dai Jin's Returning Home Late from a Spring Outing, Wu Wei's figures.

leaves.label: Wu School
leaves.defn: The Ming literati school of Suzhou (15th–16th century) around Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming: Shen Zhou's Lofty Mount Lu, Wen Zhengming's Old Trees by a Cold Waterfall.

leaves.label: Shanghai School
leaves.defn: The commercial-literati painting of late Qing Shanghai, bold in colour and subject: Ren Bonian's portraits, Wu Changshuo's flowers.

leaves.label: Lingnan School
leaves.defn: The Cantonese school (early 20th century) of the Gao brothers and Chen Shuren that joined Chinese brushwork with Japanese and Western realism: Gao Jianfu's Flying in the Rain, Zhao Shao'ang's birds.

leaves.label: Yamato-e
leaves.defn: The classical Japanese narrative and court painting style from the Heian period, continued by the Tosa school: the Tale of Genji scrolls, the Shigisan engi emaki, Tosa Mitsuoki's Quail and Millet.

leaves.label: Kanō School
leaves.defn: The hereditary school of Japanese official painting (15th–19th century) joining Chinese ink and Yamato-e colour: Kanō Eitoku's Cypress Trees, Kanō Tan'yū's Nijō Castle screens.

leaves.label: Rinpa School
leaves.defn: The decorative Japanese school of Sōtatsu, Kōrin and Hōitsu (17th–19th century): Sōtatsu's Wind God and Thunder God, Kōrin's Irises.

leaves.label: Nanga
leaves.defn: Japanese literati painting (bunjinga) of the later Edo period and its Meiji continuation: Ike no Taiga and Yosa Buson's Ten Conveniences and Ten Pleasures, Uragami Gyokudō's Frozen Clouds.

leaves.label: Maruyama–Shijō School
leaves.defn: The naturalistic Kyoto painting of Maruyama Ōkyo and Matsumura Goshun (from the 1770s) and its modern heirs: Ōkyo's Pine Trees in Snow, Goshun's Woodcutters and Fishermen.

leaves.label: Nihonga
leaves.defn: Modern Japanese-style painting (from the 1880s) in mineral pigments and ink on silk and paper: Hishida Shunsō's Fallen Leaves, Yokoyama Taikan's works, Uemura Shōen's Flame.

leaves.label: Ink Wash Painting
leaves.defn: Monochrome ink painting of the Zen monasteries of Muromachi Japan (suibokuga), after Song and Yuan models: Mokuan Reien's Four Sleepers, Josetsu's Catching a Catfish with a Gourd, Sesshū's Landscape of the Four Seasons.
leaves.see: T3 Literati Painting;T9 Kanō School;T11 Nanga
leaves.weak: Suibokuga and Sumi-e redirect to Ink wash painting; used for Japanese painters born 1300–1499 with no school

subs.label: Icon Painting
subs.axis: Axis: school. Built at scale (Byzantine, Russian, Ethiopian, Cretan icons).

leaves.label: Ethiopian Icon Painting
leaves.defn: Panel painting of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church from the 15th century, in tempera on gessoed wood (later over glued cloth), as diptychs, triptychs and processional icons, in the styles named First and Second Gondarine: Virgin and Child with archangels, St George on horseback, Kwer'ata Re'esu.

leaves.label: Byzantine Icons
leaves.defn: Devotional images painted in encaustic or egg tempera on wooden panels in the Byzantine empire and its orbit, 6th–15th century: Sinai Christ Pantokrator, Theotokos of Vladimir, Hodegetria and Deesis icons.

leaves.label: Cretan School
leaves.defn: Post-Byzantine icon painting of Venetian Crete, 15th–17th century, joining the Palaiologan manner with Italian elements: icons of Andreas Ritzos and Michael Damaskinos, Theophanes the Cretan's Athonite murals.

leaves.label: Georgian Icon Painting
leaves.defn: Painted panel icons of medieval and early modern Georgia, from the 10th century, often set in chased silver revetments: icons of Svaneti, Gelati iconostasis, Georgian icons at Sinai.
leaves.weak: no English Wikipedia article; attested by art-historical article (N. Chichinadze); leaf made for the routed europe_folk_east row 'Georgian / icon painting'

leaves.label: Palaeologan Renaissance
leaves.defn: Late Byzantine painting (1261–1453), classicising and intensely expressive in icons and frescoes: the Chora Church frescoes, Theophanes the Greek's icons.

leaves.label: Russian Icons
leaves.defn: Icon painting of Rus' and Muscovy and its schools (Novgorod, Moscow, Vologda, Stroganov): Rublev's Trinity, Dionisius's Ferapontov icons.

subs.label: Cloth & Scroll Painting
subs.axis: Axis: tradition. Built at scale (thangka, pata, phad, kalighat).

leaves.label: Pattachitra
leaves.defn: Cloth-based painting of Odisha by the chitrakar community of Puri and Raghurajpur, in mineral colour on gum-and-chalk-primed cotton: Jagannath images, Gita Govinda panels, palm-leaf pothis.

leaves.label: Bengal Patachitra
leaves.defn: The narrative scroll painting of the patuas (chitrakars) of West Bengal and Bangladesh, unrolled frame by frame while the painter sings (pater gaan): Manasamangal scrolls, Jadupatua scrolls of the Santal.

leaves.label: Kalighat Painting
leaves.defn: Watercolours on mill paper sold by patua painters at the Kalighat temple in Calcutta, 19th–early 20th century, with bold outlines and satire of urban life: Durga and Kali icons, Tarakeswar scandal, babu and courtesan pictures.

leaves.label: Pichwai
leaves.defn: Large painted cloth hangings made at Nathdwara to hang behind the image of Shrinathji: Sharad Purnima, Annakut, cows and lotus ponds.

leaves.label: Mata ni Pachedi
leaves.defn: Ritual cloth shrines of the Vaghri community of Ahmedabad, hand-painted and block-printed in red and black around the Mother Goddess: Mata on her vahana, temple cloth panels.

leaves.label: Cheriyal Scroll Painting
leaves.defn: Narrative scrolls of Cheriyal in Telangana painted for the bardic storytellers of the Kaki Padagollu: Markandeya Purana scrolls, Gauda Purana.

leaves.label: Thangka
leaves.defn: Buddhist painting on cotton or silk mounted in a textile frame to be hung, rolled and carried, the principal portable painting of Tibet, Bhutan, Ladakh and Mongolia: deity and lineage portraits, mandalas, wheel-of-life paintings, appliqué festival thangkas.
leaves.see: A4-8 Beri;A4-9 Menri;A4-10 Khyenri;A4-11 Karma Gadri;A4-13 Paubha;L2-13

leaves.label: Beri
leaves.defn: The Newar-derived style of Tibetan painting (13th–15th century) and its later continuations, with dense red and blue grounds and Nepalese figure canons: Sakya lineage thangkas, Ngor mandala sets.

leaves.label: Menri
leaves.defn: The central Tibetan painting tradition founded by Menla Döndrub (15th century), with Chinese-inspired landscape and a canon of peaceful deities, renewed as New Menri by Choying Gyatso at Tashi Lhunpo (17th century): arhat sets, lineage paintings.

leaves.label: Khyenri
leaves.defn: The central Tibetan painting style created by Khyentse Chenmo of Gongkar Chöde (15th century), known for wrathful deities, bright palettes and near-circular haloes: Gongkar Chöde murals, wrathful protector thangkas.

leaves.label: Karma Gadri
leaves.defn: The 'encampment' painting tradition of the Karma Kagyu, founded by Namkha Tashi (16th century) and renewed by Situ Panchen at Palpung (18th century), with open Chinese-style landscapes and pale grounds: Situ Panchen's Eight Great Mahasiddhas, Tenth Karmapa paintings.

leaves.label: Regong Arts
leaves.defn: The thangka painting (with murals, sculpture and appliqué) of the monastic artists of Rebkong (Tongren) in Amdo, from the 17th century to the present, on UNESCO's list since 2009: Wutun monastery thangkas, contemporary Rebkong painting.

leaves.label: Paubha
leaves.defn: Newar Buddhist and Hindu painting on cloth of the Kathmandu Valley, from the 12th century to the present, with flat red grounds and donor registers: Vasudhara mandalas, Chakrasamvara paubhas, long narrative vratha paintings.

leaves.label: Dunhuang Paintings
leaves.defn: The portable Buddhist paintings and banners on silk, hemp and paper deposited in the Library Cave (Cave 17) at the Mogao Caves, 8th–10th century: Tejaprabha and the Five Planets (897), bodhisattva banners, Famous Images of the Buddha.

leaves.label: Kamasan Painting
leaves.defn: The classical wayang-style painting of Kamasan village in Klungkung, Bali, on cloth and bark paper for temples and palaces since the Gelgel court (16th century): ider-ider friezes, langse hangings, palelintangan calendars, Kerta Gosa ceilings.
leaves.aliases: Kamasan wayang painting;wayang style painting;sangging Kamasan

leaves.label: Wayang Beber
leaves.defn: Javanese narrative scroll painting on dluwang bark paper, unrolled scene by scene by a dalang: Panji scrolls of Pacitan and Gunung Kidul.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Magic Scrolls
leaves.defn: Protective parchment scrolls cut to the owner's height and painted by däbtära (church-trained scholars) with talismanic figures, eyes, angels and nets beside Ge'ez prayers: healing scrolls, talismanic eyes and faces, Solomon's net designs.

leaves.label: Plains Hide Painting
leaves.defn: Painting on tanned or raw hide by the peoples of the Great Plains: men's figurative war-exploit and calendar painting and women's geometric designs, on painted buffalo robes, tipi covers and liners, parfleches and winter counts.

subs.label: Easel Painting
subs.axis: Axis: period style, school or movement. Built at scale for the European lineage and modern and contemporary painting; the pilot holds one non-European court tradition.

leaves.label: Qajar Painting
leaves.defn: court painting of Qajar Iran (1789–1925) in oil on canvas and in watercolour: life-size royal portraits and figures of pleasure (Mihr 'Ali), and the realist watercolours of Abu'l-Hasan Ghaffari (Sani' al-Mulk).
leaves.see: A1-2 Persian Miniature; I2-1 Persian Lacquer.

leaves.label: Balinese Painting
leaves.defn: The modern painting of Bali from the late 1920s on paper and canvas, in the village schools that grew up around the Pita Maha association: Ubud genre and landscape, Batuan dense ink-and-wash scenes, Lempad's line drawings.
leaves.weak: the Balinese painting article redirects to Balinese art; woodcarving of Mas in the source row has no leaf yet

leaves.label: Sơn Mài
leaves.defn: Vietnamese lacquer painting on panel, developed as a fine art at the École des Beaux-Arts de l'Indochine from the 1930s: landscape and genre panels, gold- and eggshell-inlaid screens.

leaves.label: Fayum Mummy Portraits
leaves.defn: Portraits painted in encaustic or tempera on wooden panels and bound over the faces of mummies in Roman Egypt, 1st–3rd century: Hawara and Er-Rubayat portraits, Tomb of Aline, portraits from Antinoöpolis.

leaves.label: New Spanish Baroque
leaves.defn: The painting of the Viceroyalty of New Spain in the Baroque idiom, 17th–18th century, from the large altarpieces and sacristy canvases of Mexico City to devotional and civic pictures: Villalpando's Puebla cathedral dome, Juan Correa's sacristy canvases, Miguel Cabrera's Virgins of Guadalupe.
leaves.see: A5-6 Casta Painting;A5-7 Enconchado;A5-8 Biombo;A5-9 Cusco School

leaves.label: Casta Painting
leaves.defn: Sets of paintings made in 18th-century New Spain (and occasionally Peru) depicting the hierarchy of racial mixtures as family groups with their dress and produce: Miguel Cabrera's casta series (1763), José de Páez series.

leaves.label: Enconchado
leaves.defn: Paintings of late 17th- and early 18th-century New Spain in oil on panel with inlaid fragments of mother-of-pearl under translucent glazes, influenced by Japanese namban lacquer: González family Conquest of Mexico series, Virgin of Guadalupe (1698).
leaves.see: A5-5 New Spanish Baroque;A5-8 Biombo;I2-15 Mexican Lacquerware
leaves.weak: pool QID Q135448181 not verified; Met object record names the technique

leaves.label: Biombo
leaves.defn: Painted folding screens made in New Spain from the early 17th century after Japanese byōbu, with views of Mexico City, the Conquest and festivities: Biombo of the Conquest and View of Mexico City, Indian wedding and flying pole screen.

leaves.label: Cusco School
leaves.defn: The school of religious painting centred on Cusco in the Viceroyalty of Peru, 16th–18th century, with Andean painters working from Flemish prints and adding brocade gold (brocateado) and local flora: Corpus Christi series, archangel arquebusiers, Diego Quispe Tito's zodiac series.
leaves.see: A5-10 Potosí School;A5-11 Quito School;A5-5 New Spanish Baroque

leaves.label: Potosí School
leaves.defn: The school of painting of the silver city of Potosí in Upper Peru (Bolivia), 17th–18th century, led by Melchor Pérez de Holguín: Entry of Viceroy Morcillo into Potosí, Virgin of the Cerro.

leaves.label: Quito School
leaves.defn: The painting and polychrome sculpture of the Audiencia of Quito, 16th–18th century, known for its realist carved and estofado images and its painting workshops: Miguel de Santiago's Augustinian series, Legarda's winged Virgin of Quito, Caspicara's sculptural groups.

leaves.label: Western Desert Painting
leaves.defn: The acrylic painting movement of the Central and Western Desert begun at Papunya in 1971, in which Dreaming (Tjukurrpa/Jukurrpa) designs once made in sand, body paint and ceremony are painted on canvas and board in dotted and concentric-circle fields, carried on by community art centres: Papunya Tula boards, Warlukurlangu Jukurrpa canvases, Utopia and APY Lands painting.
leaves.aliases: Western Desert art movement;dot painting;Papunya Tula painting;acrylic desert painting
leaves.weak: Western Desert art movement and Dot painting both redirect to Papunya Tula; art centres are kinds; Utopia (Anmatyerre/Alyawarr, Arandic) is placed here by convention as Central Desert painting

leaves.label: Contemporary Indigenous Australian Art
leaves.defn: Painting by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists from the 1970s onward outside the Western Desert and bark-painting lineages, in ochre and acrylic on canvas, worked through community art centres: Warmun (Turkey Creek) ochre paintings, Mangkaja and Ngukurr acrylics, Mornington Island painting, Mowanjum Wandjina paintings.

leaves.label: Hermannsburg School
leaves.defn: The Western Arrernte watercolour landscape school of the Hermannsburg mission (from 1934), founded by Albert Namatjira after lessons with Rex Battarbee and carried on by his family and followers: MacDonnell Ranges landscapes, ghost gums.

leaves.label: Romanesque Painting
leaves.defn: Panel, book and wall painting of Latin Europe in the 11th–12th centuries, with flat, linear, hieratic figures: the Master of Pedret, painted altar frontals of Catalonia, the Registrum Gregorii.

leaves.label: Gothic Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Latin Europe from the 13th to the late 14th century, from Italo-Byzantine panel crosses to the narrative altarpieces of Giotto and his followers: Coppo di Marcovaldo's crucifixes, Giotto's Ognissanti Madonna, Catalan Gothic retables.

leaves.label: Sienese School
leaves.defn: The school of painting of Siena, 13th–15th century, with its gold grounds, lyrical line and colour: Duccio's Maestà, Simone Martini's Annunciation, Lorenzetti's Allegory of Good Government.

leaves.label: International Gothic
leaves.defn: The courtly late Gothic style shared by painters across Europe c. 1375–1425, elegant, decorative and richly detailed: the Wilton Diptych, Gentile da Fabriano's Adoration of the Magi, the Très Riches Heures.
leaves.see: T18 Gothic Painting;T21 Early Netherlandish Painting

leaves.label: Early Netherlandish Painting
leaves.defn: Oil painting of the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands in the 15th and early 16th centuries, with minute naturalism and luminous glazes: the Ghent Altarpiece, the Arnolfini Portrait, Rogier van der Weyden's Descent from the Cross.

leaves.label: Italian Renaissance Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Italy c. 1400–1530, from the perspective and naturalism of the Florentine Early Renaissance to the High Renaissance: Masaccio's Trinity, Piero della Francesca's Flagellation, Leonardo's Last Supper, Raphael's School of Athens.
leaves.see: T23 Venetian School;T25 Mannerism;T24 Northern Renaissance

leaves.label: Venetian School
leaves.defn: The painting of Venice and its terraferma from the Bellini to the 18th century, built on colour and light: Giovanni Bellini's San Zaccaria Altarpiece, Giorgione's Tempest, Titian's Assumption, Veronese's Wedding at Cana.

leaves.label: Northern Renaissance
leaves.defn: The Renaissance north of the Alps (German lands, the Low Countries, France, England), c. 1490–1580: Dürer's Self-Portrait of 1500, the Isenheim Altarpiece, Holbein's Ambassadors, Bruegel's Hunters in the Snow.
leaves.aliases: German Renaissance;Dutch and Flemish Renaissance painting;French Renaissance

leaves.label: Mannerism
leaves.defn: The artificial, elongated and complex style that followed the High Renaissance, c. 1520–1600: Pontormo's Deposition, Parmigianino's Madonna with the Long Neck, Bronzino's Allegory with Venus and Cupid.
leaves.see: T26 School of Fontainebleau;T27 Baroque Painting

leaves.label: School of Fontainebleau
leaves.defn: The Mannerist decoration and painting of the French court at Fontainebleau, led by Rosso and Primaticcio (c. 1530–1610): the Galerie François I, Gabrielle d'Estrées and One of Her Sisters.

leaves.label: Baroque Painting
leaves.defn: European painting of the 17th and early 18th centuries, dramatic in light, movement and emotion, from Rome to Madrid and the colonial Americas: Rubens's Elevation of the Cross, Velázquez's Las Meninas, Pietro da Cortona's Barberini ceiling.
leaves.see: T28 Caravaggisti;T29 Flemish Baroque Painting;T30 Dutch Golden Age Painting;T31 Rococo

leaves.label: Caravaggisti
leaves.defn: Followers of Caravaggio's dramatic tenebrism and naturalism across Europe, c. 1600–1640: Gentileschi's Judith Slaying Holofernes, Ter Brugghen's Calling of Saint Matthew, Valentin de Boulogne's Concert.

leaves.label: Flemish Baroque Painting
leaves.defn: Painting of the Southern Netherlands c. 1585–1700 around Rubens, van Dyck and Jordaens: Rubens's Descent from the Cross, van Dyck's Charles I at the Hunt, Snyders's market stalls.
leaves.see: T27 Baroque Painting;T30 Dutch Golden Age Painting

leaves.label: Dutch Golden Age Painting
leaves.defn: Painting of the Dutch Republic in the 17th century, its genres sold on an open market: Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's View of Delft, Ruisdael's Jewish Cemetery, Heda's breakfast pieces.
leaves.see: T29 Flemish Baroque Painting;T27 Baroque Painting

leaves.label: Rococo
leaves.defn: The light, ornamental, intimate style of the 18th century, from the French fêtes galantes to Venetian ceilings: Watteau's Pilgrimage to Cythera, Fragonard's The Swing, Tiepolo's Würzburg ceiling.

leaves.label: Neoclassicism
leaves.defn: Painting of the later 18th and early 19th century modelled on antiquity, severe in line and moral in subject: David's Oath of the Horatii, Mengs's Parnassus, Ingres's Grande Odalisque.

leaves.label: Romanticism
leaves.defn: Painting c. 1780–1850 that put feeling, the sublime and the imagination before rule: Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, Géricault's Raft of the Medusa, Delacroix's Liberty Leading the People, Turner's Slave Ship.
leaves.see: T32 Neoclassicism;T40 Academic Art;T34 Nazarene Movement

leaves.label: Nazarene Movement
leaves.defn: German Romantic painters in Rome (from 1809) who revived the religious art of Dürer and early Raphael: Overbeck's Italia and Germania, the Casa Bartholdy frescoes.

leaves.label: Danish Golden Age
leaves.defn: Danish painting of the first half of the 19th century, around Eckersberg and his pupils: Købke's View of Lake Sortedam, Eckersberg's views of Rome.

leaves.label: Düsseldorf School of Painting
leaves.defn: Painters trained at the Düsseldorf Academy c. 1819–1918, known for detailed landscapes and history scenes: Achenbach's seascapes, Leutze's Washington Crossing the Delaware.

leaves.label: Barbizon School
leaves.defn: French landscape painters working from nature in the forest of Fontainebleau c. 1830–1870: Rousseau's Forest of Fontainebleau, Millet's The Gleaners, Corot's Souvenir de Mortefontaine.

leaves.label: Hudson River School
leaves.defn: American Romantic landscape painting c. 1825–1875: Cole's The Oxbow, Church's Heart of the Andes, Bierstadt's Rocky Mountains.

leaves.label: Norwich School of Painters
leaves.defn: The regional landscape school of Norwich (1803–1833) around John Crome and John Sell Cotman: Crome's Mousehold Heath, Cotman's Greta Bridge.

leaves.label: Academic Art
leaves.defn: Painting shaped by the European academies and their Salons in the 19th century, finished, idealising and hierarchical in subject: Cabanel's Birth of Venus, Bouguereau's Nymphs and Satyr, Gérôme's Pollice Verso.

leaves.label: Neo-Grec
leaves.defn: A mid-19th-century French current of small-scale, archaeologically detailed antique genre scenes: Gérôme's Cock Fight, Hamon's My Sister Is Not In.

leaves.label: Realism
leaves.defn: The mid-19th-century movement that painted contemporary life and labour without idealisation: Courbet's A Burial at Ornans, Millet's The Angelus, Repin's Barge Haulers on the Volga.

leaves.label: Costumbrismo
leaves.defn: Spanish and Latin American painting of local customs, types and manners in the 19th century: Bécquer's Andalusian scenes, Pancho Fierro's Lima watercolours.

leaves.label: Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood
leaves.defn: The English brotherhood (1848) and its circle that painted with the detail and colour of art before Raphael: Millais's Ophelia, Rossetti's Beata Beatrix, Hunt's The Light of the World.

leaves.label: Hague School
leaves.defn: Dutch painters working in The Hague c. 1860–1900 in grey-toned realist landscape and genre: Mesdag's Panorama, Mauve's Morning Ride on the Beach.

leaves.label: Macchiaioli
leaves.defn: Tuscan painters of the 1850s–1870s who built pictures from patches (macchie) of light and shade: Fattori's The Rotonda di Palmieri, Lega's The Visit.

leaves.label: Naturalism
leaves.defn: Late-19th-century plein-air painting of rural and working life with photographic truth: Bastien-Lepage's Haymaking, Stanhope Forbes's A Fish Sale on a Cornish Beach, the Skagen Painters.

leaves.label: Munich School
leaves.defn: Painters trained at the Munich Academy c. 1850–1914 in dark, painterly realism: Leibl's Three Women in Church, Gyzis's works, Chase's early portraits.

leaves.label: Impressionism
leaves.defn: The French movement of the 1860s–1880s that painted modern life and light in broken colour outdoors, and its national offshoots: Monet's Impression, Sunrise, Renoir's Bal du moulin de la Galette, Morisot's The Cradle.

leaves.label: Neo-Impressionism
leaves.defn: The systematic colour-division of Seurat and Signac from 1886 and its Italian divisionist branch: Seurat's A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Signac's Portrait of Félix Fénéon.

leaves.label: Post-Impressionism
leaves.defn: Painting after Impressionism c. 1886–1905 that turned colour and form to structure and expression: Cézanne's Mont Sainte-Victoire, Van Gogh's Starry Night, Gauguin's Vision after the Sermon.

leaves.label: Pont-Aven School
leaves.defn: Painters around Gauguin and Émile Bernard in Brittany from 1886, flat colour and bounding line (synthetism, cloisonnism): Bernard's Breton Women in the Meadow, Sérusier's The Talisman.

leaves.label: Symbolism
leaves.defn: Late-19th-century painting of dream, myth and inner states: Moreau's The Apparition, Redon's The Cyclops, Khnopff's I Lock My Door Upon Myself.
leaves.see: T44 Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood;T168 Art Nouveau;T54 Aestheticism

leaves.label: Aestheticism
leaves.defn: The British "art for art's sake" painting of the 1860s–1890s: Whistler's Symphony in White, Leighton's Flaming June, Albert Moore's Midsummer.

leaves.label: Tonalism
leaves.defn: American (and Australian) landscape painting c. 1880–1915 in muted, atmospheric tones: Inness's Home of the Heron, Dewing's The Recitation.

leaves.label: Luminism
leaves.defn: American landscape painting c. 1850–1875 of calm, hidden-brushwork light: Fitz Henry Lane's Owl's Head, Heade's Approaching Thunder Storm.

leaves.label: Glasgow School
leaves.defn: The Glasgow Boys (c. 1880–1900), Scottish painters of plein-air naturalism and decorative colour: Guthrie's A Highland Funeral, Henry and Hornel's The Druids.

leaves.label: Expressionism
leaves.defn: Painting from c. 1905 that distorted colour and form for emotional force, centred in Germany and Austria: Kirchner's Street, Berlin, Kokoschka's The Bride of the Wind, Marc's Blue Horse.

leaves.label: Fauvism
leaves.defn: The French painting of pure, arbitrary colour around Matisse and Derain, 1904–1908: Matisse's Woman with a Hat, Derain's Charing Cross Bridge.

leaves.label: Cubism
leaves.defn: The movement of Picasso and Braque (from 1907) that fractured objects into planes and multiple viewpoints, with its Salon Cubist and Section d'Or circles: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Braque's Violin and Candlestick, Gris's Portrait of Picasso.

leaves.label: Futurism
leaves.defn: The Italian movement (1909) celebrating speed, machines and the city, and its Russian Cubo-Futurist branch: Boccioni's The City Rises, Balla's Dynamism of a Dog on a Leash, Severini's Armoured Train.

leaves.label: Orphism
leaves.defn: Abstract painting of prismatic colour around Robert and Sonia Delaunay and Kupka, c. 1912: Robert Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows, Kupka's Amorpha.

leaves.label: Vorticism
leaves.defn: The British avant-garde of 1914–1915 around Wyndham Lewis and the magazine BLAST: Bomberg's The Mud Bath, Lewis's The Crowd.

leaves.label: Suprematism
leaves.defn: Malevich's abstraction of pure geometric forms from 1915: Black Square, Suprematist Composition: White on White.

leaves.label: Constructivism
leaves.defn: The Russian movement from c. 1915 of art as construction and production, and its international heirs: Tatlin's Monument to the Third International, Rodchenko's Pure Colours, El Lissitzky's Proun.
leaves.see: T64 Suprematism;T66 De Stijl;T89 Concrete Art

leaves.label: De Stijl
leaves.defn: The Dutch movement (1917) of Neoplasticism, reducing art to primaries and the right angle: Mondrian's Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow, van Doesburg's Counter-Composition.

leaves.label: Dada
leaves.defn: The anti-art movement born in Zurich in 1916 and spread to Berlin, Paris and New York: Duchamp's Fountain, Höch's Cut with the Kitchen Knife, Arp's collages.

leaves.label: Surrealism
leaves.defn: The movement launched by Breton in 1924 that painted dream and the unconscious: Dalí's The Persistence of Memory, Magritte's The Treachery of Images, Ernst's Europe after the Rain.
leaves.see: T67 Dada;T69 Metaphysical Painting;T71 Magic Realism

leaves.label: Metaphysical Painting
leaves.defn: Giorgio de Chirico's and Carrà's painting of uncanny piazzas and mannequins, 1910–1920: The Disquieting Muses, Mystery and Melancholy of a Street.

leaves.label: New Objectivity
leaves.defn: The sober, sharp-focus realism of Weimar Germany in the 1920s: Dix's Portrait of Sylvia von Harden, Grosz's Pillars of Society, Schad's Self-Portrait with Model.

leaves.label: Magic Realism
leaves.defn: Realist painting of the 1920s–1950s that makes the everyday strange: Carel Willink's Wilma, Pyke Koch's Shooting Gallery, Ivan Albright's The Picture of Dorian Gray.

leaves.label: Precisionism
leaves.defn: American painting of the 1920s–1930s rendering industry and the city in crisp geometric planes: Sheeler's American Landscape, Demuth's My Egypt.

leaves.label: Regionalism
leaves.defn: American painting of the 1930s of the rural Midwest: Wood's American Gothic, Benton's America Today, Curry's Tragic Prelude.

leaves.label: Ashcan School
leaves.defn: New York realist painters of the early 20th century who depicted the city's streets and poor: Bellows's Stag at Sharkey's, Sloan's McSorley's Bar.

leaves.label: Social Realism
leaves.defn: Politically engaged realist painting of the 1920s–1940s on labour and poverty: Ben Shahn's The Passion of Sacco and Vanzetti, Isabel Bishop's working women.
leaves.see: T76 Socialist Realism;T73 Regionalism;T191 Mexican Muralism

leaves.label: Socialist Realism
leaves.defn: The official style of the Soviet Union from 1932 and of the socialist states: Gerasimov's Lenin on the Tribune, Deineka's Defence of Petrograd.

leaves.label: Harlem Renaissance
leaves.defn: The flowering of African-American art in the 1920s–1930s centred in Harlem: Aaron Douglas's Aspects of Negro Life, Archibald Motley's Nightlife, Augusta Savage's The Harp.

leaves.label: School of Paris
leaves.defn: The international, often émigré artists working in Paris c. 1900–1940 outside a single movement: Modigliani's Jeanne Hébuterne, Chagall's I and the Village, Soutine's Carcass of Beef.

leaves.label: Scuola Romana
leaves.defn: Roman painters of the 1920s–1930s around Scipione and Mafai, expressionist in colour against the classicising Novecento: Mafai's Demolitions, Scipione's Cardinal Decano.

leaves.label: Neo-Romanticism
leaves.defn: Figurative painting of the 1930s–1950s (Berman, Tchelitchew; the British Neo-Romantics) reviving Romantic landscape and mood: Paul Nash's Totes Meer, Sutherland's Entrance to a Lane.

leaves.label: Naïve Art
leaves.defn: Painting by artists without academic training, flat, detailed and frontal: Henri Rousseau's The Dream, Séraphine Louis's Tree of Paradise, Ivan Generalić's Hlebine paintings.
leaves.see: T82 Art Brut;A6 Folk & Popular Painting

leaves.label: Art Brut
leaves.defn: Dubuffet's "raw art" of outsiders, the untrained and the institutionalised, and its successor outsider art: Adolf Wölfli's illustrated books, Aloïse Corbaz's theatres.

leaves.label: Abstract Expressionism
leaves.defn: The New York painting of the 1940s–1950s, gestural or field-based: Pollock's Autumn Rhythm, de Kooning's Woman I, Kline's Chief.
leaves.see: T84 Color Field;Art Informel;T85 Lyrical Abstraction

leaves.label: Color Field
leaves.defn: Abstraction of large expanses of flat or stained colour from the late 1940s: Rothko's No. 61 (Rust and Blue), Frankenthaler's Mountains and Sea, Newman's Vir Heroicus Sublimis.

leaves.label: Lyrical Abstraction
leaves.defn: Post-war gestural abstraction in Paris (abstraction lyrique) and its American 1960s sense: Georges Mathieu's Capetians Everywhere, Zao Wou-Ki's large canvases.

leaves.label: Informalism
leaves.defn: European post-war abstraction of matter, sign and gesture (art informel, tachisme, matter painting): Fautrier's Hostages, Wols's It's All Over, Tàpies's matter paintings.

leaves.label: COBRA
leaves.defn: The Copenhagen–Brussels–Amsterdam movement (1948–1951) of spontaneous, childlike expressionist painting: Appel's Questioning Children, Jorn's Letter to My Son.

leaves.label: Hard-edge Painting
leaves.defn: Abstraction of crisp-edged flat colour areas from the late 1950s: Ellsworth Kelly's Red Blue Green, Karl Benjamin's compositions.
leaves.see: T84 Color Field;T89 Concrete Art;T90 Op Art

leaves.label: Concrete Art
leaves.defn: Geometric abstraction built from pure plastic means, after van Doesburg's 1930 manifesto, in Switzerland, Italy and Latin America: Max Bill's Endless Ribbon, Lygia Clark's Bichos, Tomás Maldonado's works.
leaves.see: T66 De Stijl;T65 Constructivism;T90 Op Art

leaves.label: Op Art
leaves.defn: Abstraction of the 1960s exploiting optical effects: Bridget Riley's Movement in Squares, Vasarely's Vega series.

leaves.label: Pop Art
leaves.defn: Art of the late 1950s–1960s drawn from mass media, advertising and consumer goods: Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans, Lichtenstein's Whaam!, Hamilton's Just What Is It ....

leaves.label: Neo-Dada
leaves.defn: American art of the late 1950s reviving Dada assemblage and found imagery: Rauschenberg's Monogram, Johns's Flag.

leaves.label: Nouveau Réalisme
leaves.defn: The French movement founded in 1960 around Restany, appropriating the real (décollage, accumulation, wrapping): Arman's Accumulations, Yves Klein's Anthropometries, Villeglé's torn posters.

leaves.label: Funk Art
leaves.defn: Irreverent figurative art of the San Francisco Bay Area in the 1960s, often in ceramics: Robert Arneson's self-portrait busts, Roy De Forest's paintings.
leaves.see: T91 Pop Art;T95 Bay Area Figurative Movement

leaves.label: Bay Area Figurative Movement
leaves.defn: San Francisco painters of the 1950s–1960s who returned from abstraction to the figure: Diebenkorn's Cityscape I, David Park's Four Men.

leaves.label: Northwest School
leaves.defn: Painters of the Pacific Northwest in the 1930s–1950s, mystical and Asian-influenced: Mark Tobey's white writing, Morris Graves's Blind Bird.

leaves.label: Pattern and Decoration
leaves.defn: The American movement of the mid-1970s that reclaimed ornament, textile and craft: Miriam Schapiro's femmages, Robert Kushner's costumes.

leaves.label: Photorealism
leaves.defn: Painting from the late 1960s that reproduces photographs with exacting fidelity: Richard Estes's storefronts, Chuck Close's Big Self-Portrait.

leaves.label: Neo-figurative
leaves.defn: The return to the figure in 1960s Latin America and Spain (Otra Figuración): Jorge de la Vega's works, Luis Felipe Noé's Introduction to Hope.

leaves.label: Neo-Expressionism
leaves.defn: Figurative, expressive painting of the late 1970s–1980s: Baselitz's upside-down figures, Kiefer's Margarethe, Basquiat's Untitled (Skull).

leaves.label: Lettrism
leaves.defn: Isidore Isou's movement (from 1945) of letters and signs as the material of poetry and painting: Isou's hypergraphic novels, Lemaître's works.

leaves.label: Black Arts Movement
leaves.defn: The African-American art movement of 1965–1975 tied to Black Power (AfriCOBRA, the Wall of Respect): Jeff Donaldson's Wives of Shango, Wadsworth Jarrell's Revolutionary.
leaves.see: T77 Harlem Renaissance;T103 British Black Arts Movement

leaves.label: British Black Arts Movement
leaves.defn: Black British artists of the 1980s (the BLK Art Group) addressing race and diaspora: Lubaina Himid's A Fashionable Marriage, Keith Piper's works.

leaves.label: Lowbrow
leaves.defn: Californian pop-surrealist painting from the late 1970s rooted in comics, hot-rod and tattoo culture: Robert Williams's paintings, Mark Ryden's The Meat Show.

leaves.label: Mission School
leaves.defn: San Francisco artists of the 1990s working from street, folk and graffiti culture: Barry McGee's installations, Margaret Kilgallen's murals.

leaves.label: Stuckism
leaves.defn: The figurative painting movement founded in London in 1999 against conceptual art: Charles Thomson's Sir Nicholas Serota Makes an Acquisitions Decision.

leaves.label: Superflat
leaves.defn: Takashi Murakami's Japanese postmodern movement (2000) of flat anime and print-derived imagery: Murakami's Tan Tan Bo, Aya Takano's paintings.

leaves.label: Hurufiyya Movement
leaves.defn: Modern art of the Arab world and Iran (from the 1950s) that uses Arabic letters as abstract form: Madiha Omar's works, Shakir Hassan Al Said's The Contemplative Dimension, Parviz Tanavoli's Heech.

leaves.label: Dakar School
leaves.defn: Senegalese painting of the 1960s–1970s fostered by Senghor's Négritude policy: Papa Ibra Tall's tapestries, Iba N'Diaye's works.

leaves.label: Yōga
leaves.defn: Japanese painting in Western oil technique from the Meiji period: Kuroda Seiki's Lakeside, Takahashi Yuichi's Salmon, Kishida Ryūsei's Reiko.

leaves.label: Bengal School of Art
leaves.defn: The Indian nationalist painting movement of Abanindranath Tagore and his pupils (c. 1900–1940) reviving Mughal and Ajanta idioms: Abanindranath Tagore's Bharat Mata, Nandalal Bose's Haripura posters.

leaves.label: Modern Art
leaves.defn: The period style of painters born c. 1860–1944 working outside a recorded movement, across the global lineages of easel painting: academic-trained modern portraitists, independent landscape painters, national modernisms.

leaves.label: Contemporary Art
leaves.defn: The period style of painters born from 1945, working after modernism in global, plural practices: post-colonial figurative painting, new abstraction.

leaves.label: Hispano-Flemish Style
leaves.defn: Fifteenth-century painting of Castile and Aragon shaped by Early Netherlandish oil technique and realism, under the patronage of Isabella I: Bartolomé Bermejo's Saint Michael Triumphant, Fernando Gallego's Pietà, Pedro Berruguete's altarpieces.
leaves.see: T21 Early Netherlandish Painting;T24 Northern Renaissance

leaves.label: Dansaekhwa
leaves.defn: The Korean monochrome painting movement of the 1970s: Park Seo-bo's Ecriture, Yun Hyong-keun's Umber-Blue, Chung Sang-hwa's grids, Ha Chong-hyun's Conjunction.
leaves.see: T193 Installation Art (Mono-ha kind);T84 Color Field

leaves.label: Madhubani Painting
leaves.defn: The Mithila painting of women of Bihar and Nepal's Terai, moved from house walls to paper from the 1960s, in bharni, kachni and godna styles: kohbar ghar marriage paintings, Baua Devi nagas.

leaves.label: Warli Painting
leaves.defn: White rice-paste painting of the Warli of Maharashtra, from marriage chauk on house walls to works on paper (Jivya Soma Mashe): Palaghata chauk, tarpa dance circles.

leaves.label: Gond Painting
leaves.defn: The painting of the Pardhan Gond of Madhya Pradesh in dot-and-dash infill on paper and canvas since Jangarh Singh Shyam (Jangarh kalam): trees of life, Bhajju Shyam animals.

leaves.label: Tanjore Painting
leaves.defn: Devotional painting of Thanjavur on wooden board with gesso relief, gold leaf and glass stones, 18th–19th century: Balakrishna, Rama pattabhishekam.

leaves.label: Mysore Painting
leaves.defn: Devotional painting of the Mysore court in gesso and gold leaf, finer and lighter than Tanjore work: Krishna and Rama icons, Sritattvanidhi illustrations.

leaves.label: Truck Art
leaves.defn: The painted, mirrored and calligraphic decoration of lorries in Pakistan and India, from Rawalpindi, Peshawar and Karachi workshops: jingle trucks, Horn OK Please tailboards.
leaves.aliases: jingle truck;Truck art in South Asia

leaves.label: Rickshaw Painting
leaves.defn: Hand-painted cycle-rickshaw panels and hoods of Dhaka (UNESCO 2023), with film stars, landscapes and animals: backboard paintings, applique hoods.

leaves.label: Letras y Figuras
leaves.defn: The 19th-century Philippine genre of watercolour letters composed of figures and scenes, with the costume pictures (tipos del país) of the same Manila painters: name monograms, Damián Domingo costume albums.

leaves.label: Ōtsu-e
leaves.defn: Folk paintings sold to travellers at Ōtsu on the Tōkaidō from the 17th century, brushed quickly with stencils and few colours: the Demon Chanting the Nembutsu, Wisteria Maiden, Fujimusume, Buddhist icons.

leaves.label: Ema
leaves.defn: Painted wooden votive plaques offered at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples, from small mass-made tablets to large framed ema halls painted by town and ukiyo-e painters: horse ema, Kitano Tenmangū votive tablets.

leaves.label: Minhwa
leaves.defn: Korean folk painting of the late Joseon period, anonymous decorative screens and scrolls for houses: chaekgeori book-and-scholar's-object screens, munjado ideograph paintings, magpie and tiger, sipjangsaeng ten longevity symbols.

leaves.label: Tingatinga Painting
leaves.defn: The Dar es Salaam school of enamel painting on board founded by Edward Said Tingatinga in 1968 and carried on by his followers and the Tingatinga Arts Cooperative: flat-coloured animals and birds, crowded village and spirit scenes.

leaves.label: Retablo
leaves.defn: Small devotional paintings of saints in oil on tin (lámina) made by popular painters in Mexico in the 19th century, with the related ex-voto paintings giving thanks for a miracle: Santo Niño de Atocha láminas, ex-votos of San Juan de los Lagos.

leaves.label: Amate Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in bright colours on amate bark paper by Nahua artists of the Alto Balsas in Guerrero since the 1960s, with Otomí paper cut-figures from San Pablito: village fiesta scenes, birds and flowers.

leaves.label: Tablas de Sarhua
leaves.defn: Painted boards of Sarhua (Ayacucho), originally genealogical beams given at house-raisings, later sold as narrative paintings of village life: house-beam tablas, Piraq Causa series.

leaves.label: Tigua Painting
leaves.defn: Painting on stretched sheepskin by Kichwa artists of Tigua in Ecuador's central highlands, begun by Julio Toaquiza in the 1970s, depicting fiestas and Andean landscapes: Corpus Christi dancers, Cotopaxi landscapes.
leaves.weak: weak attestation (collection record only); see problems

leaves.label: Fileteado
leaves.defn: The decorative painting of Buenos Aires carts, buses and shop signs with scrolls, flowers and lettering, inscribed by UNESCO in 2015: colectivo panels, filete signboards.

leaves.label: Bark Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in natural ochres on prepared stringybark sheets, the classic medium of Arnhem Land, with clan designs in fine cross-hatching (rarrk) in the east and figurative and x-ray figures in the west: Yolŋu miny'tji clan paintings, Kunwinjku x-ray figures, Groote Eylandt black-ground barks.

leaves.label: Theorem Painting
leaves.defn: American stencilled still lifes of fruit and flowers painted on velvet or paper with cut stencils (theorems), a schoolgirl and amateur art of c. 1810–1860: fruit baskets on velvet, bowls of flowers.
leaves.weak: Theorem painting redirects to Theorem stencil

leaves.label: Reverse Glass Painting
leaves.defn: Folk pictures painted in reverse on the back of a glass pane, made in glassworks districts of Austria, Bavaria and Bohemia from the 18th century and sold at fairs and shrines: Sandl devotional pictures with the Sandl rose, saints and Madonnas for the home altar.

leaves.label: Petrykivka Painting
leaves.defn: Ornamental painting of the village of Petrykivka (Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine) with flowers, berries and birds brushed with fingers, cat-hair brushes and reeds on house walls, paper sheets and wooden objects (UNESCO 2013): painted malyovky sheets, painted chests and plates.

leaves.label: Tauric Painting
leaves.defn: Traditional decorative painting of Mykolaiv Oblast in southern Ukraine, inscribed on the National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Ukraine.

leaves.label: Gorodets Painting
leaves.defn: Painting of the Gorodets district on the Volga from the mid-19th century, first on distaff bottoms and later on boards, boxes and furniture, with horsemen, ladies, birds and roses in a quick brush style on bright grounds: distaff bottoms (donce), painted panels.

leaves.label: Mezen Painting
leaves.defn: Red-and-black painting on distaffs, boxes and ladles from the lower Mezen River (Arkhangelsk region), with rows of horses, deer and birds in a graphic, archaic style: Palashchelye distaffs.

leaves.label: Northern Dvina Painting
leaves.defn: The painting of distaffs, chests and utensils in the villages along the Northern Dvina (Arkhangelsk region), in local styles with red floral grounds, birds, sirins and scenes of sleighing: Borok distaffs, Permogorye distaffs, Rakulka distaffs.

leaves.label: Ural-Siberian Painting
leaves.defn: Floral painting of the Old Believer and peasant households of the Urals and western Siberia (18th–19th century) on furniture, chests, walls and utensils, with large peonies and roses in a free brush.

leaves.label: Zhostovo Painting
leaves.defn: Oil painting of flower bouquets on black-lacquered iron trays made in Zhostovo near Moscow since the early 19th century, built up in layers and varnished: bouquet trays, gilded-rim trays.
leaves.see: Nizhny Tagil Tray Painting;I2 Russian lacquer miniatures

leaves.label: Nizhny Tagil Tray Painting
leaves.defn: Painted and lacquered iron trays made in Nizhny Tagil in the Urals from the 18th century, with flowers and genre scenes under a translucent varnish, the forerunner of Zhostovo.

leaves.label: Naïve Painting of Kovačica
leaves.defn: Naïve painting of the Slovak community of Kovačica in Vojvodina (Serbia) from the 1950s, in oil on canvas and on objects, with village life, harvests and weddings (UNESCO 2024).
leaves.aliases: Kovačica naive art;Slovak naive art painting

leaves.label: Pysanka
leaves.defn: Easter eggs decorated in the Slavic and East European wax-resist (batik) technique with layered dyes and symbolic patterns; regional schools and related types (krashanka, krapanka, drapanka) are kinds: Hutsul pysanky, Boyko pysanky.

leaves.label: Haitian Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Haiti since the founding of the Centre d'Art in Port-au-Prince (1944), from the self-taught masters around DeWitt Peters to the Vodou-inspired Saint-Soleil group (1972) and the Jacmel and Cap-Haïtien schools: Hyppolite's Ogoun Ferraille, Philomé Obin's Funeral of Charlemagne Péralte, Bigaud's Murder in the Jungle, Saint Fleurant's Mother with Children.
leaves.see: A5-79 Naïve Art;D5-75 Haitian Metal Art;H4-35 Drapo Vodou
leaves.weak: Wikipedia 'Haitian painting' redirects to Haitian art#Painting; 17 Haitian painters in artist_placements now in Modern Art or Naïve Art; Tropenmuseum and Smithsonian hold Haitian oils

fams.label: Drawings & Prints
fams.test: a drawing made as an end in itself or as a design, or an impression pulled from a matrix (woodblock, plate, stone, screen).
key: 1. Drawn by hand? → B1. 2. Printed from a matrix? → B2.

leaves.label: Saz Style
leaves.defn: the Ottoman court style of feathery serrated leaves, rosettes and fabulous creatures drawn in ink by the nakkaşhane under Shahkulu and Kara Memi (16th century), and carried from drawings into tiles, textiles and bindings.
leaves.see: E2-7 Iznik Pottery; H3-3 Ottoman Silk Textiles.

leaves.label: Ledger Art
leaves.defn: Plains narrative drawing in pencil, crayon and ink on the pages of account ledgers and on muslin, from the 1860s, continuing hide painting on paper: the Fort Marion drawings, Cheyenne and Kiowa warrior ledgers, Lakota ledger books.

leaves.label: American Comics
leaves.defn: Comic strips and comic books of the United States from the newspaper Sunday pages of the 1890s through the superhero comic book, underground comix and the graphic novel: Winsor McCay's Little Nemo in Slumberland, Herriman's Krazy Kat, Kirby and Lee's Fantastic Four, Spiegelman's Maus.
leaves.aliases: US comics;American comic books;American comic strips
leaves.see: B1-8 Manga;B1-6 Ligne Claire;B1-7 Marcinelle School;B1-4 Illustration
leaves.weak: listed after B1-8 Manga with the other comics leaves; 'American comics' is a short Wikipedia page ('Comics of the United States' redirects to American comic book); cartoonists of single-panel gag and editorial cartoons s

leaves.label: Old Master Drawing
leaves.defn: European drawing before c. 1800 as preparatory study and finished work, in metalpoint, chalk, pen and wash: Leonardo's Vitruvian Man, Dürer's Praying Hands, Rembrandt's landscape drawings.

leaves.label: Illustration
leaves.defn: Drawing made for books, periodicals, posters and caricature from the 18th century to the present: Gillray's caricatures, Tenniel's Alice illustrations, Saul Steinberg's New Yorker covers.

leaves.label: Golden Age of Illustration
leaves.defn: Book and magazine illustration c. 1880–1920, when colour printing made illustrators celebrities: Arthur Rackham's Peter Pan, Howard Pyle's pirates, Edmund Dulac's Arabian Nights.

leaves.label: Ligne Claire
leaves.defn: The clear-line drawing style of Hergé and the Brussels school of Franco-Belgian comics: The Adventures of Tintin, Blake and Mortimer.

leaves.label: Marcinelle School
leaves.defn: The dynamic, rounded Franco-Belgian comics style of Spirou magazine (Jijé, Franquin, Morris): Spirou et Fantasio, Lucky Luke, Gaston.

leaves.label: Manga
leaves.defn: Japanese comics and their drawn idiom from the 20th century: Tezuka's Astro Boy, Oda's One Piece, Takeuchi's Sailor Moon.

subs.label: Printmaking
subs.axis: Axis: school and tradition; the process (woodcut, etching, lithography, screen print) is a tag.

leaves.label: Đông Hồ Painting
leaves.defn: Woodblock prints of Đông Hồ village in Bắc Ninh on điệp (shell-coated) paper with natural colours, sold for Tết: Mouse Wedding, Jealousy, pig and piglets.

leaves.label: Hàng Trống Painting
leaves.defn: Hanoi's urban folk pictures, printed in outline from woodblocks and hand-coloured: Five Tigers, Carp Gazing at the Moon, Mother Goddess images.

leaves.label: Kim Hoàng Painting
leaves.defn: Woodblock prints of Kim Hoàng village west of Hanoi, printed on red or yellow paper: Tết pigs and roosters, calligraphic scrolls.

leaves.label: Nianhua
leaves.defn: Chinese New Year pictures: popular colour woodblock prints of door gods, auspicious children and opera scenes pasted up at the New Year, made in named print towns: Yangliuqing, Taohuawu, Yangjiabu, Zhuxianzhen.
leaves.aliases: New Year picture;Chinese New Year prints;nianhua woodblock prints

leaves.label: Cordel Literature
leaves.defn: The chapbooks of north-eastern Brazil sold hung on strings, whose covers are woodcuts (xilogravura) by popular printmakers: J. Borges woodcuts, cordel covers of Caruaru and Juazeiro.

leaves.label: Inuit Printmaking
leaves.defn: Stonecut, stencil and lithographic printmaking of Inuit community co-operatives in Canada since 1957, issued in annual collections: Kinngait (Cape Dorset) annual print collections, Baker Lake prints, Kenojuak Ashevak's The Enchanted Owl.

leaves.label: Torres Strait Islander Printmaking
leaves.defn: The linocut and etching movement of the Torres Strait (Zenadth Kes) from the 1990s, cutting island cosmology, totems and turtle-shell mask forms into large black-and-white prints: Badu and Moa linocuts, Mabuiag etchings.

leaves.label: Lubok
leaves.defn: Russian popular prints from the 17th to the early 20th century, first woodcuts then copper engravings and lithographs, hand-coloured and sold at fairs, with saints, folk tales, satire and the Mice Burying the Cat: The Mice Burying the Cat, Baba Yaga.

leaves.label: Poster Art
leaves.defn: The artistic lithographic poster from the colour posters of Jules Chéret in 1870s Paris through the Belle Époque, the Italian, Swiss and British schools and the psychedelic concert poster: Chéret's Bal du Moulin Rouge, Mucha's Gismonda, Toulouse-Lautrec's Divan Japonais, Cappiello's Le Thermogène.
leaves.see: B2-10 Plakatstil;B2-11 Soviet Poster;B2-12 Polish School of Posters;I3-11 Art Nouveau;I3-12 Art Deco
leaves.weak: 'Poster art' redirects to Poster and 'Affichiste' to Poster artist; Belle Époque poster is unattested as a title, so it is a kind group here, not a leaf

leaves.label: Plakatstil
leaves.defn: The German 'poster style' founded by Lucian Bernhard's Priester matches poster (1906): a single object, flat colour and a brand name: Bernhard's Priester and Stiller posters, Hohlwein's Riquet, Erdt's Opel, Klinger's Berlin posters.

leaves.label: Soviet Poster
leaves.defn: The political, film and propaganda poster of Soviet Russia and the USSR from 1917 to 1991, from the Civil War lithographs and ROSTA windows through Constructivist photomontage to the TASS windows and Socialist Realist posters: Moor's Have You Volunteered?, Lissitzky's Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge, Stenberg brothers' film posters, Toidze's The Motherland Calls.
leaves.aliases: Soviet poster art;Soviet propaganda poster;Russian avant-garde poster
leaves.see: B2-9 Poster Art;A5-63 Constructivism;A5-74 Socialist Realism
leaves.weak: no Wikipedia article 'Soviet poster' (Propaganda in the Soviet Union is not an art label); attested by The Museum of Russian Art exhibition 'Poster Art of the Soviet Era' and the NMAH TASS-window poster records; ROSTA wi

leaves.label: Polish School of Posters
leaves.defn: The Polish poster art of c. 1950–1990 for film, theatre and circus, painterly, metaphorical and hand-lettered, around Henryk Tomaszewski's Warsaw Academy studio: Tomaszewski's Moore, Lenica's Wozzeck, Cieślewicz's Vertigo, Świerzy's Jimi Hendrix.

leaves.label: Old Master Print
leaves.defn: Western printmaking before c. 1830 in woodcut, engraving, etching and mezzotint: Dürer's Melencolia I, Rembrandt's Hundred Guilder Print, Piranesi's Carceri.
leaves.see: T124 Etching Revival;T117 Old Master Drawing

leaves.label: Etching Revival
leaves.defn: The re-emergence of etching as an original art c. 1850–1930 in France, Britain and the United States: Whistler's Thames Set, Méryon's Eaux-fortes sur Paris, Seymour Haden's landscapes.

leaves.label: Modern Printmaking
leaves.defn: Printmaking by artists born c. 1880–1944: the expressionist woodcut, the artist's lithograph and the screenprint: Kollwitz's War cycle, Picasso's Vollard Suite.

leaves.label: Contemporary Printmaking
leaves.defn: Printmaking by artists born from 1945 across print and multiple practices.

leaves.label: Ukiyo-e
leaves.defn: Japanese woodblock prints and paintings of the floating world (17th–19th century): Hokusai's Great Wave, Hiroshige's Fifty-three Stations, Utamaro's beauties.

leaves.label: Shin-hanga
leaves.defn: The 20th-century Japanese revival of ukiyo-e production by publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō: Kawase Hasui's landscapes, Hashiguchi Goyō's beauties.

leaves.label: Sōsaku-hanga
leaves.defn: Japanese "creative prints" (from 1904) designed, carved and printed by the artist: Onchi Kōshirō's abstractions, Munakata Shikō's Buddhist prints.

fams.label: Book Arts & Calligraphy
fams.test: the written or decorated book or page is the work: calligraphy, illumination (ornament), binding and paper decoration, or a manuscript tradition studied as the book.
key: 1. Writing as an art, judged by its script? → C1 (placed by script family).
2. A manuscript tradition or its illumination (ornament, frontispieces, headings, borders)? → C2.
3. The binding? → C3. Decorated paper (marbling, paper cutting)? → C4.

subs.label: Calligraphy
subs.axis: Axis: script family and its lineage of masters.

leaves.label: Kufic
leaves.defn: the angular early Arabic script of Qur'ans on parchment and of inscriptions, with its later Eastern (broken cursive), floriated, plaited and square (banna'i) forms.

leaves.label: Maghribi Script
leaves.defn: the rounded scripts of al-Andalus, North Africa and West Africa (mabsut, mujawhar, Andalusi, Sudani), written with a pointed pen.

leaves.label: Six Pens (al-Aqlam al-Sitta)
leaves.defn: the proportioned cursive scripts — thuluth, naskh, muhaqqaq, rayhani, tawqi' and riqa' — codified by Ibn Muqla and Ibn al-Bawwab and perfected by Yaqut al-Musta'simi, then carried by his pupils and by the Ottoman masters (Sheikh Hamdullah, Hafiz Osman).
leaves.aliases: aqlam al-sitta; six scripts; Thuluth; Naskh; Muhaqqaq;Islamic calligraphy;Arabic calligraphy

leaves.label: Nasta'liq
leaves.defn: the hanging Persian script attributed to Mir 'Ali Tabrizi (14th century), the script of Persian poetry and album calligraphy (Sultan 'Ali Mashhadi, Mir 'Ali Haravi, Mir 'Imad), with its shikasta (broken) offshoot.
alias_rows: Dated 1494, copied by Salik b. Sa‘id, and dedicated to Sultan 'Ali Mirza
Copied by Salik b. Sa‘id, and dedicated to Sultan 'Ali Mirza, ca
Calligraphy attributed to Muhammad Husayn al-Kashmiri (“Zarin Qalam”)

leaves.label: Diwani
leaves.defn: the Ottoman chancery script of decrees and imperial documents, with the tughra, the sultan's calligraphic monogram.

leaves.label: Sini
leaves.defn: Chinese Arabic calligraphy, written with a brush in a rounded style on scrolls and Qur'ans of the Hui Muslims.

leaves.label: Mongolian Calligraphy
leaves.defn: Writing as an art in the vertical Classical Mongolian script, with its six basic strokes, on paper, silk and wood (UNESCO 2013): sutra manuscripts, calligraphic scrolls.

leaves.label: Georgian Calligraphy
leaves.defn: Writing of the Georgian scripts (asomtavruli, nuskhuri, mkhedruli) as an art, in manuscripts and inscriptions.

leaves.label: Chinese Calligraphy
leaves.defn: The art of writing Chinese characters with the brush, in seal, clerical, regular, running and cursive scripts: Wang Xizhi's Lantingji Xu, Huaisu's Autobiography, Mi Fu's Poems Written on a Boat on the Wu River.

leaves.label: Japanese Calligraphy
leaves.defn: Shodō: the Japanese art of the brush in kanji and kana, with its court lineages (Sesonji-ryū) and Zen bokuseki: Ono no Michikaze's works, Fujiwara no Yukinari's Hakubunshū.

leaves.label: Western Calligraphy
leaves.defn: The art of Latin-script writing, from Renaissance chancery hands and writing masters to modern lettering: Arrighi's La Operina, Palatino's writing book.

leaves.label: Type Design
leaves.defn: The design of typefaces and lettering for print and screen since the 19th century: Johnston's Underground typeface, Frutiger's Univers, Miedinger's Helvetica.

leaves.label: Early Qur'anic Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Qur'ans written on parchment in Hijazi and Kufic scripts from the 7th to the 10th century, in horizontal format with sparse illuminated headings (the Blue Qur'an, the Tübingen and Birmingham fragments).
leaves.aliases: early Qur'ans; Hijazi Qur'ans; Kufic Qur'ans

leaves.label: Islamic Illumination
leaves.defn: the illumination of Qur'ans and books after about 1000: gilded and painted frontispieces, sura headings, margins and borders, in the Abbasid, Mamluk, Ilkhanid, Timurid and Safavid (tazhib), Ottoman (tezhip) and Mughal traditions, with its named illuminators.

leaves.label: Timbuktu Manuscripts
leaves.defn: the manuscripts of the West African Islamic scholarly tradition (Timbuktu, Djenné, the Sahel), in Arabic and in Ajami (African languages in Arabic script), with their Sudani script and leather satchel bindings.

leaves.label: Malay Manuscripts
leaves.defn: illuminated Malay manuscripts in Jawi script from the Islamic sultanates of the Malay world (Aceh, Terengganu, Java), with their floral frontispieces.

leaves.label: Palm-Leaf Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Books of incised or inked palm leaves strung between wooden boards, the manuscript tradition of South Asia and Sri Lanka: Tamil and Grantha olas, Odia incised and painted pothis, Sinhalese Pali texts, Pala Buddhist Prajnaparamita.

leaves.label: Lontar
leaves.defn: Manuscripts on incised leaves of the lontar palm, blackened with soot, the book form of Bali, Lombok and older Java: Kakawin Sutasoma, Nagarakretagama, illustrated prasi leaves.

leaves.label: Folding-Book Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Concertina-folded books of mulberry or khoi paper, lacquered at the ends, in Burma, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia: parabaik, samut khoi, Lanna phap sa, kraing.
leaves.aliases: folding book manuscript;parabaik;samut khoi;samut thai;kraing;phap sa

leaves.label: Kammavaca
leaves.defn: Burmese ordination texts written in square tamarind-seed script in lacquer and gold on lacquered palm leaf, cloth or metal: gilt kammavaca leaves, painted covers.

leaves.label: Pustaha
leaves.defn: The divination and ritual books of the Batak datu, written on folded tree bark between carved wooden covers: Great Pustaha.

leaves.label: Dunhuang Manuscripts
leaves.defn: The manuscripts sealed in the Library Cave (Cave 17) of the Mogao Caves about 1000 and opened in 1900: Buddhist sutras, documents and the earliest dated printed book, the Diamond Sutra of 868, with illustrated sutra frontispieces.

leaves.label: Uigwe
leaves.defn: Illustrated royal protocol books of the Joseon court (1392–1910), recording ceremonies, weddings and funerals in text and painted processions: Hwaseong seongyeok uigwe, Banchado procession paintings.

leaves.label: Sutra Copying
leaves.defn: Buddhist sutras transcribed as acts of devotion and decorated with gold and silver on dyed paper, frontispiece paintings and ornamented rollers in Japan and Korea: the Heike Nōkyō, Lotus Sutra fan papers, Goryeo sagyeong in gold on indigo paper.

leaves.label: Dongba Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Ritual manuscripts of the Naxi Dongba priests of Lijiang in Yunnan, written in pictographic Dongba script and painted with deities, with painted ritual cards and scrolls.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Manuscripts
leaves.defn: The Ge'ez (and later Amharic) manuscript tradition of the Ethiopian and Eritrean church: parchment codices in wooden boards with blind-tooled leather, written in Ge'ez script with ornamental harag frames: gospel books, Psalters, Arganonä Maryam prayer books.
leaves.weak: pool QID Q16632158 not verified; Gondarine and early (to 1500) rows are period tags

leaves.label: Book of the Dead
leaves.defn: Illustrated Egyptian funerary papyri of spells for the afterlife, with painted vignettes, New Kingdom to Ptolemaic: Papyrus of Ani, Papyrus of Hunefer, Greenfield Papyrus.
leaves.aliases: Egyptian funerary papyri;Coming Forth by Day

leaves.label: Maya Codices
leaves.defn: The surviving bark-paper screenfold books of the Postclassic Maya, written in hieroglyphs with painted almanacs: Dresden Codex, Madrid Codex, Paris Codex, Maya Codex of Mexico.
leaves.see: A1-17 Borgia Group;L2-36 Maya Mural Painting

leaves.label: Late Antique Illumination
leaves.defn: Illustrated and decorated Latin books of late antiquity, 4th–7th century, in rustic capitals and uncial: Vergilius Vaticanus, St Augustine Gospels, Codex Argenteus.
leaves.weak: Wikidata 'art of Late Antique illumination'; no English Wikipedia article

leaves.label: Insular Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript art of Ireland and Britain, c. 600–900, joining Celtic, Germanic and Mediterranean ornament in carpet pages and great initials: Book of Durrow, Lindisfarne Gospels, Book of Kells, Book of Armagh.

leaves.label: Merovingian Illumination
leaves.defn: Book decoration of Frankish Gaul, 7th–8th century, with zoomorphic initials of fish and birds: Gellone Sacramentary, Gelasian Sacramentary.

leaves.label: Carolingian Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of the Frankish empire, c. 780–900, in its court and monastic schools: Godescalc Evangelistary, Coronation Gospels, Utrecht Psalter, Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram.

leaves.label: Ottonian Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of the Ottonian empire, c. 950–1050, at Reichenau, Trier, Echternach, Cologne and Regensburg: Gospels of Otto III, Pericopes of Henry II, Registrum Gregorii, Bamberg Apocalypse.
leaves.weak: Ottonian illumination redirects to Ottonian art#Manuscripts

leaves.label: Anglo-Saxon Illumination
leaves.defn: Late Anglo-Saxon manuscript art, 10th–11th century, in the acanthus-bordered Winchester style and in outline drawing: Benedictional of St Æthelwold, Harley Psalter, Ramsey Psalter.

leaves.label: Mozarabic Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of early medieval Christian Iberia, 10th–11th century, in flat banded colour, above all the illustrated commentaries of Beatus of Liébana: Morgan Beatus, Gerona Beatus, León Bible of 960.
leaves.aliases: Spanish illumination of the Early Middle Ages;Visigothic illumination
src: Wikidata Q18214676 (art of illumination in early medieval Spain)

leaves.label: Romanesque Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of Latin Europe c. 1050–1200, with large-format Bibles and monumental figure style: Bury Bible, Winchester Bible, St Albans Psalter, Hortus deliciarum.
leaves.see: T134 Gothic Book Illustration (artist);T157 Mosan Art (artist);L2-43

leaves.label: Renaissance Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript illumination of the 15th–16th century influenced by Renaissance painting, in Italy, France and the courts that collected it: Farnese Hours, Bible of Borso d'Este, Hours of Étienne Chevalier, Corvinian manuscripts.
leaves.see: T134 Gothic Book Illustration (artist);T135 Ghent-Bruges School (artist)

leaves.label: Hebrew Illuminated Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Decorated and illustrated Hebrew books of the Middle Ages and early modern period — Bibles, haggadot and mahzorim — with micrography and painted cycles: Sarajevo Haggadah, Golden Haggadah, Birds' Head Haggadah, Rothschild Miscellany.

leaves.label: Russian Illuminated Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Gospel books, chronicles and service books of Kievan Rus' and Muscovy, 11th–17th century, with Byzantine-derived miniatures and teratological headpieces and initials: Ostromir Gospels, Khitrovo Gospels, Radziwiłł Chronicle.

leaves.label: Fraktur
leaves.defn: Illuminated folk documents of the Pennsylvania Germans, 18th–19th century, lettered in a broken script and painted with birds, hearts and tulips: Taufschein (birth and baptismal certificates), Vorschrift (writing samples).

leaves.label: Gothic Book Illustration
leaves.defn: The illumination of Gothic manuscripts (13th–15th century), from Paris workshops to the Books of Hours: Jean Pucelle's Hours of Jeanne d'Évreux, the Douce Apocalypse, the Bedford Hours.

leaves.label: Ghent-Bruges School
leaves.defn: Flemish manuscript illumination c. 1475–1560 with illusionistic borders: the Grimani Breviary, Simon Bening's Da Costa Hours.
leaves.see: T134 Gothic Book Illustration;T21 Early Netherlandish Painting

leaves.label: Islamic Bookbinding
leaves.defn: the bindings of the Islamic book: tooled, stamped and filigree-cut leather with the envelope flap, and from the 15th century painted lacquer bindings.

leaves.label: Treasure Binding
leaves.defn: Medieval European book covers worked by goldsmiths in gold, silver-gilt, enamel, gems and carved ivory for Gospel books and altar books, c. 700–1200: Lindau Gospels upper cover, Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram, Ashburnham Pentateuch ivory covers, Gospels of Theodelinda.
leaves.aliases: jewelled binding;jeweled book cover;cover of a Gospel book
leaves.see: C3-3 Fine Binding;C3-1 Islamic Bookbinding;G1-43 Mosan Art;D2 Ivory & Bone Carving

leaves.label: Fine Binding
leaves.defn: Decorated leather bookbinding of Europe and America from the Gothic blind-stamped binding through Renaissance gold tooling to the designer bindings of the 20th century, named after binders, patrons and tooling styles: Grolier bindings, à la fanfare, Le Gascon pointillé, Derome dentelle, Cobden-Sanderson's Doves bindings, Legrain's Art Deco bindings.
leaves.aliases: European fine binding;fine bindings;decorated bookbinding;gold-tooled binding

leaves.label: Ebru
leaves.defn: paper marbling as practised in Ottoman Turkey and Iran: colours floated on size and transferred to paper, used for album margins and endpapers.

leaves.label: Sanjhi
leaves.defn: Paper-stencil cutting of the Braj temples of Mathura and Vrindavan, used to lay coloured powder images: Krishna lila stencils.

leaves.label: Chinese Paper Cutting
leaves.defn: Designs cut from red and coloured paper with scissors or knives for windows, doors and festivals across China (UNESCO 2009): window flowers (chuanghua), xi double-happiness cuts, embroidery patterns.

leaves.label: Papel Picado
leaves.defn: Mexican cut tissue paper banners chiselled through stacked sheets with designs for the Day of the Dead and fiestas.

leaves.label: Vytsinanka
leaves.defn: Belarusian folk paper cutting, symmetrical designs cut with scissors from folded paper for interiors and festivals (UNESCO 2024).

leaves.label: Slovenian Paper Flower Making
leaves.defn: The Slovenian craft of making crepe and tissue paper flowers for church feasts, processions and festive decoration.

fams.label: Sculpture & Carving
fams.test: carved, modelled or cast in three dimensions as an image or as carving for its own sake: statues, reliefs, carved stucco and stone ornament, ivory, bone, jade, rock crystal and hardstone, masks and puppets.
key: 1. Carved stucco, stone or terracotta ornament from buildings? → D1. 2. Ivory or bone? → D2. 3. Rock crystal, jade or other hardstone? → D3.
4. A mask or puppet made for performance? → D4. 5. Figurative sculpture in stone, wood, metal or clay? → D5.
6. An object of ritual or office (staff, reliquary, altar, regalia) that is not a mask or a figure? → D6.

leaves.label: Samarra Stucco
leaves.defn: the carved and moulded stucco of the Abbasid capital Samarra (9th century) in its three styles, of which the third, the bevelled style, carried abstract ornament across the early Islamic world.

leaves.label: Nasrid Stucco (Yesería)
leaves.defn: the carved and painted stucco of Nasrid Granada and the Mudéjar workshops (Alhambra wall panels, muqarnas).

leaves.label: Assyrian Palace Reliefs
leaves.defn: Carved gypsum orthostat reliefs from Neo-Assyrian palaces, 9th–7th century BC, with lamassu gateway figures: Ashurnasirpal II at Nimrud, Sennacherib's Lachish reliefs, Ashurbanipal's lion hunt.
leaves.weak: Assyrian palace reliefs redirects to Assyrian sculpture

leaves.label: Andalusian Ivories
leaves.defn: carved ivory boxes and pyxides of the Umayyad caliphal workshops of Córdoba and Madinat al-Zahra and of the taifa courts (10th–11th century).
src: Wikidata Q2864629 (art of the Umayyads of Cordoba)

leaves.label: Siculo-Arabic Ivories
leaves.defn: painted and gilded ivory caskets made in Norman Sicily and southern Italy (12th–13th century) in an Arabic decorative idiom.

leaves.label: Begram Ivories
leaves.defn: Carved ivory and bone plaques and furniture fittings of the 1st–2nd century found in the Kushan treasure at Begram (Kapisa) in Afghanistan, in an Indian idiom: river-goddess brackets, openwork throne-leg panels.

leaves.label: Netsuke
leaves.defn: Miniature toggles carved in ivory, wood and other materials to secure hanging containers to the kimono sash, Edo to Meiji period, with named carvers and regional schools: katabori figures, manjū netsuke, sashi netsuke.

leaves.label: Benin Ivories
leaves.defn: Ivory carved for the Oba of Benin by the Igbesanmwan guild and in neighbouring Owo, 15th–19th century: pendant masks of the Iyoba Idia, carved tusks for royal altars, double gongs and armlets.
src: Wikidata Q4888026 (art of the Kingdom of Benin)

leaves.label: Afro-Portuguese Ivories
leaves.defn: Ivories carved by Sapi (Sierra Leone), Edo (Benin) and Kongo carvers for Portuguese patrons in the 15th–16th century: salt cellars, side-blown oliphants, spoons and pyxes.

leaves.label: Nimrud Ivories
leaves.defn: Carved, gilded and inlaid ivory plaques and figures of the 9th–7th century BC found at the Assyrian capital Nimrud, made in Assyrian, Phoenician and North Syrian styles: Lioness attacking a Nubian, Woman at the Window, furniture plaques.

leaves.label: Byzantine Ivories
leaves.defn: Ivory carving of the Byzantine empire, 5th–12th century: consular diptychs, Barberini Ivory, Romanos group icons, Veroli Casket.

leaves.label: Alaska Native Ivory Carving
leaves.defn: Carving and engraving of walrus ivory and bone by the Iñupiat, Yupik and St Lawrence Island peoples of the Bering Strait, from ancient engraved hunting gear to figures, cribbage boards and engraved tusks for the curio trade.
leaves.aliases: walrus ivory carving;Bering Strait ivory carving;Eskimo ivory

leaves.label: Mississippian Shell Gorgets
leaves.defn: Engraved discs of marine-shell worn at the neck in the Mississippian Southeast (c. 1000–1600), cut with Southeastern Ceremonial Complex imagery: Spiro and Etowah gorgets, rattlesnake and cross-in-circle gorgets, mask gorgets.

leaves.label: Gothic Ivories
leaves.defn: Elephant-ivory carving of Gothic Europe, c. 1200–1530, led by Parisian workshops: devotional diptychs and polyptychs, statuettes of the Virgin, mirror cases and caskets with romance scenes.

leaves.label: Scrimshaw
leaves.defn: Engraving and carving on whale teeth, whalebone and walrus ivory by sailors of the whaling fleets, 18th–19th century: engraved sperm-whale teeth, busks, jagging wheels.

leaves.label: Duodji
