leaves.defn: The handicraft of the Sámi of Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Kola peninsula, divided into hard duodji (antler, bone and wood) and soft duodji (leather, textiles and pewter-thread embroidery): antler-handled knives, carved drinking cups (guksi), pewter-thread embroidered bags.

leaves.label: Uelen Bone Carving
leaves.defn: Engraving and carving of walrus ivory by Chukchi and Yupik carvers at Uelen in Chukotka, institutionalised as a workshop in 1931: engraved walrus tusks with hunting scenes, small figures of walrus and bears.

leaves.label: Tobolsk Bone Carving
leaves.defn: Bone and mammoth-ivory carving of Tobolsk in western Siberia from the 18th century, with small sculptures of northern life (reindeer sleds, hunters); a factory since 1929.

leaves.label: Yakut Bone Carving
leaves.defn: Mammoth-ivory carving of the Sakha (Yakutia), from 19th-century combs and caskets to Soviet-era sculptural compositions combined with silver and leather.

leaves.label: Fatimid Rock Crystal
leaves.defn: vessels and objects carved from rock crystal in Fatimid Egypt (10th–11th century), above all the ewers with relief decoration later mounted in European church treasuries.

leaves.label: Mughal Jade
leaves.defn: jade and hardstone vessels carved for the Timurid and Mughal courts, culminating in Shah Jahan's wine cup (1657).
src: Wikidata Q17053650 (Wine cup of Shah Jahan)

leaves.label: Chinese Jade
leaves.defn: Nephrite and later jadeite carved in China from the Neolithic to the Qing: ritual bi discs and cong tubes of Hongshan and Liangzhu, Shang and Zhou pendants and Han burial suits, Qing imperial boulders and vessels.

leaves.label: Chinese Snuff Bottles
leaves.defn: Small stoppered bottles made at the Qing court and in China's workshops (late 17th–20th century) in hardstone, glass, porcelain, enamel and lacquer, including inside-painted glass: Beijing palace glass bottles, carved agate, inside-painted bottles.

leaves.label: Cylinder Seals
leaves.defn: Engraved stone cylinders rolled on clay to leave a continuous image, the glyptic art of Mesopotamia, Iran, Syria and Anatolia from the Uruk period to the Achaemenids: Uruk and Jemdet Nasr seals, Akkadian contest scenes, Old Syrian and Mitanni seals, Neo-Assyrian ritual scenes.

leaves.label: Minoan Seals
leaves.defn: Engraved sealstones of hardstone, bone and gold made on Bronze Age Crete and adopted on the Mycenaean mainland, 3rd–2nd millennium BC: lentoid and amygdaloid seals, Pylos Combat Agate, gold signet rings.

leaves.label: Engraved Gems
leaves.defn: Intaglios and cameos cut in hardstone in the Greek, Etruscan and Roman world, 6th century BC – 4th century AD: Graeco-Persian gems, Etruscan scarabs, Roman Republican ringstones, Gemma Augustea.

leaves.label: Mesoamerican Jade
leaves.defn: Jadeite and greenstone carved by the peoples of Mesoamerica and Costa Rica from the Olmec to the Aztec, as masks, figures, celts, earspools and pendants: Olmec votive axes, Maya jade mosaic masks of Palenque and Calakmul, Costa Rican axe-god pendants.

leaves.label: Hei-tiki
leaves.defn: Māori ornaments carved from pounamu (New Zealand nephrite and bowenite) with stone tools, worn as heirlooms (taonga): hei-tiki human figure pendants, hei matau hook pendants, kuru ear pendants, mere pounamu clubs.

leaves.label: Pietra Dura
leaves.defn: Pictorial inlay of cut and fitted coloured hardstones (commesso), developed in the grand-ducal workshops of Florence from 1588 and practised in Rome, Milan, Prague and Paris: pietre dure table tops and cabinets, Cappella dei Principi panels, Badminton Cabinet.
leaves.see: I1 Carved & Inlaid Woodwork;E4-25 Mosaic & Tile Revetment

leaves.label: Karagöz Shadow Puppets
leaves.defn: the translucent painted leather puppets of the Ottoman shadow theatre of Karagöz and Hacivat.

leaves.label: Tholu Bommalata
leaves.defn: Shadow-puppet theatre of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka with large translucent painted-leather figures: Ramayana Ravana puppets, togalu gombeyata figures.

leaves.label: Wayang Kulit
leaves.defn: The flat, pierced and painted buffalo-hide shadow puppets of Java and Bali (UNESCO 2003/2008), cut by named craftsmen: Arjuna and Bima figures, gunungan, Semar and the punakawan.

leaves.label: Wayang Golek
leaves.defn: Carved and painted wooden rod puppets of Sunda and Java, with the flat wooden wayang klitik of East Java: Sundanese Ramayana and Mahabharata sets, Menak cycle puppets.

leaves.label: Topeng
leaves.defn: Carved and painted wooden masks of Javanese and Balinese masked dance-drama: Panji masks of Cirebon and Malang, Balinese topeng pajegan sets.

leaves.label: Nang Yai
leaves.defn: Large perforated hide panels of the Thai court shadow theatre, each a whole scene from the Ramakien, with the small jointed puppets of southern nang talung: Wat Khanon panels.

leaves.label: Sbek Thom
leaves.defn: Large cut-hide panels of the Khmer shadow theatre (UNESCO 2005) performed with the Reamker.

leaves.label: Yoke Thé
leaves.defn: The carved, painted and costumed string marionettes of the Burmese court theatre: zawgyi alchemist, nat and princess figures.

leaves.label: Chinese Shadow Puppetry
leaves.defn: Translucent puppets cut from leather or paper and painted, used in shadow theatre across China (UNESCO 2011), with regional styles: Shaanxi, Tangshan (Luanzhou), Sichuan puppets.

leaves.label: Bunraku
leaves.defn: The puppets of the Japanese ningyō jōruri theatre, carved and painted wooden heads (kashira) with mechanisms and costumed bodies worked by three puppeteers, and regional puppet troupes.

leaves.label: Korean Masks
leaves.defn: Carved wooden and gourd masks of Korean mask-dance drama (talchum) and village rites, by regional tradition: Hahoe and Byeongsan masks (National Treasure), Bongsan, Yangju, Ogwangdae masks.

leaves.label: Dogon Masks
leaves.defn: Masks of the Dogon Awa society danced at the dama funerary rites and the Sigi, carved in wood with rectangular faces and superstructures: kanaga, satimbe, sirige (storeyed house), imina na (great mask).

leaves.label: Chiwara
leaves.defn: Antelope crest headdresses of the Bamana Ciwara association, danced in pairs at planting and harvest, in vertical, horizontal and abstract regional styles: male and female pairs, vertical Bamako-region crests, horizontal Ségou crests.

leaves.label: Senufo Masks
leaves.defn: Masks and helmet masks of the Senufo Poro and Tyekpa societies of northern Côte d'Ivoire, Mali and Burkina Faso: kpeliye'e face masks, kponyugu fire-spitter helmet masks, wanyugo helmets.

leaves.label: Chokwe Masks
leaves.defn: Masks of the Chokwe of Angola, Zambia and the DR Congo danced at mukanda initiation and festivals: mwana pwo (young woman) masks, cihongo male masks, resin-and-barkcloth initiation masks.

leaves.label: Gelede
leaves.defn: Masks of the Yoruba (Ketu, Egbado, Anago) Gelede society, danced in pairs to honour the mothers: helmet masks with carved superstructures, Efe night masks.

leaves.label: Igbo Masks
leaves.defn: Masks and masquerades of the Igbo of south-eastern Nigeria, by village and society: agbogho mmuo maiden-spirit masks, Ijele towering masquerade, Afikpo okumkpa masks, Izzi elephant-spirit helmets.

leaves.label: Dan Masks
leaves.defn: Wooden face masks of the Dan (Gio, Yacouba) of Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire, with polished oval faces, slit or round eyes and named spirit roles: deangle masks, gunyege racing masks, ma go miniature masks.

leaves.label: Sowei Masks
leaves.defn: Black helmet masks of the women's Sande society of the Mende, Vai, Temne and Gola of Sierra Leone and Liberia, with neck rings and elaborate coiffures: ndoli jowei, sowo gande masterworks.

leaves.label: Kuba Masks
leaves.defn: The royal masks of the Kuba kingdom, danced as a trio of founding figures: mwaash aMbooy, ngady amwaash, bwoom.

leaves.label: Kifwebe
leaves.defn: Striated masks of the Songye and Luba bwadi bwa kifwebe society: male crested kifwebe, female white kifwebe.

leaves.label: Pende Masks
leaves.defn: Masks of the Central and Kwilu Pende of the DR Congo, danced at mbuya village masquerades and chiefs' rites, with their ivory miniatures: mbuya character masks, giwoyo and kipoko masks, ikhoko pendants.

leaves.label: Punu Masks
leaves.defn: The white-faced okuyi masks of the Punu and Lumbo of southern Gabon, danced on stilts: okuyi maiden masks.

leaves.label: Northwest Coast Masks
leaves.defn: Carved and painted wooden masks of the Northwest Coast peoples, danced at winter ceremonials and potlatches: Kwakwaka'wakw transformation masks, Hamat'sa bird masks, Nuu-chah-nulth and Heiltsuk masks, Tlingit shaman's masks.

leaves.label: Yup'ik Masks
leaves.defn: Shamanic dance masks of driftwood, feathers and paint carved by the Yup'ik and Cup'ik of south-western Alaska, made in pairs and destroyed after use, from finger masks to large hanging masks.

leaves.label: Torres Strait Turtle-Shell Masks
leaves.defn: Masks of the Torres Strait Islands built from heated and stitched turtle-shell plates, worn in initiation, funerary and increase ceremonies, with composite human-animal forms in the west and human faces in the east: krar (western islands), le op (Mer, Erub), crocodile-head masks.

leaves.label: Processional Giants
leaves.defn: Huge carried effigies of giants, animals and dragons, built of wicker, wood and papier-mâché and paraded at town festivals of the Low Countries, northern France and Iberia: gegants of Catalonia, giants of Flanders and Wallonia, Jas de Keistamper of Boxtel.

subs.label: Figurative Sculpture
subs.axis: Axis: period style, school or movement. Built at scale.

leaves.label: Gandharan Art
leaves.defn: Buddhist sculpture of Gandhara (Peshawar valley, Swat, Taxila), 1st century BCE–5th century CE, in schist and stucco with Hellenistic drapery: standing Buddhas, bodhisattva Maitreya, narrative stupa reliefs.

leaves.label: Art of Mathura
leaves.defn: The school of red-sandstone sculpture of Mathura (2nd century BCE–12th century), at its height under the Kushans and Guptas: Katra Buddha, yakshi railing pillars, Kanishka statue.

leaves.label: Amaravati Art
leaves.defn: The Andhra school of limestone relief sculpture of the Krishna valley under the Satavahanas and Ikshvakus: Amaravati stupa drum slabs, Nagarjunakonda friezes.
leaves.weak: evidence weak (Andhra Pradesh row, excluded Amaravati row)

leaves.label: Pala Art
leaves.defn: The stone and bronze Buddhist and Hindu sculpture of Bengal and Bihar under the Palas and Senas (8th–12th century), in black basalt and eight-metal alloy: Kurkihar bronzes, Nalanda bodhisattvas, Surya steles.

leaves.label: Chola Bronzes
leaves.defn: Lost-wax bronze images cast in the Chola kingdom of Tamil Nadu (c. 850–1280) for temple processions: Shiva Nataraja, Somaskanda, Parvati.

leaves.label: Dhokra
leaves.defn: Lost-wax brass casting of tribal smiths of central and eastern India (Bastar, Bengal, Odisha) with wax-thread surfaces: Bastar horse and elephant figures, measure bowls.

leaves.label: Bankura Horse
leaves.defn: Stylised terracotta votive horses of Panchmura in Bankura, West Bengal, offered at village shrines.

leaves.label: Molela Terracotta
leaves.defn: Hand-modelled terracotta votive plaques of Molela in Rajasthan, made for shrines of Dharmaraja and Devnarayan.

leaves.label: Nepalese Sculpture
leaves.defn: The metal, stone and wood sculpture of the Newars of the Kathmandu Valley from the Licchavi period on, above all gilt-copper images cast by lost wax and repoussé: standing Vajrapani (6th–7th c.), gilt-copper Taras, dancing Ganeshas.

leaves.label: Kashmiri Bronzes
leaves.defn: Buddhist and Hindu images cast in brass with silver and copper inlay in Kashmir (6th–12th century), largely preserved in Tibetan monasteries, the source of the Kashmiri (Kache) style of western Tibet: crowned Buddhas, Vajrasattva with silver-inlaid eyes.

leaves.label: Tibetan Buddhist Sculpture
leaves.defn: Images cast in gilt copper and brass, or modelled in clay and stucco, for Tibetan monasteries from the 11th century on, in Indian, Newar and Chinese-derived styles that fused into Tibetan workshops: Densatil stupa figures, portrait sculptures of lamas, Tsang gilt-copper images.

leaves.label: Zanabazar School
leaves.defn: The gilt-bronze sculpture of the first Jebtsundamba Khutukhtu Zanabazar (1635–1723) and his workshop at Tövkhön, in a Nepalese-derived style, and its Mongolian followers: White Tara, Vajradhara (1683), Five Dhyani Buddhas.

leaves.label: Sino-Tibetan Sculpture
leaves.defn: Tibetan Buddhist images made in Chinese imperial and northern workshops for Tibetan and Mongol patrons, from the Yuan atelier of Aniko through the Yongle and Xuande bronzes to Qing court and Dolonnor casting: Yongle-marked gilt bronzes, Kangxi gilt bronzes.

leaves.label: Khmer Sculpture
leaves.defn: The stone and bronze sculpture of Cambodia and the Khmer lands from the pre-Angkor kingdoms to the Bayon (6th–13th century), in its successive temple styles: Harihara of Prasat Andet, Angkor Wat apsaras, Jayavarman VII portrait heads, Prakhon Chai bronzes.

leaves.label: Dvaravati Art
leaves.defn: The Buddhist sculpture of the Mon kingdoms of central Thailand (6th–11th century), in stone, bronze, terracotta and stucco: standing Buddhas with double vitarka, Dharmachakra wheels, Ku Bua terracottas.

leaves.label: Cham Sculpture
leaves.defn: The sandstone and bronze sculpture of the Cham kingdoms of central Vietnam (7th–15th century): Mỹ Sơn E1 pedestal, Đồng Dương Buddha and dvarapalas, Tháp Mẫm guardians.

leaves.label: Majapahit Terracotta
leaves.defn: Earthenware figurines, heads, reliefs and models from Trowulan and other East Javanese sites of the Majapahit era (13th–15th century): portrait heads, piggy banks, house models.

leaves.label: Bulul
leaves.defn: Carved wooden granary guardian figures of the Ifugao of northern Luzon, seated or standing, made in pairs.

leaves.label: Philippine Santos
leaves.defn: Carved and polychromed wooden and ivory devotional images made in the Spanish Philippines from the late 16th century, many for export to Mexico and Spain: Santo Niño, Virgin of the Immaculate Conception, ivory Christ child.

leaves.label: Haniwa
leaves.defn: Unglazed terracotta cylinders and figures set on and around Kofun-period burial mounds in Japan (3rd–6th century): warriors in armour, horses, houses, dancing figures.

leaves.label: Mingqi
leaves.defn: Figures and models made to furnish Chinese tombs, from Han pottery houses and attendants to Tang lead-glazed camels, horses and tomb guardians: sancai camel with musicians, zhenmushou tomb guardians, Northern Wei soldiers.
leaves.aliases: Chinese tomb figures;tomb pottery;Tang dynasty tomb figures

leaves.label: Chinese Buddhist Sculpture
leaves.defn: Buddhist images in China in stone, bronze, wood and clay from the 4th century, in cave temples and for altars: Yungang and Longmen caves, Xiangtangshan reliefs, Liao painted wooden Guanyin, Dazu rock carvings.

leaves.label: Korean Buddhist Sculpture
leaves.defn: Buddhist images of the Three Kingdoms, Unified Silla, Goryeo and Joseon in gilt bronze, stone and wood: pensive bodhisattvas, Seokguram, the Seosan rock-carved triad.

leaves.label: Japanese Buddhist Sculpture
leaves.defn: Buddhist images of Japan in bronze, lacquer and wood from the Asuka period onward, made by workshop lineages of sculptors (busshi): Tori school Shaka triad, Tōdai-ji guardian kings, Kei school Kamakura figures.
leaves.weak: redirect from Japanese Buddhist sculpture; workshop lineages (Kei, In, En) are kinds for the artist pass

leaves.label: Japanese Dolls (Ningyō)
leaves.defn: Japanese dolls and folk toys of clay, wood, papier-mâché and fabric, made in named regional centres: Hakata and Fushimi clay dolls, Kyō-ningyō, hina dolls, inu-hariko papier-mâché dogs.

leaves.label: Kokeshi
leaves.defn: Lathe-turned and painted wooden dolls of the Tōhoku hot-spring towns (from the 19th century), in named lineages: Naruko, Tōgatta, Tsuchiyu kokeshi.

leaves.label: Huishan Clay Figurines
leaves.defn: Painted clay figurines from Huishan near Wuxi in Jiangsu (Ming to the present): A-fu plump children, opera figures (shouniezi).
alias_rows: Chinese clay figurines (Huishan, Clay Figure Zhang)

leaves.label: Clay Figure Zhang
leaves.defn: The painted clay figure sculpture of the Zhang family workshop of Tianjin, founded by Zhang Mingshan (1826–1906): genre figures and opera characters modelled with realism.

leaves.label: Tu'er Ye
leaves.defn: Clay figures of the Moon Rabbit dressed as a warrior or official, made in Beijing for the Mid-Autumn Festival since the Ming.

leaves.label: Nok Terracottas
leaves.defn: Terracotta sculpture of the Nok culture of central Nigeria (c. 900 BCE–300 CE), hollow-built figures and heads with triangular pierced eyes and elaborate coiffures; the related Sokoto and Katsina Ala styles are kinds: seated figures, heads, animal figures.

leaves.label: Ife Art
leaves.defn: The classical sculpture of Ile-Ife (c. 1000–1450) in copper alloy and terracotta: naturalistic heads and figures of rulers and court: Wunmonije heads, Obalufon mask, terracotta heads from shrine sites.

leaves.label: Benin Bronzes
leaves.defn: Cast brass of the Edo court of Benin, 13th–19th century, by the Igun Eronmwon guild: palace plaques, commemorative heads for royal altars, figures of the Iyoba and of Portuguese, altarpieces.
leaves.see: Benin Ivories;Ife Art;Lower Niger Bronze Industry

leaves.label: Lower Niger Bronze Industry
leaves.defn: Fagg's name for copper-alloy castings of the 14th–16th centuries from the lower Niger that fit neither Ife nor Benin, among them the Tsoede bronzes of Tada and Jebba: Tada seated figure, Jebba bowman, bells and plaques.
leaves.weak: Met uses the label as a culture name; no Wikipedia article found

leaves.label: Esie Soapstone Figures
leaves.defn: Over a thousand soapstone figures of seated men and women (c. 12th–15th century) found at Esie in Yoruba-speaking Kwara State, the largest corpus of stone sculpture in sub-Saharan Africa.

leaves.label: Djenné Terracottas
leaves.defn: Terracotta sculpture of the Inland Niger Delta (c. 1100–1600), from Djenné-Djeno and neighbouring sites: kneeling and seated figures, figures covered with pustules or snakes, equestrian figures; Bankoni is a related style.
leaves.aliases: Inland Niger Delta terracottas;Jenne terracottas;Middle Niger terracottas

leaves.label: Bura Terracottas
leaves.defn: Funerary terracottas of the Bura culture of Niger and Burkina Faso (c. 200–1100): cylindrical heads on jar burials, equestrian figures.

leaves.label: Koma Terracottas
leaves.defn: Terracotta figures and heads from burial mounds of Komaland in northern Ghana (c. 1100–1700), many heavily looted: stylised heads, equestrian figures.

leaves.label: Sao Terracottas
leaves.defn: Terracotta and copper-alloy sculpture of the Sao civilisation south of Lake Chad (c. 500–1600): human and animal heads, funerary jars.

leaves.label: Lydenburg Heads
leaves.defn: Seven hollow terracotta heads of the Early Iron Age (c. 500 CE) from Lydenburg in Mpumalanga, the earliest known sculpture of southern Africa.

leaves.label: Nomoli
leaves.defn: Small stone figures (soapstone, steatite) of the Sapi peoples of Sierra Leone and Guinea (c. 1400–1600), found in fields by later Mende and Kissi farmers: seated nomoli, larger pomdo heads.

leaves.label: Zimbabwe Birds
leaves.defn: The eight soapstone birds on columns from Great Zimbabwe (c. 13th–15th century).

leaves.label: Yoruba Sculpture
leaves.defn: Wood sculpture of the Yoruba of Nigeria and Benin, carved by named masters and workshops for shrines, palaces and divination: ere ibeji twin figures, Ifa divination trays and bowls, Ogboni edan brass pairs, veranda posts by Olowe of Ise.

leaves.label: Dogon Sculpture
leaves.defn: Wood sculpture of the Dogon of the Bandiagara escarpment, Mali, with the earlier Tellem figures: primordial couples, figures with raised arms, granary doors and locks, hogon cups.
leaves.weak: attest is a Met Dogon object page; Wikipedia 'Dogon art' redirects to African art

leaves.label: Bamana Sculpture
leaves.defn: Wood and iron sculpture of the Bamana (Bambara) of Mali, carved by numu blacksmiths: jonyeleni and gwan maternity figures, boli power objects, n'tomo and kore masks.

leaves.label: Senufo Sculpture
leaves.defn: Wood sculpture of the Senufo of Côte d'Ivoire, Mali and Burkina Faso by carver groups (kulebele, fonombele): pombia (child of Poro) figures, deble rhythm pounders, madeo divination figures, kalao hornbills.

leaves.label: Baule Sculpture
leaves.defn: Wood sculpture of the Baule of Côte d'Ivoire, polished and finely detailed: blolo bla and blolo bian spirit-spouse figures, asie usu nature-spirit figures, goli and mblo masks, heddle pulleys.

leaves.label: Lobi Sculpture
leaves.defn: Wood figures of the Lobi of Burkina Faso, Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire made for thil shrines: bateba figures in gesture, heads on posts.

leaves.label: Akan Sculpture
leaves.defn: Wood and terracotta sculpture of the Akan (Asante, Fante, Anyi) of Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire: akuaba fertility figures, mma terracotta memorial heads, linguist staff finials, stools.

leaves.label: Chokwe Sculpture
leaves.defn: Court sculpture of the Chokwe of Angola and the DR Congo, 19th century: Chibinda Ilunga hunter-hero figures, mwanangana chiefs' figures, royal chairs and stools.

leaves.label: Luba Sculpture
leaves.defn: Court sculpture of the Luba of the south-eastern DR Congo: caryatid stools, bowl bearers, headrests, lukasa memory boards, staffs of office.

leaves.label: Lega Sculpture
leaves.defn: Ivory, bone and wood figures and masks owned by grades of the Lega bwami association, eastern DR Congo: iginga figurines, lukwakongo masks.

leaves.label: Ndop
leaves.defn: Commemorative portrait figures of the Kuba kings (nyim), each carved with his emblem (ibol), 18th–19th century.

leaves.label: Makonde Sculpture
leaves.defn: Carving of the Makonde of Tanzania and Mozambique: lipiko helmet masks and figures, and from the 1950s the ebony sculpture of Dar es Salaam: mapiko masks, shetani figures, ujamaa trees of life.

leaves.label: Fantasy Coffins
leaves.defn: Figurative coffins carved by Ga carpenters in Teshie and Nungua near Accra since the 1950s, shaped after the deceased's trade or emblem: fish, cocoa-pod and car coffins.

leaves.label: Ancient Egyptian Sculpture
leaves.defn: Statuary and relief of pharaonic Egypt in stone, wood and metal, from the Old Kingdom to the Ptolemies: Menkaure triad, Middle Kingdom block statues and tomb models, Amarna reliefs, sunk temple relief.
leaves.weak: the title Ancient Egyptian sculpture exists only as a redirect; period rows (Old, Middle, New Kingdom, Late Period) are tags

leaves.label: Cycladic Figures
leaves.defn: Marble figures, mostly folded-arm female figures, made in the Cyclades in the Early Bronze Age, 3rd millennium BC: Spedos and Dokathismata types, harp player from Keros, marble vessels.

leaves.label: Ancient Greek Sculpture
leaves.defn: Stone and bronze sculpture of the Greek world from the Archaic to the Hellenistic period: kouroi and korai, Parthenon marbles, Riace bronzes, Pergamon Altar.

leaves.label: Greek Terracotta Figurines
leaves.defn: Mould-made and painted clay figurines of the Greek world, votive and decorative, Archaic to Hellenistic: Tanagra figurines, Tarentine votive figures, Myrina figurines, Boeotian figures.

leaves.label: Etruscan Sculpture
leaves.defn: Sculpture of Etruria in terracotta, bronze, stone and alabaster, 7th–1st century BC: Sarcophagus of the Spouses, Apollo of Veii, Chimera of Arezzo, Volterran cinerary urns.

leaves.label: Roman Portraiture
leaves.defn: Portrait sculpture of ancient Rome in marble and bronze, from veristic Republican heads to imperial portraits: Patrician Torlonia, Augustus of Prima Porta, Severan and Tetrarchic portraits.

leaves.label: Roman Sculpture
leaves.defn: Roman sculpture other than portraits: historical relief, ideal statuary and copies after Greek works, and carved sarcophagi: Ara Pacis, Trajan's Column, Ludovisi sarcophagus.

leaves.label: Olmec Sculpture
leaves.defn: The stone sculpture of the Olmec of the Gulf Coast, c. 1500–400 BCE, from monumental basalt carving to small greenstone figures and ceramic hollow babies: colossal heads of San Lorenzo and La Venta, La Venta Altar 4, Las Limas Monument 1.
leaves.see: D3-8 Mesoamerican Jade;D5-65 Classic Veracruz Sculpture

leaves.label: Maya Sculpture
leaves.defn: The carved stone and stucco sculpture of the Classic and Postclassic Maya: dated stelae, altars, lintels and panels with rulers and glyphic texts: Copán stelae, Yaxchilan Lintel 24, Piedras Negras Panel 3, Palenque stuccos.
leaves.see: E1-43 Maya Ceramics;D3-8 Mesoamerican Jade;L2-36 Maya Mural Painting

leaves.label: Aztec Sculpture
leaves.defn: The stone sculpture of the Mexica of Tenochtitlan, 14th–16th century, from colossal cult images and calendrical monuments to small household deities: Coatlicue statue, Sun Stone, Stone of Tizoc, Coyolxauhqui Stone.

leaves.label: Classic Veracruz Sculpture
leaves.defn: The sculpture of the Classic-period Gulf Coast (c. 100–1000 CE): carved stone ballgame yokes, hachas and palmas with scrollwork, and hollow ceramic figures: El Tajín ballcourt panels, Remojadas smiling figures, stone yokes.

leaves.label: West Mexican Shaft-Tomb Figures
leaves.defn: Hollow and solid ceramic figures and village tableaux placed in shaft tombs of Jalisco, Nayarit and Colima, c. 300 BCE–400 CE: Colima dogs, Nayarit house and ballgame models, Jalisco Ameca figures.
src: Wikidata Q2446653 (Western Mexico shaft tomb tradition)

leaves.label: Chavín Sculpture
leaves.defn: The carved granite of Chavín de Huántar and the Chavín horizon, c. 900–200 BCE, with fanged composite deities in contour-rivalry: Lanzón, Raimondi Stele, Tello Obelisk, tenon heads.

leaves.label: Valdivia Figurines
leaves.defn: Small fired-clay female figures of the Valdivia culture of coastal Ecuador (c. 3500–1500 BCE), among the earliest ceramics of the Americas: Venus of Valdivia.

leaves.label: Estofado
leaves.defn: Polychrome wooden sculpture of Spain and Spanish America in which gilded surfaces are painted and scratched to imitate brocade, the technique of viceregal image-makers (imagineros) of Mexico, Guatemala and Quito: Antigua Guatemala saints, Quito sculptural groups.
leaves.see: A5-11 Quito School;D5-70 Brazilian Baroque;D5-71 Santos

leaves.label: Brazilian Baroque
leaves.defn: The sculpture and church decoration of colonial Brazil, 17th–early 19th century, culminating in the Rococo of Minas Gerais: Aleijadinho's soapstone prophets at Congonhas, Mestre Ataíde's ceilings, Bahia gilded talha.

leaves.label: Santos
leaves.defn: Carved and painted devotional images of saints made by santeros in the Hispanic Caribbean and New Mexico: bultos in the round and painted retablo panels: New Mexican bultos, Puerto Rican santos de palo, Three Kings figures.
leaves.see: A6-13 Retablo;D5-69 Estofado;southeast_asia D5-68 Philippine Santos

leaves.label: Alebrije
leaves.defn: Brightly painted fantastic creatures, first made in papier-mâché by Pedro Linares in Mexico City and from the 1980s carved in copal wood by Zapotec carvers of Oaxaca: Arrazola carvings, San Martín Tilcajete tonas.

leaves.label: Cartonería
leaves.defn: Mexican papier-mâché sculpture for festivals: Judas figures burned on Holy Saturday, skeletons for the Day of the Dead and mojigangas: Judas figures, Linares calaveras.

leaves.label: Caruaru Clay Figures
leaves.defn: Small painted clay figures of north-eastern rural life made at Alto do Moura, Caruaru (Pernambuco), after Mestre Vitalino: bands of zabumba players, retirantes, cangaceiros.

leaves.label: Haitian Metal Art
leaves.defn: Sculpture cut and hammered from flattened oil drums by the smiths of Croix-des-Bouquets after Georges Liautaud: vodou lwa figures, trees of life, mermaids.

leaves.label: Totem Poles
leaves.defn: Monumental carved cedar poles of the Northwest Coast in formline style — memorial, mortuary, house-frontal and welcome poles carrying crests: Haida poles of SGang Gwaay, Tlingit and Tsimshian crest poles, Kwakwaka'wakw poles.
leaves.see: D4-24 Northwest Coast Masks;I1-14 Bentwood Boxes

leaves.label: Inuit Sculpture
leaves.defn: Figurative carving of the Canadian and Greenlandic Inuit in soapstone, serpentine, ivory and bone, above all the stone sculpture made for sale through co-operatives since the late 1940s.
leaves.see: B2-6 Inuit Printmaking;D2-9 Alaska Native Ivory Carving

leaves.label: Kachina Dolls
leaves.defn: Carved and painted cottonwood-root figures of the katsinam given to Hopi (and Zuni) children at ceremonies, from flat cradle dolls to the action figures of the 20th-century market.

leaves.label: Zuni Fetishes
leaves.defn: Small carved stone, shell and antler animal figures of Zuni Pueblo, made for ritual and since the 20th century for collectors, often with inlaid eyes and bundled offerings.

leaves.label: Storyteller Figures
leaves.defn: Painted clay figures of a seated storyteller covered with listening children, created by Helen Cordero at Cochiti Pueblo in 1964 and taken up across the Rio Grande pueblos.

leaves.label: Whakairo
leaves.defn: Māori wood carving: the carved figures, panels, gateways and canoe prows of meeting houses (wharenui), storehouses and canoes, cut in regional and tribal schools with manaia, spiral and figure motifs: poupou wall panels, pātaka storehouse carvings, tauihu canoe prows, waka huia treasure boxes.

leaves.label: Malagan
leaves.defn: The carved and painted funerary sculpture of northern New Ireland, made for malagan memorial ceremonies and discarded after display: openwork friezes, figures and masks of softwood with opercula eyes: vavara friezes, totok poles, tatanua masks.

leaves.label: Uli
leaves.defn: The massive hermaphroditic ancestor figures of central New Ireland (Mandak and Barak), displayed in the long ceremonies of skull reburial: uli figures with raised arms and crested headdresses.

leaves.label: Asmat Woodcarving
leaves.defn: The wood carving of the Asmat of south-west New Guinea (Papua, Indonesia), carvers (wowipits) working in the tradition of the culture hero Fumeripits: bisj ancestor poles, carved shields, canoe prows, ancestor figures.

leaves.label: Sepik Carving
leaves.defn: The figure sculpture, masks and ceremonial-house carving of the peoples of the Sepik River basin of Papua New Guinea: Iatmul orator's stools and ancestor figures, Sawos malu boards, Abelam yam masks and ancestor figures.

leaves.label: Massim Carving
leaves.defn: The curvilinear carving of the Massim region (Milne Bay, PNG), above all the Trobriand Islands, in hardwood incised and filled with lime: tabuya and lagim canoe prow boards for kula voyages, lime spatulas, dance shields.

leaves.label: Nguzu Nguzu
leaves.defn: The blackened wood canoe-prow figureheads of New Georgia in the western Solomon Islands, inlaid with nautilus shell, the emblem of the Solomon Islands shell-inlay tradition: nguzu nguzu figureheads, shell-inlaid bowls.

leaves.label: Marquesan Carving
leaves.defn: The carving of the Marquesas Islands (Te Henua ʻEnana) in wood, bone and stone, dense with the eye-and-face (mata) motifs shared with Marquesan tattoo: uʻu clubs, tiki figures, carved bowls and fan handles, bone ear ornaments (taiana).

leaves.label: Moai Kavakava
leaves.defn: The small wooden figures of Rapa Nui (Easter Island) carved in toromiro, emaciated male ancestor images worn at feasts, with their companion carvings: moai kavakava, moai paepae, rei miro pectorals.

leaves.label: Aurukun Sculpture
leaves.defn: The ochre-painted softwood sculpture of the Wik and Kugu peoples of Aurukun on Cape York, made for ceremony and since the 1990s through the art centre: Ku' (camp dog) figures, ancestral beings.

leaves.label: Neapolitan Nativity Scene
leaves.defn: Elaborate crèches of 18th-century Naples, with articulated figures of terracotta heads on tow bodies, dressed in silk, set among angels, Magi's retinues and street life: Met Neapolitan Baroque Crèche, Presepe Cuciniello.

leaves.label: Wildfowl Decoys
leaves.defn: Carved and painted wooden decoys of ducks, geese and shorebirds made by North American hunters and carvers, 19th–20th century, collected as folk sculpture: Shang Wheeler's black duck, Elmer Crowell's shorebirds.

leaves.label: Weathervanes
leaves.defn: American weathervanes of carved wood and moulded sheet copper, 18th–19th century, and the related whirligigs, collected as folk sculpture: Ames and Dexter heart-and-hand vane, J. W. Fiske and Cushing copper horses.

leaves.label: Estremoz Clay Figures
leaves.defn: Small modelled and painted clay figures of Estremoz in the Alentejo, made since the 17th century, first for nativity scenes and then of saints and rural types in regional dress: presépios, Primavera, Amor é cego.
leaves.aliases: Bonecos de Estremoz;figurado de barro de Estremoz

leaves.label: Matryoshka Doll
leaves.defn: Russian nesting dolls of turned and painted lime wood, first made at the Abramtsevo circle in 1890 (Malyutin, Zvyozdochkin) and then in Sergiev Posad, Semyonov and Polkhovsky Maidan.

leaves.label: Polkhovsky Maidan
leaves.defn: Turned and brightly painted wooden toys and matryoshkas of Polkhovsky Maidan (Nizhny Novgorod region), with large aniline-coloured flowers over ink outlines.

leaves.label: Bogorodskoye Carving
leaves.defn: Carved lime-wood toys and figures of the village of Bogorodskoye near Sergiev Posad, often with moving parts: the Blacksmiths (bear and peasant), pecking hens.

leaves.label: Dymkovo Toys
leaves.defn: Moulded, whitewashed and brightly painted clay figures of the Dymkovo settlement near Vyatka (Kirov): ladies in crinolines, turkeys, water-carriers.

leaves.label: Filimonovo Toys
leaves.defn: Clay whistles and figures of Filimonovo (Tula region) with elongated bodies painted in stripes of red, green and yellow.

leaves.label: Kargopol Toys
leaves.defn: Clay figures of the Kargopol district (Arkhangelsk region), squat and painted in earth colours: Polkan, bereginya, peasant figures (Babkin family).

leaves.label: Abashevo Toys
leaves.defn: Clay whistles of Abashevo (Penza region) shaped as goats, deer and rams with long necks and horns, glazed or painted.

leaves.label: Yavoriv Toy
leaves.defn: Turned and painted wooden toys of Yavoriv in Lviv Oblast (Ukraine): carts, horses and rattles painted in red, green and black.

leaves.label: Valky Whistle Toy
leaves.defn: Small ceramic whistle toys of the town of Valky (Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine).

leaves.label: Wooden Toys of Hrvatsko Zagorje
leaves.defn: Hand-carved and painted willow and lime-wood toys of Hrvatsko Zagorje (Croatia), sold at pilgrimage fairs (UNESCO 2009).

leaves.label: Pauper Statues
leaves.defn: Carved and painted wooden figures of beggars holding alms boxes placed outside Lutheran churches in Finland and Sweden, 18th–19th century.

leaves.label: Moai
leaves.defn: The monolithic statues of Rapa Nui (Easter Island), c. 1250–1500, carved from Rano Raraku tuff and set on ceremonial ahu platforms with red scoria pukao topknots and coral eyes: Ahu Tongariki moai, Hoa Hakananai'a (British Museum), Paro, unfinished moai of Rano Raraku.
leaves.aliases: moai statues;Easter Island heads;Rapa Nui stone statues

leaves.label: Archaic Greek Sculpture
leaves.defn: Greek sculpture c. 650–480 BC: kouroi, korai and temple pediments: the New York Kouros, the Peplos Kore, the Aegina pediments.

leaves.label: Classical Greek Sculpture
leaves.defn: Greek sculpture c. 480–323 BC from the Severe Style to Praxiteles and Lysippos: the Riace bronzes, the Parthenon marbles, Polykleitos's Doryphoros.
leaves.see: T136 Archaic Greek Sculpture;T138 Hellenistic Sculpture

leaves.label: Hellenistic Sculpture
leaves.defn: Greek sculpture 323–31 BC, theatrical and realistic: the Pergamon Altar, the Winged Victory of Samothrace, the Laocoön.
leaves.see: T137 Classical Greek Sculpture;T139 Roman Sculpture

leaves.label: Romanesque Sculpture
leaves.defn: Carved portals, capitals and church furnishings of the 11th–12th centuries: Gislebertus's Last Judgement at Autun, Wiligelmo's Modena reliefs, the Pórtico de la Gloria.

leaves.label: Gothic Sculpture
leaves.defn: Sculpture of the Gothic cathedrals and their workshops (c. 1140–1500): the Chartres Royal Portal, the Naumburg donor figures, Giovanni Pisano's pulpits.

leaves.label: Renaissance Sculpture
leaves.defn: European sculpture c. 1400–1560 reviving antique form: Donatello's David, Ghiberti's Gates of Paradise, Michelangelo's David.

leaves.label: Baroque Sculpture
leaves.defn: Sculpture of the 17th and early 18th centuries, dynamic and theatrical: Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa, the Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi, Gregorio Fernández's pasos.

leaves.label: Neoclassical Sculpture
leaves.defn: Sculpture c. 1750–1840 on antique models in white marble: Canova's Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss, Thorvaldsen's Jason, Houdon's Voltaire.

leaves.label: Academic Sculpture
leaves.defn: Salon and public-monument sculpture of the 19th-century academies, Romantic to Beaux-Arts: Rude's La Marseillaise, Carpeaux's The Dance, Bartholdi's Statue of Liberty.
leaves.see: T144 Neoclassical Sculpture;T148 Modern Sculpture;T146 New Sculpture

leaves.label: New Sculpture
leaves.defn: The British movement (1880s–1910s) of naturalistic, symbolist bronze sculpture: Leighton's Athlete Wrestling with a Python, Gilbert's Eros.

leaves.label: Animalier School
leaves.defn: 19th-century French sculpture of animals in small bronzes: Barye's Lion Crushing a Serpent, Mêne's hunting groups.

leaves.label: Modern Sculpture
leaves.defn: Sculpture by artists born c. 1850–1944, from Rodin to abstraction, assemblage and constructed sculpture: Rodin's The Thinker, Brâncuși's Bird in Space, Hepworth's Single Form.

leaves.label: Contemporary Sculpture
leaves.defn: Sculpture by artists born from 1945, object, figure and installation-based.

leaves.label: Kinetic Art
leaves.defn: Sculpture that moves or appears to move, from Calder's mobiles to the ZERO group: Calder's Lobster Trap and Fish Tail, Tinguely's Homage to New York.

leaves.label: Minimalism
leaves.defn: American sculpture of the 1960s of industrial, serial, geometric units: Judd's Untitled stacks, Carl Andre's Equivalent VIII, Dan Flavin's fluorescent works.

leaves.label: Postminimalism
leaves.defn: Sculpture after Minimalism (late 1960s) of process, materials and the body: Eva Hesse's Contingent, Serra's Splash Piece.

leaves.label: Kei School
leaves.defn: The Japanese Buddhist sculptors' lineage of Unkei and Kaikei (Kamakura period), realistic in joined-wood technique: the Tōdai-ji Niō, Unkei's Muchaku.

subs.label: Ritual Objects & Regalia
subs.axis: Axis: tradition. Carved or assembled objects made for ritual, office and power that are neither masks nor figures (staffs, reliquaries, altars, ceremonial weapons of office).

leaves.label: Kaavad
leaves.defn: Portable painted wooden shrines of Bassi in Rajasthan whose hinged panels are opened by kaavadiya storytellers: Ram and Krishna kaavads.

leaves.label: Minkisi
leaves.defn: Power objects of the Kongo peoples, figures and containers charged with medicines by a nganga; Songye and Teke power figures are kinds: nkondi nail figures, nkisi in animal form, Songye mankishi.

leaves.label: Fang Reliquary Guardians
leaves.defn: Wooden figures and heads set on bark boxes of ancestral relics by the Fang of Gabon, Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea: eyema byeri figures, byeri heads.

leaves.label: Asen
leaves.defn: Iron and brass memorial altars of the Fon of Benin (Abomey, Ouidah): a staff topped by a cone with cut-out figures and emblems commemorating the dead.

leaves.label: Taíno Zemís
leaves.defn: Sculptural objects of the Taíno of the Greater Antilles that housed deities and ancestral spirits, in stone, wood, shell and cotton, with the ritual seats and cohoba stands of the same cult: three-pointer stones, Vere zemís of Jamaica, duhos.

leaves.label: Peruvian Retablo
leaves.defn: Portable box altars of Ayacucho (Huamanga) filled with painted plaster and potato-paste figures, from the cajón de San Marcos to scenes of village life: cajón de San Marcos, Joaquín López Antay retablos.
alias_rows: Ayacucho retablos and Huamanga alabaster (piedra de Huamanga)

leaves.label: Ceremonial Pipes
leaves.defn: Carved stone pipes of Native North America made for ceremony and diplomacy: Hopewell platform pipes, Adena tubular pipes, Mississippian figural pipes, Iroquoian effigy pipes, catlinite (pipestone) pipes of the Plains.

leaves.label: Pukumani Poles
leaves.defn: The carved and ochre-painted ironwood grave posts (tutini) of the Tiwi Islands, erected round the grave at the Pukumani mourning ceremony and crowned with painted bark baskets: tutini, tunga bark baskets, carved figures.

leaves.label: Toas
leaves.defn: Small painted direction-markers of gypsum, wood and found materials made by the Diyari and neighbouring peoples of the Lake Eyre basin about 1904, left to show where a group had gone.

leaves.label: Khachkar
leaves.defn: Armenian carved memorial stones bearing a cross over a rosette or sun disc, surrounded by lace-like interlace, from the 9th century (Noratus, Julfa): Amenaprkich khachkar.

leaves.label: Lithuanian Cross Crafting
leaves.defn: Lithuanian making of wooden crosses, roofed poles and shrines with carved figures of saints (rūpintojėlis), set at roadsides and farms (UNESCO 2008).

fams.label: Ceramics
fams.test: made of fired clay: pottery, tiles and ceramic objects, placed by their body (fabric) and then their named ware.
key: 1. Earthenware body (porous, fired low), whether unglazed, slip-decorated, lead-glazed, tin-glazed or lustred? → E1.
2. Fritware (stonepaste: ground quartz, glass frit and a little clay)? → E2.
3. Stoneware? → E3. 4. Porcelain? → E4.
Then the named ware; lustre and tin-glaze are techniques inside a body, not sub-families (P4).

subs.label: Earthenware
subs.axis: Axis: named ware (decoration technique and centre).

leaves.label: Abbasid Tin-Glazed Ware
leaves.defn: earthenware with an opaque white tin glaze made in Basra and southern Iraq from the 9th century in imitation of Chinese porcelain, painted in cobalt blue and green (Abbasid blue-and-white).
leaves.aliases: opaque white ware; Basra ware; Abbasid blue-and-white

leaves.label: Abbasid Lustreware
leaves.defn: the first lustre pottery: tin-glazed earthenware painted in metallic lustre in 9th–10th-century Iraq, polychrome then monochrome, exported as far as Samarra and Kairouan.
leaves.see: E1-3 Fatimid Lustreware; E2-2 Kashan Lustreware.

leaves.label: Fatimid Lustreware
leaves.defn: lustre-painted earthenware of Fatimid Egypt (10th–12th century), often figural, signed by potters such as Muslim ibn al-Dahhan and Sa'd.

leaves.label: Samanid Slipware
leaves.defn: earthenware of Nishapur and Samarqand (9th–10th century) painted in coloured slips under a clear glaze, above all the epigraphic ware with Arabic aphorisms on a white ground.
leaves.aliases: Nishapur ware; epigraphic slipware; Samanid epigraphic ware

leaves.label: Splashware
leaves.defn: earthenware splashed with green, yellow and brown glazes in imitation of Chinese sancai, made in Iraq and Iran from the 9th century.

leaves.label: Persian Sgraffito Ware
leaves.defn: slip-covered earthenware incised through the slip and glazed, made in Iran and the Caucasus from the 10th to the 13th century (Garrus, Aghkand and Amol wares).
leaves.aliases: Garrus ware; Aghkand ware; Amol ware; sgraffito

leaves.label: Islamic Unglazed Pottery
leaves.defn: unglazed earthenware with carved, moulded, stamped or barbotine decoration, above all the pierced filters of water jugs (Egypt, Syria, Iraq, 10th–14th century).

leaves.label: Hispano-Moresque Ware
leaves.defn: tin-glazed and lustred earthenware of Islamic and Christian Spain (Málaga, Manises, Paterna, Valencia), 13th–16th century, carried to Italy as the model of maiolica.
leaves.aliases: Valencian lustreware; Manises ware; Málaga ware

leaves.label: Çanakkale Pottery
leaves.defn: the boldly modelled and splash-painted earthenware of Çanakkale on the Dardanelles (17th–19th century).

leaves.label: Fez Pottery
leaves.defn: the urban and rural earthenware of Morocco: the blue-and-polychrome tin-glazed wares of Fez, the pottery of Safi and the green glazed ware of Tamegroute.
leaves.aliases: Fassi pottery; Moroccan pottery; Safi pottery; Tamegroute pottery
leaves.weak: no English source names 'Moroccan pottery' as one tradition; 'poterie de Fès / de Safi' in French sources

leaves.label: Kabyle Pottery
leaves.defn: hand-built earthenware painted in red and black slips by Kabyle women potters of northern Algeria.

leaves.label: Sejnane Pottery
leaves.defn: hand-modelled earthenware of the women of Sejnane in northern Tunisia, inscribed by UNESCO in 2018.
leaves.aliases: pottery skills of the women of Sejnane

leaves.label: Rishton Ceramics
leaves.defn: the blue-glazed (ishkor) earthenware of Rishtan and the centres of the Fergana Valley and Bukhara oasis (Gijduvan) in Uzbekistan.

leaves.label: Ban Chiang Pottery
leaves.defn: Burial earthenware of the Ban Chiang culture of north-east Thailand, its late phase (c. 300 BCE–200 CE) painted with red swirls on buff: carinated jars with spirals, pedestal bowls.

leaves.label: Cham Pottery
leaves.defn: Hand-built, open-fired earthenware made by Cham women of Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2022): water jars, cooking pots.
leaves.aliases: Art of pottery-making of Chăm people;Bàu Trúc pottery

leaves.label: Kasongan Pottery
leaves.defn: Earthenware of Kasongan village near Yogyakarta, from votive animals to large decorated jars.

leaves.label: Yangshao Painted Pottery
leaves.defn: Hand-built red earthenware painted in black and red of the Neolithic Yellow River cultures (c. 5000–2000 BCE): Banpo fish-and-face basins, Miaodigou bowls, Majiayao and Banshan spiral jars of Gansu.
leaves.aliases: Neolithic Chinese painted pottery;Majiayao pottery;Gansu painted pottery

leaves.label: Jōmon Pottery
leaves.defn: Cord-marked earthenware of the Jōmon hunter-gatherers of Japan (c. 14,000–300 BCE), among the oldest pottery in the world: flame-style (kaen) vessels, deep cord-marked jars, and clay dogū figurines.

leaves.label: Yayoi Pottery
leaves.defn: Wheel-finished, smooth reddish earthenware of the Yayoi period in Japan (c. 300 BCE–300 CE): storage jars, pedestalled bowls and cooking pots, first found at Yayoi in Tokyo.

leaves.label: Tang Sancai
leaves.defn: Lead-glazed earthenware splashed in amber, green and cream (and rarely cobalt) made in Tang China for tombs and for use: phoenix-head ewers, dishes with stamped designs, camels and horses, and its Liao and Song successors.

leaves.label: Raku Ware
leaves.defn: Hand-modelled, low-fired tea bowls made in Kyoto from the 1570s by Chōjirō and the Raku family for the wabi tea ceremony: black Raku and red Raku bowls, and Hon'ami Kōetsu's bowls.

leaves.label: Satsuma Ware
leaves.defn: Pottery of Satsuma province in southern Kyushu founded by Korean potters (from 1598), from dark stoneware (kuro-satsuma) to the crackled ivory earthenware painted in enamels and gold for export in the Meiji era (Kyō-Satsuma, Yokohama-Satsuma).

leaves.label: Onggi
leaves.defn: Korean earthenware storage jars glazed with wood-ash and leaf-mould glaze, coil-built and paddled for fermenting kimchi, soy and pastes; master potters designated onggijang.

leaves.label: Kgatleng Pottery
leaves.defn: Earthenware pottery made by Bakgatla women potters in the Kgatleng District of Botswana, burnished and decorated (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2012).

leaves.label: Geometric Pottery
leaves.defn: Greek painted pottery of c. 900–700 BC with banded meanders and, in its late phase, figural funeral and battle scenes: Dipylon amphora, Hirschfeld Krater, Protogeometric amphorae.

leaves.label: Corinthian Vase Painting
leaves.defn: Painted pottery of Corinth, 725–550 BC, where black-figure was invented: miniature Protocorinthian aryballoi such as the Chigi olpe, and Corinthian animal-frieze kraters and alabastra.
leaves.weak: no English Wikipedia article (red link); Britannica entry is for the Proto-Corinthian phase

leaves.label: Black-Figure Pottery
leaves.defn: Greek vase painting with figures painted in black slip and incised on the red clay, above all in Attica, c. 620–480 BC: François Vase, Exekias's Achilles and Ajax amphora, Panathenaic prize amphorae.
leaves.aliases: Attic black-figure;black-figure vase painting;Greek vase painting;Greek pottery;Greek vase

leaves.label: Red-Figure Pottery
leaves.defn: Greek vase painting with figures reserved in the red clay on a black ground, invented in Athens c. 530 BC and carried to South Italy: Euphronios Krater, Berlin Painter's amphorae, Niobid Krater.
leaves.aliases: Attic red-figure;red-figure vase painting;Greek vase painting;Greek vase

leaves.label: Laconian Vase Painting
leaves.defn: Black-figure and earlier painted pottery of Sparta and Laconia, 7th–6th century BC: Arkesilas Cup, cups of the Hunt and Naucratis Painters.

leaves.label: East Greek Vase Painting
leaves.defn: Painted pottery of the Ionian coast and East Aegean islands, 7th–6th century BC: Wild Goat Style oinochoai, Fikellura amphorae, Klazomenian sarcophagi and vases, Chian chalices.

leaves.label: South Italian Vase Painting
leaves.defn: Red-figure pottery made by Greek workshops of Magna Graecia and Sicily, late 5th–3rd century BC, in its Apulian, Lucanian, Campanian, Paestan and Sicilian fabrics: Darius Vase, Asteas's phlyax kraters.
leaves.aliases: South Italian ancient Greek pottery;Italiote vase painting
src: Wikidata Q3373275 (South Italian ancient Greek pottery)

leaves.label: Gnathia Vases
leaves.defn: Black-glazed pottery of Apulia painted over the glaze in white, yellow and red, c. 370–250 BC: Gnathia skyphoi and oinochoai with vines, masks and garlands.

leaves.label: Centuripe Ware
leaves.defn: Hellenistic Sicilian pottery painted in tempera after firing, with pink grounds and figures in relief, 3rd–2nd century BC: lebetes and lekanides from Centuripe and Morgantina.

leaves.label: Etruscan Vase Painting
leaves.defn: Painted pottery of Etruria, 7th–3rd century BC, from Etrusco-Corinthian and black-figure to red-figure workshops at Vulci and Falerii: Pontic Group amphorae, Caeretan hydriae, Genucilia plates.

leaves.label: Bucchero
leaves.defn: The black, burnished, reduction-fired pottery of the Etruscans, 7th–5th century BC, from thin-walled bucchero sottile to moulded heavy bucchero: kantharoi, stamped oinochoai, rhyta.

leaves.label: Minoan Pottery
leaves.defn: Painted pottery of Bronze Age Crete, from Vasiliki ware through polychrome Kamares ware to the Marine and Floral Styles: Kamares cups, Octopus flask from Palaikastro, Palace Style jars.

leaves.label: Mycenaean Pottery
leaves.defn: Painted pottery of Late Bronze Age mainland Greece, c. 1600–1100 BC, traded across the Mediterranean: stirrup jars, pictorial chariot kraters, Warrior Vase.

leaves.label: Terra Sigillata
leaves.defn: The glossy red-slipped Roman tableware, plain and mould-decorated, made in Arezzo, Gaul, Germany and North Africa, 1st century BC – 3rd century AD: Arretine ware, South Gaulish samian bowls, African red slip ware.

leaves.label: Hadra Vases
leaves.defn: Hellenistic cinerary hydriae painted on a light slip, used for burials at the Hadra cemetery of Alexandria, 3rd century BC: Laurel Group and Dolphin Group hydriae.

leaves.label: Kerma Ware
leaves.defn: The thin, polished, black-topped red pottery of the Kerma kingdom of Upper Nubia, c. 2500–1500 BC: Classic Kerma bell-shaped beakers with a grey band.

leaves.label: Meroitic Pottery
leaves.defn: Wheel-made fine ware of the Meroitic kingdom of Kush, 1st century BC – 4th century AD, painted with religious emblems, plants and animals: painted jars and cups from Karanog and Faras.
leaves.weak: attestation weaker than others; owner check

leaves.label: Nabataean Pottery
leaves.defn: The eggshell-thin painted fine ware of the Nabataeans of Petra, 1st century BC – 2nd century AD, decorated with leaves and palmettes: Nabataean painted bowls.
leaves.weak: Nabataean pottery redirects to Nabataean art

leaves.label: Maya Ceramics
leaves.defn: The painted and carved pottery of the Classic Maya, above all the polychrome and codex-style cylinder vases and plates with courtly and mythological scenes and glyphic texts: codex-style vases of the Mirador Basin, Ik'-style vases of Motul de San José, Jaina figurines.

leaves.label: Teotihuacan Ceramics
leaves.defn: The pottery of Teotihuacan (c. 100–650 CE): cylindrical tripod vessels with painted stucco, Thin Orange ware and composite theatre-type censers: stuccoed tripod vases, Thin Orange effigy vessels, theatre censers.

leaves.label: Gran Coclé Pottery
leaves.defn: The polychrome pottery of central Panama (c. 200–1500 CE) in its named styles, painted with stylised crocodiles, birds and rays: Conté style plates from Sitio Conte, Macaracas pedestal dishes, Parita style.

leaves.label: Nicoya Polychrome
leaves.defn: The white-slipped polychrome pottery of Greater Nicoya (north-western Costa Rica and Nicaragua), c. 800–1500 CE, with Mexican-derived feathered-serpent motifs: Papagayo polychrome vessels, effigy jars.

leaves.label: Moche Ceramics
leaves.defn: Mould-made and painted stirrup-spout vessels of the Moche of Peru's north coast (c. 100–800 CE): naturalistic portrait heads, effigy vessels and fineline painted narrative scenes: portrait vessels, Presentation Theme fineline vessels.
leaves.see: G1-26 Moche Metalwork;L2-39 Moche Murals;E1-48 Nazca Pottery

leaves.label: Nazca Pottery
leaves.defn: Slip-painted polychrome pottery of the Nazca of Peru's south coast (c. 100 BCE–700 CE) in up to twelve colours, with mythical beings and trophy heads: double-spout and bridge bottles, Anthropomorphic Mythical Being bowls.

leaves.label: Chimú Blackware
leaves.defn: The burnished reduction-fired black pottery of the Chimú kingdom of Peru's north coast (c. 900–1470 CE), mould-made in stirrup-spout and effigy forms: stirrup-spout bottles with monkey adornos, double-chambered whistling vessels.

leaves.label: Shipibo-Conibo Pottery
leaves.defn: Pottery painted by Shipibo-Conibo women of the Peruvian Amazon with the maze-like kené designs that also cover their textiles and bodies: chomo jars, quenti cooking pots.

leaves.label: Talavera Poblana
leaves.defn: Tin-glazed earthenware of Puebla and Tlaxcala made since the 16th century by guild potters after Spanish maiolica, in blue-and-white and polychrome: tibores, lebrillos, azulejos of Puebla façades.

leaves.label: Barro Negro Pottery
leaves.defn: Black burnished pottery of San Bartolo Coyotepec (Oaxaca), reduction-fired and polished to a metallic sheen since Doña Rosa in the 1950s: cántaros, openwork vessels.

leaves.label: Tonalá Pottery
leaves.defn: The burnished and painted pottery of Tonalá and Tlaquepaque in Jalisco, in its colonial and modern styles: bruñido, petatillo, bandera, canelo.

leaves.label: Mata Ortiz Pottery
leaves.defn: Fine-walled painted pottery of Juan Mata Ortiz (Chihuahua) revived by Juan Quezada from the 1970s after Casas Grandes (Paquimé) wares.

leaves.label: Tree of Life
leaves.defn: Multi-branched painted clay candelabra-sculptures of Metepec and Izúcar de Matamoros depicting Eden and other narratives: Adam and Eve trees, Soteno family trees.

leaves.label: Pucará Bulls
leaves.defn: Paired glazed clay bulls of Pucará and Santiago de Pupuja (Puno) set on house roofs for protection and fertility.
leaves.see: E1-55 Tree of Life;D5-74 Caruaru Clay Figures

leaves.label: Chulucanas Pottery
leaves.defn: Burnished and smoke-resist decorated pottery of Chulucanas (Piura), revived from Vicús and Tallán techniques, with a denomination of origin.

leaves.label: Quinchamalí Pottery
leaves.defn: Black burnished pottery with white incised inlay made by women potters of Quinchamalí and Santa Cruz de Cuca in central Chile (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2022): guitarrera figure, chanchito alcancía.
leaves.aliases: Quinchamalí and Santa Cruz de Cuca pottery
alias_rows: Quinchamalí and Santa Cruz de Cuca pottery

leaves.label: Awajún Pottery
leaves.defn: Pottery made by Awajún women of the Peruvian Amazon with its knowledge and ritual, inscribed by UNESCO in 2021.

leaves.label: Goiabeiras Clay Pots
leaves.defn: Black clay cooking pots (panelas) of the paneleiras of Goiabeiras in Vitória (Espírito Santo), smoke-blackened with tannin, the first Brazilian intangible heritage registered by IPHAN (2002).
leaves.aliases: panelas de barro de Goiabeiras;craft of the clay pot makers of Goiabeiras

leaves.label: Ancestral Puebloan Pottery
leaves.defn: Pottery of the Ancestral Puebloans of the Four Corners (c. 500–1300), above all the painted black-on-white wares and corrugated grey wares: Mesa Verde black-on-white mugs, Chaco cylinder jars, Kayenta and Tusayan wares.

leaves.label: Mimbres Pottery
leaves.defn: Black-on-white bowls of the Mimbres branch of the Mogollon in south-western New Mexico (c. 1000–1130), painted with figural and geometric designs and buried, 'killed', with the dead.
leaves.see: E1-61 Ancestral Puebloan Pottery;E1-65 Casas Grandes Pottery

leaves.label: Hohokam Red-on-Buff Ware
leaves.defn: Buff-bodied pottery of the Hohokam of the Sonoran Desert (c. 300–1450) painted in iron-red with geometric, animal and human figures: Sacaton Red-on-buff, Santa Cruz Red-on-buff, Casa Grande Red-on-buff.

leaves.label: Salado Polychrome
leaves.defn: Red, white and black painted pottery of the Classic period southern Southwest (c. 1275–1450): Pinto Polychrome, Gila Polychrome, Tonto Polychrome.
leaves.see: E1-63 Hohokam Red-on-Buff Ware;E1-65 Casas Grandes Pottery

leaves.label: Casas Grandes Pottery
leaves.defn: Polychrome pottery of the Casas Grandes (Paquimé) culture of Chihuahua in its Medio period (c. 1200–1450), with macaws, plumed serpents and effigy forms: Ramos Polychrome, Babícora Polychrome.
leaves.see: mesoamerica_south_america H8-20 Mata Ortiz Pottery;E1-62 Mimbres Pottery

leaves.label: Pueblo Pottery
leaves.defn: Hand-coiled, slipped and painted pottery of the Pueblo peoples of New Mexico and Arizona from the Pueblo IV period to the present, made by women potters of each pueblo in its own ware: Zuni owls and water jars, Zia and Santo Domingo polychromes, Taos micaceous ware, Tesuque rain gods.
leaves.see: E1-61 Ancestral Puebloan Pottery;E1-67 Acoma Pottery;E1-68 Hopi Pottery;E1-69 Black-on-Black Ware

leaves.label: Acoma Pottery
leaves.defn: Thin-walled white-slipped pottery of Acoma Pueblo painted in black and orange, from historic water jars with parrots and rainbows to the fine-line revival of Lucy Lewis and Marie Chino.

leaves.label: Hopi Pottery
leaves.defn: Yellow-firing pottery of the Hopi mesas, from Jeddito and Sikyátki Polychrome (c. 1400–1625) to the Sikyátki Revival begun by Nampeyo of Hano at First Mesa around 1895 and carried on by Hopi-Tewa potters.

leaves.label: Black-on-Black Ware
leaves.defn: Burnished reduction-fired blackware with matte black designs developed by Maria and Julian Martinez at San Ildefonso Pueblo around 1918, and the polished and carved blackware of Santa Clara Pueblo.

leaves.label: Mississippian Pottery
leaves.defn: Shell-tempered pottery of the Mississippian cultures of the Eastern Woodlands (c. 800–1600): Cahokia and Moundville engraved bottles, head pots and effigy vessels, Caddo engraved bottles, Lamar complicated-stamped jars.
leaves.see: D2-10 Mississippian Shell Gorgets;E1-71 Swift Creek Pottery

leaves.label: Swift Creek Pottery
leaves.defn: Woodland-period pottery of Georgia and northern Florida (c. 100–800) paddle-stamped with curvilinear 'complicated stamped' designs carved on wooden paddles.

leaves.label: Weeden Island Pottery
leaves.defn: Pottery of the Weeden Island culture of Florida and the Gulf coast (c. 200–900): incised and punctated wares and the pierced animal-effigy vessels made for burial mounds (McKeithen effigy vessels).

leaves.label: Catawba Pottery
leaves.defn: Coil-built, burnished and pit-fired earthenware of the Catawba Nation of South Carolina, the oldest continuously practised Native pottery tradition east of the Mississippi.

leaves.label: Hermannsburg Potters
leaves.defn: The hand-built, painted terracotta of the Western Arrernte women of Hermannsburg (Ntaria) since 1990, with modelled animal lids and landscapes painted in underglaze: lidded pots.

leaves.label: Maiolica
leaves.defn: Tin-glazed earthenware of Renaissance Italy, painted in high-temperature colours, from Florentine and Faentine wares to the istoriato of Urbino and the lustre of Deruta and Gubbio: Deruta lustre dishes, Urbino istoriato plates, albarelli.

leaves.label: Faience
leaves.defn: Tin-glazed earthenware of France and its neighbours from the 16th century, made in named centres: Nevers blue-ground wares, Rouen lambrequin dishes, Moustiers grotesques.

leaves.label: Delftware
leaves.defn: Tin-glazed earthenware of Delft and the Netherlands, 17th–18th century, painted in blue in imitation of Chinese porcelain, and its English counterpart: tulip vases, tile pictures, blue-and-white chargers.

leaves.label: Saint-Porchaire Ware
leaves.defn: Rare French lead-glazed white earthenware of the mid-16th century, inlaid with coloured clays and modelled in Mannerist forms: salts, ewers, candlesticks.

leaves.label: Staffordshire Pottery
leaves.defn: The pottery of the Staffordshire Potteries, 17th–19th century: slipware, salt-glazed and creamware tablewares, Wedgwood's jasper and basalt, transfer-printed pearlware and Staffordshire figures: Toft slipware chargers, Wedgwood jasper vases, flatback figures.

leaves.label: Pennsylvania German Redware
leaves.defn: Lead-glazed red earthenware of the Pennsylvania Germans, 18th–19th century, slip-trailed or sgraffito-decorated with tulips and birds: sgraffito plates, slip-decorated pie dishes.

leaves.label: Talavera de la Reina Pottery
leaves.defn: Tin-glazed earthenware of Talavera de la Reina and El Puente del Arzobispo in Castile from the 16th century, in blue-and-white and polychrome, for tableware, apothecary jars and tile panels (UNESCO 2019, with Puebla): serie tricolor, Puente del Arzobispo green-and-ochre ware.
src: Wikidata Q5763703 (Talavera de la Reina ceramics)

leaves.label: Bisalhães Black Pottery
leaves.defn: Black earthenware of Bisalhães near Vila Real, burnished and fired in a smothered pit kiln (soenga), for cooking and decoration (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2016).

leaves.label: Gmundner Keramik
leaves.defn: Earthenware of Gmunden on the Traunsee, made since the 15th century, best known for its 'flamed' (geflammt) slip decoration in green, blue or brown.

leaves.label: Émaux de Longwy
leaves.defn: Faience of Longwy in Lorraine decorated since the 1870s with coloured enamels filled into printed outlines in the manner of cloisonné.

leaves.label: Izraztsy
leaves.defn: Russian glazed and relief stove and wall tiles from the 16th to the 19th century — terracotta, polychrome 'peacock-eye' relief tiles and painted Dutch-style tiles — for tiled stoves and church façades.
leaves.weak: attestation weak (commercial history page); Wikidata stove tile Q19921342 generic

leaves.label: Skopin Ceramics
leaves.defn: Glazed earthenware of Skopin (Ryazan region) since the 19th century, with fantastic sculptural vessels in the form of birds, beasts and dragons under green and brown glazes.

leaves.label: Balkhar Pottery
leaves.defn: Hand-built earthenware of the Lak village of Balkhar (Dagestan), made by women and painted in white engobe with free linear ornament.
leaves.weak: attestation weak (news page); ru-wiki Балхарская керамика redirects to Balkhar

leaves.label: Opishnia Ceramics
leaves.defn: The pottery of Opishnia (Poltava Oblast, Ukraine) with painted engobe ornament and sculptural vessels and toys (barany, lions).

leaves.label: Kosiv Painted Ceramics
leaves.defn: Engobe-painted earthenware of Kosiv and the Hutsul region (Ukraine), with green, yellow and brown sgraffito-painted scenes of Hutsul life on a white ground (UNESCO 2019).

leaves.label: Sokal Ceramics
leaves.defn: Traditional painted ceramics of Sokal in Lviv Oblast (Ukraine).

leaves.label: Bubnivka Ceramics
leaves.defn: Painted earthenware of Bubnivka (Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine), with dense floral ornament.

leaves.label: Oleshnia Pottery
leaves.defn: Traditional pottery of Oleshnia in Chernihiv Oblast (Ukraine).

leaves.label: Horezu Ceramics
leaves.defn: Slip-painted earthenware of Horezu in Oltenia (Romania), decorated with the cock, star and spiral in brown, red, green and blue on cream (UNESCO 2012).

leaves.label: Zlakusa Pottery
leaves.defn: Unglazed hand-wheel pottery of the village of Zlakusa in western Serbia, of clay mixed with calcite, for cooking pots (UNESCO 2020).

leaves.label: Seljuk Pottery
leaves.defn: fritware of Seljuq Iran and its neighbours (11th–13th century) other than its named lustre, mina'i and lajvardina wares: monochrome and carved, silhouette, laqabi and underglaze-painted wares.
leaves.aliases: Seljuq pottery; monochrome ware; silhouette ware; laqabi ware
leaves.see: E2-2 Kashan Lustreware; E2-3 Mina'i Ware.

leaves.label: Kashan Lustreware
leaves.defn: lustre-painted fritware of Kashan (late 12th–14th century) — vessels and the star, cross and mihrab tiles of Iranian shrines — signed by potter families such as Abu Tahir and Abu Zayd.
leaves.see: E1-2 Abbasid Lustreware; E2-3 Mina'i Ware.

leaves.label: Mina'i Ware
leaves.defn: overglaze-painted fritware of Kashan (late 12th–early 13th century), with figural scenes in seven colours.

leaves.label: Lajvardina
leaves.defn: Ilkhanid fritware with a cobalt-blue (lajvard) or turquoise glaze overpainted in white, red and gold leaf (late 13th–14th century).

leaves.label: Raqqa Ware
leaves.defn: fritware of Raqqa and Syria (12th–13th century), lustred or underglaze-painted in black under a turquoise glaze.

leaves.label: Sultanabad Ware
leaves.defn: Ilkhanid fritware of the late 13th–14th century with a grey-green slip and Chinese-inspired lotus and animal designs.

leaves.label: Iznik Pottery
leaves.defn: the fritware of Iznik in Ottoman Anatolia (late 15th–17th century) — vessels and tiles in its successive styles: blue-and-white (Abraham of Kütahya), Golden Horn, Damascus and Rhodian with its bole red.
leaves.aliases: Iznik ware; Iznik tiles; Rhodian ware
leaves.see: E2-8 Damascus Tiles; E2-11 Kütahya Ceramics; B1-1 Saz Style.

leaves.label: Damascus Tiles
leaves.defn: Ottoman-period fritware and tiles made in Damascus (16th–17th century), painted in blues, green and manganese without Iznik's red.

leaves.label: Kubachi Ware
leaves.defn: Safavid fritware of north-western Iran (16th–17th century) with crackled glaze, found in the village of Kubachi in Daghestan.

leaves.label: Safavid Pottery
leaves.defn: the fritware of Safavid Iran (16th–17th century) other than Kubachi ware: Kirman and Mashhad blue-and-white in the manner of Chinese porcelain, celadon imitations and late lustre.
leaves.aliases: Kirman ware; Persian blue-and-white; Gombroon ware

leaves.label: Kütahya Ceramics
leaves.defn: the fritware of Kütahya in western Anatolia (18th–19th century), small vessels and tiles often made by Armenian potters for church and household.
leaves.see: E2-7 Iznik Pottery; E1-9 Çanakkale Pottery.

leaves.label: Qajar Ceramics
leaves.defn: the tiles and vessels of Qajar Iran (19th century): moulded and painted figural tiles of Tehran and Shiraz (Ali Muhammad Isfahani) and revival lustre.

leaves.label: Qallaline Tiles
leaves.defn: the tin-glazed tiles of the Qallaline quarter of Tunis (17th–19th century), with Ottoman and Italian floral designs.
leaves.weak: no source found for this label yet

leaves.label: Jaipur Blue Pottery
leaves.defn: Quartz-paste (fritware) vessels and tiles of Jaipur painted in cobalt and turquoise under a clear glaze, from the 19th century: surahis, tiles.

leaves.label: Egyptian Faience
leaves.defn: Glazed sintered-quartz ware of ancient Egypt, blue and green, used for small sculpture, amulets, vessels and inlay: scarabs, ushabti figures, blue hippopotamus figurines, lotus chalices.

subs.label: Stoneware
subs.axis: Axis: named ware. Built at scale.

leaves.label: Khmer Ceramics
leaves.defn: The glazed stoneware of the Angkorian Khmer kilns of Cambodia and north-east Thailand (9th–14th century), in green and brown glazes: baluster jars, animal-form lime pots, roof finials.

leaves.label: Sawankhalok Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of the Si Satchanalai kilns in north-central Thailand (14th–16th century), celadon, brown and underglaze-black, exported widely to the archipelago: celadon dishes, covered boxes, figurines.

leaves.label: Vietnamese Ceramics
leaves.defn: Glazed stoneware of Vietnam from the Lý and Trần dynasties to the Lê export trade: Lý–Trần white and brown wares, Chu Đậu blue-and-white, Bát Tràng wares.

leaves.label: Yue Ware
leaves.defn: Grey-green celadon stoneware of Zhejiang (Eastern Han to Song), centred on Shanglin Lake, the first great Chinese celadon: chicken-head ewers, Five Dynasties mise (secret colour) ware made for the Wuyue court.

leaves.label: Yaozhou Ware
leaves.defn: Northern celadon of Tongchuan in Shaanxi (Tang to Yuan), olive-green glaze over crisply carved and moulded peonies and waves.

leaves.label: Longquan Celadon
leaves.defn: Celadon stoneware of the Longquan kilns in southern Zhejiang (Song to Ming), in thick bluish-green glazes and exported across Asia (UNESCO 2009): kinuta vases, mallet vases, large Ming dishes.

leaves.label: Ru Ware
leaves.defn: The rare celadon made for the Northern Song court at Qingliangsi in Henan (c. 1086–1125), with a crackled duck-egg-blue glaze; fewer than a hundred pieces survive.

leaves.label: Guan Ware
leaves.defn: Official ware of the Southern Song court at Hangzhou (Xiuneisi and Jiaotanxia kilns), thin dark-bodied stoneware with thick crackled glaze.

leaves.label: Jun Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of Henan (Song to Yuan) with an opalescent lavender-blue glaze splashed with copper purple: flowerpots and stands, bowls and dishes.

leaves.label: Jian Ware
leaves.defn: Dark-glazed tea bowls of Jianyang in Fujian (Song), prized in Japan as tenmoku: hare's fur, oil-spot and yōhen bowls.

leaves.label: Cizhou Ware
leaves.defn: Popular stoneware of northern China (Song to Ming) decorated through white slip by sgraffito, carving and black painting: pillows, meiping vases, jars painted with fish and peonies.

leaves.label: Yixing Ware
leaves.defn: Unglazed purple-clay (zisha) stoneware of Yixing in Jiangsu (from the 16th century), above all small teapots by named potters such as Gong Chun and Shi Dabin.

leaves.label: Goryeo Celadon
leaves.defn: The celadon stoneware of Goryeo Korea (10th–14th century) from the kilns of Gangjin and Buan, with jade-green glaze and inlaid (sanggam) decoration: maebyeong vases, kundika, incense burners.

leaves.label: Buncheong
leaves.defn: Grey stoneware of early Joseon Korea (15th–16th century) covered in white slip that is stamped, inlaid, incised, painted or brushed: mishima, hakeme and kohiki bowls prized in Japan.

leaves.label: Seto Ware
leaves.defn: Glazed stoneware of Seto in Owari, Japan's only glazed medieval kiln (from the 13th century), imitating Chinese celadon and tenmoku, and the tea wares of the neighbouring Mino kilns in the Momoyama period: Ko-Seto jars, Ki-Seto, Setoguro bowls.

leaves.label: Shino Ware
leaves.defn: Momoyama-period tea ware of the Mino kilns with a thick, pitted white feldspar glaze, sometimes painted in iron: e-Shino, nezumi (grey) Shino, the Unohanagaki tea bowl.

leaves.label: Oribe Ware
leaves.defn: Mino stoneware of the early 17th century named for the tea master Furuta Oribe, with copper-green glaze and boldly painted iron designs in asymmetric forms: kutsu (clog) tea bowls, fan-shaped dishes.

leaves.label: Bizen Ware
leaves.defn: Unglazed, wood-fired stoneware of Imbe in Okayama, one of the Six Ancient Kilns, with fire-marks (hidasuki, goma): tea-ceremony water jars, hanaire flower vases.

leaves.label: Shigaraki Ware
leaves.defn: Wood-fired stoneware of Shigaraki in Shiga, one of the Six Ancient Kilns, with feldspar inclusions and natural ash glaze: storage jars and tea wares.

leaves.label: Iga Ware
leaves.defn: Wood-fired stoneware of Iga in Mie, close to Shigaraki, with heavy ash glaze and distorted forms favoured for Momoyama tea vases and water jars.

leaves.label: Tamba Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of Tachikui in Hyōgo, one of the Six Ancient Kilns: ash-glazed storage jars and, from the Edo period, slip and glaze wares.

leaves.label: Tokoname Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of the Chita peninsula in Aichi, the largest of the Six Ancient Kilns: large medieval storage jars and later red-clay teapots.

leaves.label: Echizen Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of Fukui, one of the Six Ancient Kilns, descended from Tokoname techniques: ash-glazed storage jars and mortars.

leaves.label: Karatsu Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of northern Kyushu begun by Korean potters in the late 16th century, iron-painted (e-Garatsu) and glaze-patterned for tea and daily use.

leaves.label: Hagi Ware
leaves.defn: Soft stoneware of Hagi in Yamaguchi founded by Korean potters (1604), with pale crackled glazes that change with use, chiefly tea bowls.

leaves.label: Takatori Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of Fukuoka founded by the Korean potter Hachizō (early 17th century), refined tea caddies and bowls with flowing glazes for the Enshū taste.

leaves.label: Agano Ware
leaves.defn: Stoneware of Fukuchi in Fukuoka founded by Korean potters in the early 17th century, with green copper and iron glazes; one of Kobori Enshū's seven kilns.

leaves.label: Kyō Ware
leaves.defn: The pottery of Kyoto from the 17th century, overglaze-enamelled and painterly, by named potters and kilns: Nonomura Ninsei's enamelled tea jars, Ogata Kenzan's painted dishes, Awata and Kiyomizu wares.

leaves.label: Onta Ware
leaves.defn: Folk stoneware of a hamlet in Hita, Ōita, made by a few families since 1705 with slip, combed (tobiganna) and poured decoration; championed by the Mingei movement.

leaves.label: Koishiwara Ware
leaves.defn: Folk stoneware of Tōhō, Fukuoka (from the 17th century), the parent kiln of Onta, decorated with chattering (tobiganna) and brushed slip.

leaves.label: Mumyōi Ware
leaves.defn: High-fired red stoneware of Sado island made from iron-rich mumyōi clay, burnished and fired to a deep red-to-black (from the 19th century).

leaves.label: Rhenish Stoneware
leaves.defn: Salt-glazed stoneware of the Rhineland centres (Siegburg, Raeren, Frechen, Cologne, Westerwald), 15th–19th century, exported across Europe and its colonies: Bartmann (Bellarmine) jugs, Westerwald blue-and-grey tankards.

subs.label: Porcelain
subs.axis: Axis: named ware. Built at scale.

leaves.label: Bencharong
leaves.defn: Porcelain made in China to Thai order and enamelled in five colours on a black or coloured ground for the Ayutthaya and Bangkok courts: covered bowls, thepanom-figure jars.

leaves.label: Ding Ware
leaves.defn: Thin ivory-white porcelain of Quyang in Hebei (Tang to Yuan), fired upside-down with unglazed rims bound in metal, with carved and moulded lotus designs.

leaves.label: Xing Ware
leaves.defn: White porcelain of Hebei (Tang), the first fine Chinese white ware, paired in Tang texts with Yue celadon.

leaves.label: Qingbai Ware
leaves.defn: Bluish-white porcelain of Jingdezhen and southern China (Song and Yuan), translucent with a pale blue glaze pooling in carved designs.

leaves.label: Chinese Blue-and-White Porcelain
leaves.defn: Porcelain painted in cobalt under the glaze, made at Jingdezhen from the Yuan dynasty: Yuan large dishes, Ming imperial Xuande and Chenghua wares, Transitional and Kangxi porcelain.

leaves.label: Doucai
leaves.defn: 'Contending colours': underglaze-blue outlines filled with overglaze enamels, perfected at Jingdezhen under the Chenghua emperor (1465–87): chicken cups, Yongzheng doucai dishes.

leaves.label: Wucai
leaves.defn: 'Five-colour' porcelain of Jingdezhen (Jiajing and Wanli reigns) combining underglaze blue with red, green and yellow overglaze enamels, the precursor of famille verte.

leaves.label: Famille Verte
leaves.defn: Kangxi-period (1662–1722) Jingdezhen porcelain painted in overglaze enamels dominated by greens, with yellow-ground (famille jaune) and black-ground (famille noire) variants.

leaves.label: Famille Rose
leaves.defn: Porcelain painted in opaque pink and other overglaze enamels developed from European enamel in the 1720s: falangcai palace wares, yangcai, and export Rose Medallion and Rose Mandarin.

leaves.label: Jingdezhen Porcelain
leaves.defn: The porcelain of Jingdezhen's imperial and private kilns other than its named decorative wares: monochromes (peachbloom, robin's-egg, tea-dust), anhua hidden decoration, underglaze red and the imperial reign-marked wares of the Ming and Qing.

leaves.label: Kraak Ware
leaves.defn: Thin Jingdezhen blue-and-white export porcelain of the Wanli reign and after (c. 1570–1650), with panelled borders, shipped in quantity by the Portuguese and Dutch.

leaves.label: Swatow Ware
leaves.defn: Coarse export porcelain of the Zhangzhou kilns in Fujian (late 16th–17th century), blue-and-white and enamelled, traded to Southeast Asia and Japan.

leaves.label: Chinese Export Porcelain
leaves.defn: Porcelain made in China for European and American markets (16th–19th century) to order or in export styles: armorial services, Jesuit ware, Canton famille rose (Rose Medallion), Chine de commande.

leaves.label: Dehua Porcelain
leaves.defn: White porcelain of Dehua in Fujian (Ming and Qing), with an ivory glaze, known in Europe as blanc de Chine: Guanyin figures by He Chaozong, libation cups.

leaves.label: Joseon White Porcelain
leaves.defn: The white porcelain (baekja) of the Joseon court kilns at Gwangju (15th–19th century), plain or painted in underglaze cobalt, iron and copper: moon jars, blue-and-white dragon jars.

leaves.label: Arita Ware
leaves.defn: Porcelain of Arita in Hizen (Kyushu) from about 1616, shipped from Imari: shoki-Imari blue-and-white, Ko-Imari gold-and-red export ware, Dutch East India Company commissions.

leaves.label: Kakiemon
leaves.defn: Arita porcelain enamelled in the style of the Sakaida Kakiemon family (from the 1640s), sparse asymmetric designs on a milk-white body (nigoshide), copied at Meissen and Chantilly.

leaves.label: Nabeshima Ware
leaves.defn: Porcelain of the Nabeshima clan kiln at Ōkawachi (late 17th–19th century), made for gifts to the shogun: footed dishes with underglaze blue and enamel designs.

leaves.label: Hirado Ware
leaves.defn: Fine white porcelain of Mikawachi near Hirado (18th–19th century), painted in soft blue and finely modelled, often with Chinese boys under pines.

leaves.label: Kutani Ware
leaves.defn: Overglaze-enamelled porcelain associated with Kutani in Kaga: Ko-Kutani (17th century) in bold green, yellow and purple, and the 19th-century revival kilns (Yoshidaya, Eiraku).

leaves.label: Limoges Porcelain
leaves.defn: Hard-paste porcelain made at Limoges from the discovery of kaolin nearby (1768) to the industrial factories of the 19th–20th century (Haviland).

leaves.label: Gzhel
leaves.defn: Ceramics of the Gzhel district near Moscow, from 18th-century majolica and 19th-century semi-faience to the cobalt blue-and-white porcelain of the 20th century.

leaves.label: Meissen Porcelain
