leaves.defn: The first European hard-paste porcelain, made at the Saxon royal manufactory at Meissen from 1710 after Böttger's discovery, with enamel painting led by Höroldt and modelled figures by Kändler: Kakiemon- and chinoiserie-painted tea services, Kändler's Swan Service, Kändler's animal and commedia figures.
leaves.see: E4-26 Hard-Paste Porcelain;E4-17 Kakiemon;I3-5 Louis XV Style

leaves.label: Sèvres Porcelain
leaves.defn: The porcelain of the French royal (later national) manufactory founded at Vincennes and moved to Sèvres in 1756, soft-paste until the 1770s and hard-paste after, famous for its ground colours, gilding and biscuit figures: bleu céleste and rose Pompadour services, biscuit figures after Falconet and Boizot, Napoleon III table services.
leaves.aliases: Vincennes-Sèvres porcelain;Manufacture nationale de Sèvres;Sèvres ware
leaves.see: E4-25 Soft-Paste Porcelain;E4-26 Hard-Paste Porcelain;I3-5 Louis XV Style

leaves.label: Soft-Paste Porcelain
leaves.defn: European artificial (frit) porcelain fired at lower temperature than true porcelain, made from the Medici experiments to the French and English factories of the 18th century: Saint-Cloud and Chantilly wares, Chelsea gold-anchor figures, Worcester blue-and-white, Capodimonte figures.
leaves.see: E4-24 Sèvres Porcelain;E4-26 Hard-Paste Porcelain;E1-79 Staffordshire Pottery

leaves.label: Hard-Paste Porcelain
leaves.defn: True (feldspathic) porcelain made in Europe after Meissen's secret spread in the 18th century, by the court and private manufactories of the German states, Austria, Italy, Scandinavia, Russia and Hungary: Du Paquier Vienna tablewares, Bustelli's Nymphenburg commedia figures, Berlin KPM view-painted vases, Doccia and Cozzi wares.
leaves.see: E4-23 Meissen Porcelain;E4-25 Soft-Paste Porcelain;E4-21 Limoges Porcelain;E4-22 Gzhel

fams.label: Glass
fams.test: made of glass, placed by how it is formed and decorated.
key: 1. Decorated by cutting or carving? → F2. 2. Painted with enamel or gilding? → F3. 3. Lustre-painted? → F4. 4. Window or stained glass? → F5. 5. Otherwise blown or moulded glass → F1.

leaves.label: Beykoz Glass
leaves.defn: Ottoman glass of the Beykoz and Istanbul workshops (late 18th–19th century), above all the çeşm-i bülbül ('nightingale's eye') ware with spiral white and coloured threads.

leaves.label: Syrian Glassblowing
leaves.defn: the free-blown glass of the Damascus and Hebron workshops, inscribed by UNESCO in 2023 as a heritage in need of urgent safeguarding.

leaves.label: Roman Glass
leaves.defn: Blown, mould-blown, cast and cut glass of the Roman empire, 1st century BC – 5th century AD, made in Syria, Italy, Egypt and the Rhineland: Ennion's mould-blown cups, Portland Vase, Lycurgus cage cup.

leaves.label: Hellenistic Glass
leaves.defn: Core-formed, cast and mosaic glass of the Greek world and the Eastern Mediterranean, 6th–1st century BC: core-formed alabastra and amphoriskoi, cast bowls, gold-sandwich glass.

leaves.label: Venetian Glass
leaves.defn: The glass of Venice and Murano from the 15th century: clear cristallo, enamelled and gilded wares, filigrana (latticino), ice glass and chandeliers: Barovier wedding cup, filigrana goblets, façon de Venise.
leaves.weak: Murano glass redirects here

leaves.label: Art of Glass Beads
leaves.defn: Venetian and French lampwork and drawn glass beadmaking (perle veneziane), inscribed by UNESCO in 2020 for Italy and France.

leaves.label: Czech Blown Glass Bead Christmas Decorations
leaves.defn: Christmas tree ornaments made by hand from blown glass beads in the Poniklá region of the Czech Republic, silvered, coloured and threaded (UNESCO 2020).
leaves.aliases: Rautis decorations;handmade production of Christmas tree decorations from blown glass beads

leaves.label: Līvāni Glassblowing
leaves.defn: The glassblowing craft of Līvāni in Latvia, centre of Latvian glassmaking since 1887.

leaves.label: Art Nouveau Glass
leaves.defn: Art glass of c. 1885–1915 in Art Nouveau forms and colours: the cameo, acid-etched and marquetry glass of the École de Nancy and the iridescent blown glass of Loetz and of Tiffany: Gallé's Hand with Seaweed and Shells, Daum cameo vases, Loetz Phänomen vases.
leaves.aliases: Art Nouveau glass art;École de Nancy glass;art glass
leaves.see: F5-3 Tiffany Glass;I3-11 Art Nouveau;F2 Cut & Carved Glass;F5 Stained Glass

leaves.label: Studio Glass
leaves.defn: The movement of artists making glass in their own studios, begun at Harvey Littleton and Dominick Labino's Toledo workshops (1962) and spread through Pilchuck and the Czech school of cast glass sculpture: Littleton's Arcs, Chihuly's Macchia and Persian series, Libenský and Brychtová's cast sculptures, Tagliapietra's vessels.
leaves.aliases: Studio Glass movement;studio art glass;contemporary glass art
leaves.see: F1-5 Venetian Glass;I3-16 Contemporary Design;F1-9 Art Nouveau Glass

leaves.label: Islamic Cut Glass
leaves.defn: glass decorated by wheel-cutting and relief-carving in Iran, Iraq and Egypt (9th–11th century), from facet-cut bowls to relief-cut cameo glass and the Hedwig glasses.

leaves.label: Bohemian Glass
leaves.defn: Glass of Bohemia from the late 17th century, potash-lime crystal decorated by wheel-engraving and cutting, later with coloured and cased glass: engraved goblets, Zwischengoldglas, Biedermeier cased glass.

leaves.label: Mamluk Enamelled Glass
leaves.defn: enamelled and gilded glass of Ayyubid and Mamluk Syria and Egypt (13th–14th century): mosque lamps, beakers and bottles with blazons and inscriptions.

leaves.label: Islamic Lustre-Painted Glass
leaves.defn: glass stained with metallic lustre in Egypt, Syria and Iraq (8th–11th century), the predecessor of lustre pottery.

leaves.label: Medieval Stained Glass
leaves.defn: Coloured pot-metal glass painted with vitreous paint (and from c. 1300 silver stain) and leaded into windows for the churches of Latin Europe, c. 1100-1500, from Romanesque and High Gothic cathedral glazing to late Gothic workshops: Chartres and Sainte-Chapelle windows, Canterbury Miracle windows, Ebreichsdorf roundels, Strasbourg workshop of Peter Hemmel.
leaves.see: F5-2 Painted Glass Roundels;K4 Medieval European Architecture

leaves.label: Painted Glass Roundels
leaves.defn: Small panes of colourless glass painted in vitreous paint and silver stain, set into domestic and cloister windows in the Low Countries, northern France and the Rhineland, c. 1480-1560, often after designs by painters: roundels from the circle of the Master of the Amsterdam Cabinet, Labours of the Months roundels, Tobias roundels.
leaves.weak: Evidence: Met "South Netherlandish / glass" 75 objects (Cloisters, median 1510, 1 Timeline work). Label from the Met catalogue (Husband, The Luminous Image, 1995); no English Wikipedia article. Swiss heraldic cabinet pan

leaves.label: Tiffany Glass
leaves.defn: The opalescent and iridescent glass of Louis Comfort Tiffany's studios in New York (1878-1933) and the American opalescent window movement he shared with John La Farge: leaded windows, lamps, mosaics and blown Favrile vessels: Tiffany Studios wisteria lamps, Favrile vases, La Farge's Peonies Blown in the Wind window.
leaves.aliases: American opalescent glass;opalescent stained glass;Favrile glass
leaves.see: F1 Blown & Moulded Glass;I3-11 Art Nouveau

fams.label: Metalwork, Arms & Jewellery
fams.test: made of metal: vessels and objects, instruments, arms and armour, and jewellery.
key: 1. Worn as ornament? → G3. 2. A weapon or armour? → G2. 3. Otherwise vessels, objects and instruments of base or precious metal, cast, raised, engraved or inlaid → G1.

subs.label: Metalwork
subs.axis: Axis: workshop tradition (named school or technique).

leaves.label: Khurasan Metalwork
leaves.defn: cast and inlaid brass of eastern Iran and Herat (12th–13th century), with silver and copper inlay and figural bands (the Bobrinsky Bucket, 1163).

leaves.label: Mosul School of Metalwork
leaves.defn: inlaid brass made by craftsmen with the nisba al-Mawsili in Mosul, Syria and Egypt (13th century), the model for Ayyubid and Mamluk inlay.
leaves.see: G1-1 Khurasan Metalwork; G1-3 Mamluk Metalwork.

leaves.label: Mamluk Metalwork
leaves.defn: inlaid brass and bronze of Mamluk Egypt and Syria (1250–1517) — basins, candlesticks, Qur'an boxes — with epigraphic blazons (the Baptistère de Saint Louis by Muhammad ibn al-Zayn).
leaves.see: G1-2 Mosul School of Metalwork; G1-4 Veneto-Saracenic Metalwork.
alias_rows: Made by Muhammad ibn Sunqur al-Baghdadi, inlay by Hadj Yusuf ibn al-Ghawabi

leaves.label: Veneto-Saracenic Metalwork
leaves.defn: inlaid brass made in the Islamic manner in the 15th–16th century and long thought Venetian, now mostly given to Mamluk and Iranian workshops.
alias_rows: Mahmud al-Kurdi, Persian, active late 15th century

leaves.label: Ottoman Tombak
leaves.defn: fire-gilded copper of the Ottoman court (17th–19th century): ewers, basins, censers and mosque fittings.

leaves.label: Bidri Ware
leaves.defn: zinc-alloy objects inlaid with silver and blackened, from Bidar in the Deccan (from the 14th century).

leaves.label: Koftgari
leaves.defn: damascening of steel with gold and silver wire, practised in Mughal and Rajput India and in Iran for arms and objects.

leaves.label: Islamic Astrolabes
leaves.defn: brass astrolabes and celestial globes of the Islamic world, engraved instruments made by named makers in Baghdad, Isfahan, Lahore and al-Andalus.

leaves.label: Firoozeh Koobi
leaves.defn: Iranian metal objects set with turquoise chips in a mosaic over the surface (Isfahan, Mashhad).

leaves.label: Persian Metalwork
leaves.defn: inlaid and engraved brass and steel of Iran after the Mongols: Inju Fars inlay (14th century), Timurid and Safavid tinned-brass jugs, candlesticks and inkwells with poetic inscriptions, and Qajar cut steel (Hajji 'Abbas).
leaves.aliases: Timurid metalwork; Safavid metalwork; Qajar steel
leaves.weak: attested as a period group (Timurid, Safavid metalwork) in museum essays; no item for the umbrella name

leaves.label: Sogdian Silver
leaves.defn: Chased, engraved and gilded silver vessels of the Sogdian city-states (6th–9th century), many found in the Urals and Siberia: cups with roundels of ibexes, bowls with banquet and hunting scenes.

leaves.label: Animal Style
leaves.defn: The art of the Eurasian steppe nomads (Scythian, Saka, Sarmatian, Ordos, Xiongnu), 9th century BCE–3rd century CE, in which stylised and contorted animals cover gold and bronze plaques, harness and weapons: curled-feline plaques, Arzhan deer, Ordos belt buckles.

leaves.label: Dong Son Drums
leaves.defn: Bronze kettle drums of the Đông Sơn culture of northern Vietnam (c. 500 BCE–300 CE), cast with star-centred tympana, frogs and processions, traded across the archipelago: Ngọc Lũ drum, Hoàng Hạ drum, Makalamau of Sangeang.
leaves.aliases: Đông Sơn drums;Heger type I drums

leaves.label: Burmese Silver
leaves.defn: Repoussé and chased silver of Burma, 19th–early 20th century, with crowded narrative and zodiac friezes: offering bowls, betel boxes, presentation cups.

leaves.label: Chinese Ritual Bronzes
leaves.defn: Bronze vessels and bells cast in piece-moulds for ancestral rites from the Erligang and Shang to the Han: ding cauldrons, gu and jue wine vessels, taotie masks, inscribed Western Zhou gui.

leaves.label: Ordos Bronzes
leaves.defn: Cast bronze belt plaques, knives and fittings in the steppe animal style from the Ordos and northern frontier of China (6th–1st century BCE).

leaves.label: Yugi
leaves.defn: Korean bronze tableware forged or cast from high-tin bronze (bangjja yugi), of Anseong and Napcheong; makers designated yugijang.

leaves.label: Ipsa
leaves.defn: Korean inlay of silver and gold wire into iron and bronze (Goryeo to Joseon): incense burners, kundika and furniture fittings; makers designated ipsajang.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Crosses
leaves.defn: Processional, hand and pectoral crosses of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church in cast brass, silver and carved wood, with openwork lattices: Lalibela processional crosses, Gondar crosses, hand crosses.

leaves.label: Akan Goldweights
leaves.defn: Small brass weights cast by lost wax by the Akan for weighing gold dust, geometric and figurative (proverbs): abrammuo, with kuduo vessels and forowa boxes of the same casters.

leaves.label: Igbo-Ukwu Bronzes
leaves.defn: Leaded-bronze vessels and regalia cast by lost wax at Igbo-Ukwu (9th–10th century), with dense granular surfaces: roped pot, shell-shaped bowl, pendant ornaments.

leaves.label: Luristan Bronzes
leaves.defn: Cast bronze horse-bits, finials, standards, pins and weapons from the Zagros mountains of western Iran, early 1st millennium BC: master-of-animals finials, cheekpieces with winged creatures, votive pins.

leaves.label: Achaemenid Metalwork
leaves.defn: Gold and silver vessels and ornaments of the Persian empire, 6th–4th century BC: gold fluted bowls and rhyta, Oxus Treasure, griffin-handled amphorae.

leaves.label: Sasanian Silver
leaves.defn: Silver and silver-gilt vessels of Sasanian Iran, 3rd–7th century, hammered and chased with royal hunts and Dionysiac scenes: royal hunting plates, ewers with dancing figures, high-footed bowls.

leaves.label: Etruscan Mirrors
leaves.defn: Bronze hand mirrors of Etruria and Latium with mythological scenes engraved on the back, 6th–2nd century BC, together with the engraved cistae of Praeneste: mirror with Minerva and Hercules, Ficoroni Cista.
leaves.weak: Etruscan mirror redirects to Etruscan art; Praenestine cistae (wiki:Cista) placed as a kind

leaves.label: Moche Metalwork
leaves.defn: Gold, silver and gilded-copper objects of the Moche, worked by depletion gilding and inlaid with turquoise and shell: Sipán ear ornaments, backflaps, nose ornaments.

leaves.label: Sicán Metalwork
leaves.defn: Gold and tumbaga objects of the Sicán (Lambayeque) culture of Peru's north coast (c. 900–1100 CE): Sicán funerary masks, tumi knives, beakers.

leaves.label: Chimú Metalwork
leaves.defn: Hammered and repoussé silver and gold of the Chimú kingdom (c. 900–1470 CE): beakers, ear spools, feathered tunics with plaques.
leaves.see: E1-49 Chimú Blackware;G1-27 Sicán Metalwork;G1-29 Inca Metalwork

leaves.label: Inca Metalwork
leaves.defn: Gold and silver of the Inca empire (c. 1400–1532): cast and hammered figurines from capacocha offerings, keros and ornaments: silver llamas, gold female figurines.

leaves.label: Muisca Goldwork
leaves.defn: Lost-wax tumbaga castings of the Muisca of the Colombian highlands (c. 600–1600 CE), above all the votive tunjos: Muisca raft, tunjo figures.

leaves.label: Colonial Andean Silverwork
leaves.defn: The silver of the Viceroyalty of Peru (16th–19th century) from Potosí, Cusco and Lima: church plate, sahumadores, and the domestic and equestrian silver that continued in the Río de la Plata: incense burners in animal form, mate cups, altar frontals.
leaves.see: G3-14 Mapuche Silverwork;H2-6 Colonial Andean Tapestry

leaves.label: La Tène Art
leaves.defn: The curvilinear art of the Iron Age Celts, c. 450 BC to the Roman conquest, chiefly in bronze and gold metalwork: Basse-Yutz flagons, Waldalgesheim style torcs, Battersea Shield.

leaves.label: Migration Period Art
leaves.defn: The metalwork of the Germanic peoples, c. 300–800, in polychrome garnet cloisonné and the interlaced animal styles I and II: brooches and fibulae, Lombard gold-foil crosses, Visigothic votive crowns of Guarrazar.

leaves.label: Anglo-Saxon Metalwork
leaves.defn: Metalwork of Anglo-Saxon England, 5th–11th century, from garnet-cloisonné and filigree gold to Trewhiddle-style silver: Sutton Hoo great buckle, Staffordshire Hoard, Fuller Brooch.
leaves.weak: Anglo-Saxon metalwork redirects to Anglo-Saxon art#Metalwork

leaves.label: Viking Art
leaves.defn: The animal-ornament art of Scandinavia and its settlements, c. 750–1100, in its succession of styles named after finds (Oseberg, Borre, Jelling, Mammen, Ringerike, Urnes), chiefly in metal and wood: Oseberg ship carvings, Mammen axe, Urnes stave church portal.

leaves.label: South Staffordshire Enamels
leaves.defn: English painted enamel on copper of c. 1750–1800 from Bilston, Wednesbury, Birmingham and London (popularly 'Battersea enamels'): snuffboxes, étuis, patch boxes, cassolettes.

leaves.label: Ormolu
leaves.defn: Fire-gilt bronze of 17th–19th-century France and its imitators, cast and chased for furniture mounts, clocks and candelabra, and for mounting Chinese and Japanese porcelain: mounted porcelain vases, Gouthière candelabra.

leaves.label: Kubachi Silver
leaves.defn: Silver and metalwork of the Dargin village of Kubachi in Dagestan: engraved, niello and filigree vessels, arms and jewellery with dense floral ornament.

leaves.label: Kasli Iron Casting
leaves.defn: Cast-iron sculpture and openwork made at the Kasli works in the Urals since the 19th century: Kasli cast-iron pavilion (Paris 1900), statuettes of horsemen and animals.

leaves.label: Finift
leaves.defn: Painted enamel on copper of Russia, above all of Rostov the Great from the 18th century: icons, medallions and jewellery painted in enamel colours.

leaves.label: Hutsul Metalwork
leaves.defn: The brass casting and metal inlay of the Hutsuls of the Carpathians: cast crosses, jewellery, pipes and toporets axes, and brass-inlaid wood (UNESCO-listed in the Ukrainian National Inventory).
leaves.aliases: metalworking traditions of the Hutsul region

leaves.label: Drotárstvo
leaves.defn: Slovak wire craft developed by itinerant tinkers who mended pottery with wire and later made wire objects and sculpture (UNESCO 2023).

leaves.label: Limoges Enamel
leaves.defn: Enamel on copper made at Limoges, first as gilt champlevé (Œuvre de Limoges, c. 1150-1350) for reliquaries and liturgical objects, then as painted enamel and grisaille (c. 1470-1630) by dynasties of enamellers: champlevé chasses of Thomas Becket, Pénicaud triptychs, Léonard Limosin portraits, Pierre Reymond grisaille tableware.
leaves.aliases: Œuvre de Limoges;opus lemovicense;Limoges painted enamel;émail de Limoges
leaves.see: G1-43 Mosan Art;G1-36 South Staffordshire Enamels

leaves.label: Augsburg Goldsmiths' Work
leaves.defn: The silver and gold of the guild goldsmiths of the imperial city of Augsburg, Europe's leading exporter of display plate from the late 16th to the 18th century: embossed repoussé dishes and ewers, silver-gilt toilet services, Hildesheim prince-bishop's service, enamel- and gem-mounted Baroque cabinet pieces.
leaves.weak: Evidence: Met culture "German, Augsburg" 145 objects with 3 Timeline works, of which "German, Augsburg / metalwork" 50 (median 1690) plus enamels 5, horology 3; the rest is armour (Augsburg armourers, G2). Cooper Hewitt

leaves.label: English Silver
leaves.defn: Domestic, ceremonial and church plate made by the goldsmiths of London and the English assay towns from the Tudor period to the 19th century, transformed after 1685 by Huguenot refugee silversmiths: Huguenot ewers and wine cisterns, Paul de Lamerie's Rococo tea kettles, Georgian tea services, Regency presentation plate.
leaves.see: G1-44 Augsburg Goldsmiths' Work;I3-5 Louis XV Style
leaves.weak: Evidence: Met "British, London / metalwork" 142 objects (3 Timeline works) and "British / metalwork" 833 (8 Timeline works); Cooper Hewitt 211 silver objects made in England; Met P. de Lamerie (Q1751768) 74 objects, 1 Ti

leaves.label: Byzantine Enamel
leaves.defn: Gold cloisonné enamel of the Byzantine empire, 6th–12th century, in full (Vollschmelz) and sunk (Senkschmelz) techniques, on reliquaries, icons, crowns and book covers: Limburg Staurotheke, Pala d'Oro plaques, Holy Crown of Hungary, Fieschi Morgan Staurotheke.
leaves.see: G1-47 Chinese Cloisonné;G1-48 Japanese Cloisonné;G1-33 Migration Period Art;A3-2 Byzantine Icons

leaves.label: Chinese Cloisonné
leaves.defn: Cloisonné enamel on copper and bronze made in China from the early Ming (dated pieces from the Xuande reign, 1426–35) and at its height in the Qing imperial workshops, its turquoise grounds giving the name jingtailan: Xuande-mark lotus jars, Jingtai-mark gu vases, Qianlong cloisonné altar sets and elephants.
leaves.see: G1-48 Japanese Cloisonné;G1-46 Byzantine Enamel;D3-4 Chinese Snuff Bottles
leaves.weak: no English Wikipedia article (section Cloisonné#China); Met essay 'Chinese Cloisonné'

leaves.label: Japanese Cloisonné
leaves.defn: Japanese cloisonné enamel (shippō), revived by Kaji Tsunekichi of Owari in the 1830s and brought to its golden age c. 1880–1910 by the Kyoto and Tokyo workshops, with wired (yūsen) and wireless (musen) pictorial enamels: Namikawa Yasuyuki's Kyoto vases, Namikawa Sōsuke's Akasaka Palace medallions, Andō Jūbei's plique-à-jour.
leaves.see: G1-47 Chinese Cloisonné;G1-46 Byzantine Enamel;E1-22 Satsuma Ware
leaves.weak: Wikipedia 'Shippō' redirects to a short 'Shippo' disambiguation page, no enamel article; attested by LACMA and the Ashmolean (Namikawa Yasuyuki gallery); 58 Japanese cloisonné objects in the evidence

leaves.label: Mosan Art
leaves.defn: Romanesque goldsmiths' work and enamel of the Meuse valley (11th–13th century): Nicholas of Verdun's Klosterneuburg Altar, the Stavelot Triptych.

leaves.label: Islamic Arms and Armour
leaves.defn: the arms and armour of the Islamic courts: Mamluk and Ottoman helmets and mail, Persian shamshirs and watered-steel (wootz) blades, Ottoman yatağans and Mughal talwars, katars and jade-hilted daggers.
leaves.aliases: shamshir; yatağan; talwar; wootz steel; Damascus steel
alias_rows: The forging is attributed to As'ad Allah

leaves.label: Kris
leaves.defn: The asymmetrical pattern-welded (pamor) dagger of Java and the Malay world (UNESCO 2005), with carved hilts and sheaths, in regional forms from Sumatra to Mindanao: Javanese keris with naga blade, Balinese figural hilts, Bugis sheaths, Moro kalis.

leaves.label: Japanese Swords
leaves.defn: Blades forged and polished by Japanese swordsmiths in named traditions and schools: tachi, katana, tantō of the five traditions (Yamashiro, Yamato, Bizen, Sōshū, Mino).

leaves.label: Japanese Sword Mountings
leaves.defn: Metal sword fittings (tosogu) made by schools of metalworkers from the Muromachi to the Meiji: tsuba guards, menuki, kozuka, fuchi-kashira, in shakudō, shibuichi and mokume-gane.

leaves.label: Milanese Armour
leaves.defn: Plate armour of Milan, the leading European centre from c. 1400 to the 16th century (the Missaglia and Negroli families), from smooth white harness to embossed parade armour all'antica: Avant armour, Negroli burgonets.
leaves.weak: no English Wikipedia article; attested by Met catalogue text

leaves.label: Puukko
leaves.defn: The traditional Finnish belt knife with a wooden or birch-bark handle and leather sheath, made by named smiths (Kauhava, Fiskars).

leaves.label: Fatimid Jewellery
leaves.defn: gold jewellery of Fatimid Egypt and Syria (10th–12th century) in filigree and granulation, often enamelled.

leaves.label: Mughal Jewellery
leaves.defn: jewellery and jewelled objects of the Mughal court: kundan setting, enamelled (minakari) backs, carved emeralds and jade inlaid with gems.

leaves.label: Bedouin Jewellery
leaves.defn: the silver jewellery of the Bedouin and settled peoples of Arabia, Yemen and Oman, worked in filigree, granulation and with coral and carnelian.

leaves.label: Berber Jewellery
leaves.defn: the silver jewellery of the Amazigh peoples of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia: fibulae, headdresses and the cloisonné enamel of Kabylia.

leaves.label: Javanese Gold Jewellery
leaves.defn: Gold ornaments of Hindu-Buddhist Java (8th–15th century), cast, repoussé and set with stones: sacred-thread clasps, ear ornaments, rings with Sri inscriptions, Wonoboyo hoard.

leaves.label: Miao Silver Ornaments
leaves.defn: Silver headdresses, neck-rings and breastplates hammered and filigreed by Miao smiths of Guizhou for festival dress.
leaves.weak: museum page (Bowers Museum, Miao Masters of Silver); no Wikipedia article

leaves.label: Jangdo
leaves.defn: Korean ornamental knives in silver, horn and wood worn on the hanbok as accessory and symbol of fidelity; makers designated jangdojang.

leaves.label: Tairona Goldwork
leaves.defn: Cast gold and tumbaga ornaments of the Tairona of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (c. 900–1600 CE): bat-man and eagle pendants, nose ornaments, labrets.

leaves.label: Quimbaya Goldwork
leaves.defn: The gold of the Quimbaya of the Middle Cauca valley, with its ceramics: Quimbaya Treasure poporos, seated figures, helmets.

leaves.label: Calima Goldwork
leaves.defn: Hammered and cast gold of the Calima region of south-western Colombia in its Ilama, Yotoco and Malagana phases: diadems, nose rings, pectorals with faces.

leaves.label: Tolima Goldwork
leaves.defn: Flat cast gold pendants of the Tolima region of the Magdalena valley, with anchor-shaped human-bat figures.

leaves.label: Isthmian Goldwork
leaves.defn: Cast and hammered gold and tumbaga ornaments of the chiefdoms of Panama and Costa Rica (c. 200–1500 CE) in the Coclé, Veraguas, Chiriquí and Diquís styles: Sitio Conte plaques, eagle pendants, crocodile deity figures.
leaves.see: E1-45 Gran Coclé Pottery;G3-8 Tairona Goldwork

leaves.label: Mixtec Goldwork
leaves.defn: Lost-wax cast gold ornaments of the Postclassic Mixtec of Oaxaca, with filigree-effect wax threads: Monte Albán Tomb 7 pectorals, labrets, bell pendants.

leaves.label: Mapuche Silverwork
leaves.defn: The silver jewellery of Mapuche women in Chile and Argentina, flourishing from the 18th century: trapelacucha pectorals, tupu pins, trarilonco headbands.

leaves.label: Navajo Silverwork
leaves.defn: Silver jewellery and horse gear of Diné smiths since the 1850s, hammered, cast in tufa and stamped, set with turquoise from the 1880s: concho belts, squash blossom necklaces, ketohs, cuff bracelets.

leaves.label: Zuni Jewelry
leaves.defn: Lapidary jewellery of Zuni Pueblo, silver set with small cut stones since the 1920s: needlepoint and petit point, channel inlay, mosaic inlay.

leaves.label: Heishe
leaves.defn: Fine disc beads ground from shell, turquoise and stone and strung in necklaces, above all at Kewa (Santo Domingo) Pueblo.

leaves.label: Trade Silver
leaves.defn: Silver and later German-silver ornaments of the fur trade and of Native smiths of the Northeast, Great Lakes and Prairies (18th–19th century): ring and luckenbooth brooches, gorgets, armbands and hair plates.
leaves.weak: attestation weak (trade journal): see problems

leaves.label: Riji
leaves.defn: Pearl-shell pendants and pubic coverings of the Kimberley, engraved with interlocking meanders and filled with ochre, worn in ceremony and traded far inland: riji, jakoli, longkalongka.

leaves.label: Fabergé
leaves.defn: The jewellery and objets de luxe of the House of Fabergé in St Petersburg and Moscow, 1842–1918, in guilloché enamel, gold and hardstone: Imperial Easter eggs, cigarette cases, hardstone animals.

leaves.label: Hairwork
leaves.defn: Jewellery and pictures worked from human hair, a 19th-century fashion carried on as a village craft in Vamhus, Dalarna.

fams.label: Textiles, Carpets & Dress
fams.test: made of fibre: carpets and rugs, woven, embroidered, dyed and felted textiles, and dress.
key: 1. Knotted pile? → H1. 2. A flatweave (tapestry-woven kilim, soumak, warp-faced weaving)? → H2.
3. A figured or patterned woven textile (silk, brocade, lampas, velvet, tapestry, shawl)? → H3.
4. Decorated with the needle (embroidery, appliqué, needle lace)? → H4. 5. Patterned by resist-dyeing or printing (ikat, block print)? → H5. 6. Felt? → H6.
7. A dress tradition curated as such (a named costume ensemble)? → H7. A garment type alone is not an art tradition (P10).
8. Basketry, matting or barkcloth? → H8. Beadwork, porcupine quillwork or featherwork as the work? → H9.

subs.label: Pile Carpets & Rugs
subs.axis: Axis: weaving tradition; centres, tribes and design types are its kinds.

leaves.label: Persian Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted-pile carpets of Iran, from the Safavid court carpets (the Ardabil carpet, hunting and vase carpets, Polonaise carpets) to the city, village and tribal rugs named by their centres and peoples (Tabriz, Kashan, Isfahan, Kerman, Heriz, Qashqai, Bakhtiari).

leaves.label: Anatolian Rug
leaves.defn: knotted-pile carpets of Anatolia from the Seljuq Konya carpets onward: animal carpets, the 'Holbein' and 'Lotto' carpets known from European paintings, Ushak star and medallion carpets, and the village rugs of Bergama, Konya and Ghiordes.
leaves.aliases: Turkish carpet; Ushak carpet; Holbein carpet; Lotto carpet
leaves.see: H1-1 Persian Carpet; H1-3 Mamluk Carpet.

leaves.label: Mamluk Carpet
leaves.defn: carpets woven in Cairo under the Mamluks (late 15th–early 16th century) in red, green and blue with kaleidoscopic geometric fields.

leaves.label: Caucasian Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted-pile rugs of the Caucasus — Kazak, Karabagh, Shirvan, Kuba and the dragon carpets — and of the Azerbaijani schools.

leaves.label: Turkmen Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted-pile carpets and tent furnishings of the Turkmen tribes (Tekke, Yomut, Salor, Saryk, Ersari), with their tribal güls.
alias_rows: Traditional Turkmen carpet making art in Turkmenistan
Traditional Turkmen carpet making art in Turkmenistan

leaves.label: Baluch Rug
leaves.defn: dark-toned knotted rugs of the Baluch peoples of eastern Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
leaves.see: H1-5 Turkmen Carpet; H1-7 Afghan Rug.

leaves.label: Afghan Rug
leaves.defn: knotted rugs of Afghanistan, including the war rugs woven since 1979 with weapons and maps.

leaves.label: Mughal Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted carpets of the Mughal workshops of Lahore, Agra and Kashmir (late 16th–17th century): pictorial and flowering-plant carpets of very fine weave.

leaves.label: Moroccan Rug
leaves.defn: the pile and flatwoven rugs of the Amazigh tribes of Morocco (Beni Ouarain, Azilal, Boucherouite) and of the urban workshops of Rabat.

leaves.label: Freest Fisherman's Carpets
leaves.defn: Knotted carpets designed and made since the 1920s on the coast of the Bay of Greifswald (Freest, Western Pomerania), with motifs of fish, birds and sea.

leaves.label: Ryijy
leaves.defn: Finnish knotted-pile wall hangings and bed covers with a long shaggy pile, from 18th-century folk ryijys to modern artist-designed rugs.

leaves.label: Kilim
leaves.defn: tapestry-woven flatweaves of Anatolia, Iran, the Caucasus, Central Asia and North Africa, from slit-tapestry Anatolian kilims to Persian gelims, gabbeh-like tribal weaves and Tunisian mergoum.

leaves.label: Soumak
leaves.defn: weft-wrapped flatweaves of the Caucasus and north-west Iran, with a herringbone surface.

leaves.label: Al Sadu
leaves.defn: the warp-faced weaving of the Bedouin of Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, for tents and camel trappings (UNESCO 2011).

leaves.label: Inca Textiles
leaves.defn: The tapestry-woven cumbi cloth of the Inca state, woven by aqllakuna and cumbicamayoc, with tocapu tunics as the highest rank: Dumbarton Oaks tocapu tunic, checkerboard military tunics.
leaves.see: H2-5 Wari Textiles;H2-6 Colonial Andean Tapestry;H2-7 Andean Textiles

leaves.label: Wari Textiles
leaves.defn: The interlocking tapestry tunics of the Wari state (c. 600–1000 CE) with abstracted staff-god profiles expanded and compressed across the field.

leaves.label: Colonial Andean Tapestry
leaves.defn: Tapestry-woven textiles of the Viceroyalty of Peru (16th–19th century) in which cumbi weavers combined Inca, Spanish and Asian designs: colonial uncus with tocapu, tapices with coats of arms.
leaves.see: H2-4 Inca Textiles;G1-31 Colonial Andean Silverwork

leaves.label: Andean Textiles
leaves.defn: The living warp-faced and complementary-warp weaving of Quechua and Aymara communities of Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador, with named regional styles: Jalq'a and Tarabuco axsus, Chinchero lliclla, Otavalo weaving.
leaves.see: H2-8 Taquile Textile Art;H2-4 Inca Textiles

leaves.label: Taquile Textile Art
leaves.defn: The weaving and knitting of Taquile Island in Lake Titicaca, where men knit chullos and women weave belts (chumpi) recording the agricultural calendar, inscribed by UNESCO in 2008.

leaves.label: Saltillo Serape
leaves.defn: Tapestry-woven wool blankets of Saltillo and northern Mexico (18th–19th century) with a central diamond medallion and serrated fields.

leaves.label: Navajo Weaving
leaves.defn: Tapestry-woven blankets and rugs of Diné women on the upright loom: chief's blankets (first to third phase), eye-dazzlers, Two Grey Hills and Ganado rugs, Yeibichai rugs.

leaves.label: Chilkat Weaving
leaves.defn: Twined mountain-goat-wool and cedar-bark robes, tunics and aprons of the Tlingit and Haida, woven from painted pattern boards in formline designs.
leaves.see: H2-12 Coast Salish Weaving;H8-14 Spruce-Root Basketry

leaves.label: Coast Salish Weaving
leaves.defn: Twill and twined blankets of mountain-goat and dog wool woven by Coast Salish women on two-bar looms, revived since the 1960s.

leaves.label: Chimayó Weaving
leaves.defn: Hispano wool weaving of the upper Rio Grande valley, New Mexico, from colonial Rio Grande blankets to the Chimayó blankets and vests woven by families such as the Ortegas and Trujillos.
leaves.see: H2-10 Navajo Weaving;mesoamerica_south_america L72 Saltillo Serape

leaves.label: Māori Weaving
leaves.defn: The fibre arts of the Māori in harakeke (New Zealand flax) and muka (its fibre): finger-twined (whatu) cloaks with tāniko borders and plaited (raranga) baskets and mats: kaitaka and korowai cloaks, piupiu, kete, whāriki.

leaves.label: Ceinture Fléchée
leaves.defn: The finger-woven wool sash of French Canada and the Métis, with its arrow (flèche) and lightning patterns, an element of Quebec's intangible heritage: Assomption sashes.

leaves.label: Raanu
leaves.defn: Finnish weft-faced flatwoven wool coverlet and wall hanging in stripes and geometric patterns.

leaves.label: Chiprovtsi Kilim
leaves.defn: Tapestry-woven kilims of Chiprovtsi in north-western Bulgaria since the 17th century, with geometric and later floral designs (UNESCO 2014).

leaves.label: Pirot Kilim
leaves.defn: Double-sided tapestry-woven kilims of Pirot in south-eastern Serbia, with geometric motifs such as the turtle and the vine.

leaves.label: Sjenica-Pešter Kilim
leaves.defn: Kilims woven on the Pešter plateau around Sjenica in south-western Serbia.

leaves.label: Stapar Rugs
leaves.defn: Rug-making in the village of Stapar in Vojvodina (Serbia), with floral rugs on dark grounds.

leaves.label: Kotsy
leaves.defn: Ukrainian woollen flatwoven carpets (kots, kylym) of the Left-Bank and Polissia regions.

leaves.label: Reshetylivka Carpets
leaves.defn: Handwoven floral carpets of Reshetylivka in Poltava Oblast (Ukraine).

leaves.label: Romanian and Moldovan Wall Carpets
leaves.defn: Woollen wall carpets (scoarțe, covoare) woven in Romania and the Republic of Moldova and hung in houses as dowry and decoration (UNESCO 2016).

leaves.label: Tiraz
leaves.defn: inscribed textiles from the caliphal workshops (tiraz) of the Umayyads, Abbasids and Fatimids, with bands of embroidered or tapestry-woven Arabic inscriptions.

leaves.label: Safavid Silk Textiles
leaves.defn: the figured silks, lampas, brocades and velvets of Safavid Iran (Ghiyath al-Din 'Ali-yi Naqshband), with figural scenes and floral fields.

leaves.label: Ottoman Silk Textiles
leaves.defn: the silk lampas (kemha) and velvets (çatma) of Bursa and Istanbul (15th–17th century), with ogival lattices, tulips and çintamani.
leaves.see: H4-2 Ottoman Embroidery; B1-1 Saz Style.
src: Wikidata Q2864712 (art of the Ottoman Empire)

leaves.label: Nasrid Silk
leaves.defn: silks woven in Nasrid Granada and Almería (13th–15th century), with interlace, inscriptions and the 'Alhambra silks'.

leaves.label: Termeh
leaves.defn: Persian tapestry-twill woven with the boteh, made in Yazd and Kerman.

leaves.label: Kashmir Shawl
leaves.defn: twill-tapestry shawls woven from pashmina in Kashmir (17th–19th century), whose boteh became the paisley of European imitations.

leaves.label: Banarasi Brocade
leaves.defn: Silk brocades woven with gold and silver zari in Varanasi, from Mughal kinkhab to the Banarasi sari: kinkhab, jangla and butidar saris.

leaves.label: Jamdani
leaves.defn: Supplementary-weft figured muslin of Dhaka and Bengal (UNESCO 2013), with motifs inlaid by hand on the loom: jamdani saris, Dhaka muslin.

leaves.label: Kanchipuram Silk
leaves.defn: Heavy mulberry-silk saris of Kanchipuram with contrast korvai borders and temple motifs.

leaves.label: Paithani
leaves.defn: Silk and zari saris of Paithan and Yeola in Maharashtra with tapestry-woven peacock and lotus pallus.

leaves.label: Songket
leaves.defn: Silk or cotton brocade with supplementary weft of gold and silver thread, woven in the Malay courts of Sumatra, the Peninsula and Brunei: Palembang songket, Minangkabau songket.

leaves.label: Lampung Ship Cloths
leaves.defn: Supplementary-weft ceremonial cloths of the Lampung of south Sumatra depicting ships of the soul: the large aristocratic palepai banners and the ubiquitous tampan.

leaves.label: Piña
leaves.defn: Sheer cloth woven from pineapple-leaf fibre in Aklan and Manila, often embroidered (calado), made into barong and pañuelo.

leaves.label: Inabel
leaves.defn: The cotton handloom weaving of the Ilocos region of Luzon, in binakol whirlpool and other patterns.

leaves.label: Naga Motif Weaving in Lao Communities
leaves.defn: Handwoven Lao silks with naga serpent motifs in supplementary weft and ikat (UNESCO 2023): sinh skirts, pha biang shoulder cloths.

leaves.label: Kesi
leaves.defn: Silk tapestry woven with discontinuous wefts in China from the Tang, reproducing paintings and calligraphy in the Song and dressing the Qing court: Shen Zifan's kesi landscapes, dragon robes.

leaves.label: Zhuang Brocade
leaves.defn: Weft-patterned cotton-and-silk brocade of the Zhuang of Guangxi, one of China's four famous brocades.

leaves.label: Li Textiles
leaves.defn: The spinning, ikat-dyeing, weaving and embroidery of the Li (Hlai) women of Hainan (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2009): tube skirts, dragon quilts.

leaves.label: Shuri Weaving
leaves.defn: The court textiles of Shuri, the Ryukyu capital: hanaori and rōton-ori figured weaves and kasuri silks.

leaves.label: Bashōfu
leaves.defn: Cloth woven from Japanese banana fibre in Okinawa and Amami, plain or kasuri-patterned, centred on Kijoka.

leaves.label: Echigo-jōfu and Ojiya-chijimi
leaves.defn: Fine ramie cloth of the Uonuma region of Niigata, snow-bleached and often kasuri-patterned (UNESCO 2009).

leaves.label: Hansan Mosi
leaves.defn: Fine ramie cloth woven by women of Hansan in South Chungcheong (UNESCO 2011), for summer hanbok.
alias_rows: Weaving of Mosi (fine ramie) in the Hansan region

leaves.label: Kente Cloth
leaves.defn: Strip-woven silk and cotton cloth of the Asante and Ewe of Ghana and Togo, narrow strips with named warp and weft-float patterns sewn edge to edge: adwini asa, oyokoman, Ewe kente.

leaves.label: Aso Oke
leaves.defn: Prestige strip-woven cloth of the Yoruba of Nigeria: sanyan, alaari, etu.

leaves.label: Akwete Cloth
leaves.defn: Cloth woven by Ndoki Igbo women of Akwete on the vertical loom, with the ikaki (tortoise) motif.

leaves.label: Ivorian Loincloth Weaving
leaves.defn: The traditional loincloth (pagne) weaving of Côte d'Ivoire, strip-woven on narrow looms (Baule, Senufo, Dioula, Dan), inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.

leaves.label: Coptic Textiles
leaves.defn: Tapestry-woven linen and wool textiles of late antique and early Islamic Egypt, 3rd–8th century, from burial grounds: tunic clavi and roundels, hangings with Dionysiac and Nilotic scenes, weft-loop wall hangings.
leaves.weak: Coptic textiles redirects to Coptic art; evidenced by Egyptian (textiles 1868)

leaves.label: Maya Textiles
leaves.defn: The backstrap-woven and brocaded cotton cloth of the Maya of Guatemala and Chiapas, whose huipiles, sashes and headcloths are distinct by town and community: Chichicastenango huipiles, Santiago Atitlán tzutes, Chamula wool.

leaves.label: Chancay Textiles
leaves.defn: Cotton and camelid cloth of the Chancay culture of Peru's central coast (c. 1000–1470 CE): gauze and openwork, painted cloth and woven dolls: gauze panels, painted cloths.

leaves.label: Flemish Tapestry
leaves.defn: Tapestry woven in the Southern Netherlands, 14th–17th century, at Arras, Tournai, Brussels, Oudenaarde and Antwerp, after cartoons by leading painters: Apocalypse of Angers, Unicorn tapestries, Acts of the Apostles after Raphael.

leaves.label: Aubusson Tapestry
leaves.defn: Tapestry and carpet weaving of Aubusson and Felletin in the Creuse, from the 16th century to its 20th-century revival (Lurçat), inscribed by UNESCO in 2009.

leaves.label: Täkänä
leaves.defn: Finnish double-weave (Finn-pick) technique giving reversible two-colour cloth, used for coverlets and hangings.
leaves.weak: attestation weak (Finlandia Foundation course page)

leaves.label: Northern Vidzeme Double-Weave Blankets
leaves.defn: Double-weave colour-gradient blanket weaving of Northern Vidzeme in Latvia.

leaves.label: Sigulda Belts
leaves.defn: Patterned belts woven in Sigulda municipality (Latvia).

leaves.label: Bezdan Damask
leaves.defn: Damask linen woven in Bezdan (Vojvodina, Serbia) since the 1880s, with pictorial and floral designs.

leaves.label: Serpanok Weaving
leaves.defn: Weaving of serpanok, a fine gauze-like cloth, in Dubrovytsia hromada (Rivne Oblast, Ukraine).

leaves.label: Hlyniany Textile
leaves.defn: Patterned woven textiles of Hlyniany (Lviv Oblast, Ukraine), long known for its kilims.

leaves.label: Obukhovychi Weaving
leaves.defn: Traditional patterned weaving of the village of Obukhovychi (Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine).

leaves.label: Gobelins Tapestry
leaves.defn: Tapestry woven at the royal Gobelins Manufactory in Paris from 1662 under Le Brun, the official weaving of the French crown (The History of the King, Les Maisons royales, the Boucher Loves of the Gods).

leaves.label: Beauvais Tapestry
leaves.defn: Tapestry woven at the Beauvais Manufactory from 1664, the private royal works for furniture covers and lighter subjects after Oudry and Boucher (Fêtes italiennes, Chinese Series).

leaves.label: Suzani
leaves.defn: large embroidered hangings and covers of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan (Bukhara, Nurata, Samarkand, Shakhrisabz), worked in silk chain and couching stitch.

leaves.label: Ottoman Embroidery
leaves.defn: the silk and metal-thread embroidery of Ottoman households and court: towels, napkins, covers and garments, worked in double running and satin stitch.
leaves.see: H3-3 Ottoman Silk Textiles; H4-6 Oya.

leaves.label: Palestinian Embroidery
leaves.defn: tatreez: the cross-stitch embroidery of Palestinian women's dress by village and region (UNESCO 2021).
alias_rows: The art of embroidery in Palestine, practices, skills, knowledge and rituals

leaves.label: Pateh
leaves.defn: the wool embroidery of Kerman in Iran, densely covering woollen cloth with boteh and floral designs.

leaves.label: Rasht Embroidery
leaves.defn: felt appliqué and chain-stitch embroidery of Rasht in Gilan (Iran).

leaves.label: Oya
leaves.defn: Turkish needle lace: knotted borders of flowers for headscarves.

leaves.label: Khayamiya
leaves.defn: the appliqué tent panels of the Cairo tentmakers' street, Sharia al-Khayamiya.

leaves.label: Balochi Needlework
leaves.defn: the dense geometric embroidery of Baloch women's dress (Iran, Pakistan, Afghanistan).

leaves.label: Phulkari
leaves.defn: Darn-stitch silk embroidery on khaddar of the women of Punjab, in sparse phulkari and fully covered bagh: bagh, chope.

leaves.label: Chikankari
leaves.defn: White-on-white shadow and knot-stitch embroidery of Lucknow on fine cotton.

leaves.label: Kantha
leaves.defn: Running-stitch embroidery on layered old cloth by the women of Bengal and Bangladesh: nakshi kantha, lep kantha.

leaves.label: Sujani
leaves.defn: Running-stitch embroidered quilts of Bhusura in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, with narrative figures.

leaves.label: Ralli Quilt
leaves.defn: Patchwork, applique and embroidered quilts of Sindh, Cholistan, Kutch and Rajasthan.

leaves.label: Chakan
leaves.defn: The silk-on-cotton floral embroidery of Tajikistan for garments, coverlets and wall hangings (UNESCO 2018): chakan dresses, wall hangings.

leaves.label: Khamak
leaves.defn: The fine geometric satin-stitch embroidery of Kandahar and of Hazara women in Afghanistan, worked from the back on fine cotton: shirt panels, pillow covers, shawls.

leaves.label: Turkmen Needlework
leaves.defn: The embroidery applied to Turkmen dress of all ages and sexes in Turkmenistan and Iran, in chain, satin and stitch-band techniques (UNESCO 2022): chyrpy mantles, tahya caps.

leaves.label: Tapis
leaves.defn: The ceremonial tube skirts of Lampung women, warp-ikat and woven grounds couched with gold thread, mica and embroidery.

leaves.label: Kalaga
leaves.defn: Burmese padded appliqué hangings embroidered with sequins and metal thread in scenes from the Jatakas and court life.

leaves.label: Tekat
leaves.defn: Malay raised gold-thread embroidery couched over card or padding, for cushions, betel covers and wedding furnishings.

leaves.label: Suzhou Embroidery
leaves.defn: Silk embroidery of Suzhou in Jiangsu, one of China's four famous embroideries, fine-split thread and double-sided pieces: cats, goldfish, painting copies.

leaves.label: Xiang Embroidery
leaves.defn: Silk embroidery of Changsha in Hunan, one of the four famous embroideries, famed for tigers and lions in shaded stitches.

leaves.label: Shu Embroidery
leaves.defn: Silk embroidery of Chengdu in Sichuan, one of the four famous embroideries: pandas, carp and hibiscus on satin.

leaves.label: Cantonese Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery of the Pearl River Delta (Guangzhou and Chaozhou), dense and brilliant, with raised gold-thread work; one of the four famous embroideries.

leaves.label: Gu Embroidery
leaves.defn: Painting-embroidery of the Gu family of Shanghai (late Ming), copying Song and Yuan paintings in silk thread: Han Ximeng's albums.

leaves.label: Korean Embroidery
leaves.defn: Silk embroidery of Joseon court and household (jasu): embroidered screens, rank badges (hyungbae), pillow ends, wedding robes (hwarot); masters designated jasujang.

leaves.label: Bojagi
leaves.defn: Korean wrapping cloths, above all jogakbo patchwork of leftover ramie and silk, and embroidered subo.

leaves.label: Sashiko
leaves.defn: Japanese running-stitch quilting and darning of indigo cloth, in regional forms: kogin of Tsugaru, hishizashi, mended boro.

leaves.label: Hmong Textile Art
leaves.defn: Embroidery, batik, appliqué and pleating of the Miao (Hmong) of Guizhou and the Hmong diaspora: pleated skirts, baby carriers, story cloths (paj ntaub).

leaves.label: Ainu Textiles
leaves.defn: Ainu robes of elm-bark (attus) and nettle cloth and of imported cotton, with appliqué and chain-stitch embroidery of curving designs: ruunpe, chikarkarpe, kaparamip.
alias_rows: Ainu textiles and carving (attush, ruunpe, ikupasuy)

leaves.label: Kuba Raffia Textiles
leaves.defn: Raffia cloth of the Kuba peoples of the DR Congo, woven by men and embroidered by women: Shoowa cut-pile ('Kasai velvet') panels, appliqué overskirts, Bushoong ceremonial skirts.

leaves.label: Asafo Flags
leaves.defn: Appliqué regimental flags (frankaa) of the Fante Asafo companies of coastal Ghana, with proverb designs and a corner Union Jack or Ghanaian flag.

leaves.label: Paracas Textiles
leaves.defn: Camelid-wool embroidered mantles from the Paracas Necropolis on Peru's south coast (c. 300 BCE–200 CE), stem-stitched with repeating flying figures: Paracas Necropolis mantles.

leaves.label: Mola
leaves.defn: Reverse-appliqué cotton panels made by Guna women of Panama and Colombia for the front and back of their blouses.

leaves.label: Arpillera
leaves.defn: Appliqué and embroidered burlap-backed pictures made by women's workshops in Chile under the Pinochet dictatorship and later in Peru.

leaves.label: Drapo Vodou
leaves.defn: Sequinned and beaded ritual flags of Haitian Vodou, carried to salute the lwa: vèvè flags, Myrlande Constant tapestries.

leaves.label: Ñandutí
leaves.defn: Paraguayan needle lace of radiating spider-web suns, made in Itauguá.

leaves.label: Divina Pastora Irish Lace
leaves.defn: The needle lace (renda irlandesa) made with cord and buttonhole stitches in Divina Pastora, Sergipe, registered by IPHAN.

leaves.label: Seminole Patchwork
leaves.defn: Machine-pieced bands of cotton strips sewn into skirts, jackets and shirts by Seminole and Miccosukee women of Florida since the early 20th century.

leaves.label: Ribbonwork
leaves.defn: Silk-ribbon appliqué cut and layered in negative and positive designs on skirts, leggings and blankets by Great Lakes and Prairie peoples (Menominee, Ho-Chunk, Meskwaki, Potawatomi, Osage) since the late 18th century.

leaves.label: Moosehair Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery in dyed moosehair on birchbark and black cloth by Wendat (Huron) women of Wendake (Lorette) and other Northeastern peoples, learned from Ursuline nuns: floral moccasins, calling-card boxes, cigar cases.

leaves.label: Star Quilts
leaves.defn: Pieced quilts centred on a single eight-pointed star of diamond patches, made by Lakota, Dakota and other Plains women since the reservation era and given at honouring and memorial giveaways.

leaves.label: Tivaevae
leaves.defn: The appliqué and piecework quilts of the Cook Islands (and tīfaifai of Tahiti), sewn communally by women's groups (vainetini) and given at weddings, birthdays and funerals: tivaevae manu, tivaevae taorei, tivaevae tataura.

leaves.label: Opus Anglicanum
leaves.defn: English medieval embroidery in silk and gold thread, c. 1200–1400, prized across Europe for vestments: Syon Cope, Butler-Bowdon Cope, Steeple Aston Cope.

leaves.label: Bucks Point Lace
leaves.defn: English bobbin lace of Buckinghamshire and the East Midlands, 18th–19th century, a point-ground lace in the manner of Lille and Mechlin.
leaves.see: D2-11 Brussels Lace, D2-12 Mechlin Lace, D5-92 Honiton Lace (europe_folk_west)

leaves.label: Bedfordshire Lace
leaves.defn: English bobbin lace of the Midlands from the mid-19th century, a guipure lace of plaits and leaves influenced by Maltese lace.

leaves.label: Amish Quilts
leaves.defn: Pieced quilts of the Amish of Pennsylvania and the Midwest, c. 1870–1950, in solid dark colours and bold geometric fields with fine quilting: Center Diamond, Bars, Sunshine and Shadow.
leaves.see: T158 Quilts of Gee's Bend (artist);G3-20 Star Quilts (north_america_indigenous)

leaves.label: Hooked Rugs
leaves.defn: Rugs and mats made by hooking strips of cloth or yarn through a backing, in New England and the Canadian Maritimes from the 19th century, including the Grenfell mats of Labrador and Newfoundland.

leaves.label: Greek Island Embroidery
leaves.defn: The silk-on-linen embroidery of the Aegean and Ionian islands and Epirus (17th–19th century), each island with its own stitches and designs, used for bed curtains, cushions and dress: Cretan skirt borders, Rhodian bed tents, Naxos and Dodecanese hangings.

leaves.label: Hardanger Embroidery
leaves.defn: Norwegian whitework of counted satin-stitch blocks (kloster) with cut and drawn threads, from the Hardanger district, used on bunad aprons and linens.

leaves.label: Mountmellick Embroidery
leaves.defn: Irish white embroidery of raised floral designs in thick cotton on white cotton satin, begun in Mountmellick, County Laois, about 1825 by Johanna Carter.

leaves.label: Arraiolos Rug
leaves.defn: Portuguese wool rugs embroidered in Slav (long-armed cross) stitch on linen or jute canvas, made in Arraiolos in the Alentejo since the 17th century.

leaves.label: Bordados da Glória do Ribatejo
leaves.defn: The embroidery of Glória do Ribatejo (Salvaterra de Magos), worked mainly in cross stitch on household linens and local dress.

leaves.label: Alençon Lace
leaves.defn: French needle lace of Alençon in Normandy, developed in the 1660s under royal patronage and made into the 19th century, with fine réseau ground and corded outlines: flounces, lappets.

leaves.label: Burano Lace
leaves.defn: Venetian needle lace of the island of Burano, revived in 1872 by the Burano lace school on the model of the old Venetian points.
leaves.weak: enwiki redirect goes to Argentella; QID used

leaves.label: Lefkara Lace
leaves.defn: The drawn-thread and needle-lace embroidery of Pano Lefkara in Cyprus, worked on linen in geometric designs (UNESCO 2009).

leaves.label: Brussels Lace
leaves.defn: Pillow lace of Brussels and Brabant, its motifs made separately in bobbin or needle lace and joined to a droschel or bride ground (17th–19th century), including point de gaze and Brussels appliqué.

leaves.label: Mechlin Lace
leaves.defn: Flemish bobbin lace of Mechelen with a hexagonal ground and a flat thread outlining the motifs, the 18th century's favourite lace for ruffles.

leaves.label: Quill Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery of leather with split quills of peacock tail feathers on belts, braces and shoes of Alpine dress, practised in Tyrol (Sarntal) and Austria.

leaves.label: Honiton Lace
leaves.defn: English bobbin lace of east Devon whose motifs are made separately and joined, famed for Queen Victoria's wedding lace (1840).

leaves.label: Le Puy Lace
leaves.defn: Bobbin lace of Le Puy-en-Velay in the Auvergne, in linen, silk and wool guipures and Cluny-style laces made by cottage lacemakers.

leaves.label: Maltese Lace
leaves.defn: Bobbin lace of Malta and Gozo, above all the 19th-century silk guipure with the Maltese cross and wheatears.

leaves.label: Headford Lace
leaves.defn: The bobbin lace of Headford, County Galway, a cottage industry of the 18th–19th centuries revived today.

leaves.label: Carrickmacross Lace
leaves.defn: Irish appliqué lace of County Monaghan, cambric shapes cut and sewn on machine net, introduced about 1820 by Mrs Grey Porter.
leaves.see: H4-64 Limerick Lace;H4-65 Irish Crochet Lace

leaves.label: Limerick Lace
leaves.defn: Irish embroidered net lace of Limerick (from 1829), worked in tambour (chain stitch) or run (darning) stitch on machine net.

leaves.label: Irish Crochet Lace
leaves.defn: Crochet made in imitation of Venetian needle lace, spread as famine relief from the 1840s; motifs are worked separately and joined with a crocheted mesh: Clones lace, Youghal-area crochet.

leaves.label: Ukrainian Embroidery
leaves.defn: The regional embroidery of Ukraine on shirts (vyshyvanka), rushnyky and household linen in cross, satin and counted stitches, distinct by region and village: Reshetylivka white-on-white, Borshchiv black shirts, Podillia nyz.

leaves.label: Rushnyk
leaves.defn: East Slavic ritual cloths of linen embroidered or woven with symbolic red and black ornament, used at weddings, funerals and to dress icons: Krolevets woven rushnyky.

leaves.label: Belarusian Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery of Belarus on ritual towels, shirts and aprons in counted red geometric ornament, including the Vetka negliubka tradition.

leaves.label: Chuvash Embroidery
leaves.defn: Counted-thread embroidery of the Chuvash of the Volga in red, black and green on white linen, for headdresses, shirts and ritual cloths.

leaves.label: Mari Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery of the Mari of the Volga-Kama region, dense red-and-black geometric patterns on shirts and headdresses (shurka, shymaksh).

leaves.label: Karelian Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery of the Karelians of Finland and Russia, in red counted and drawn work on towels and shirts.

leaves.label: Krestets Stitch
leaves.defn: Drawn-thread whitework embroidery of Krestsy (Novgorod region) on linen, with geometric openwork grounds.

leaves.label: Mstyora Embroidery
leaves.defn: White satin-stitch and openwork embroidery of Mstyora (Vladimir region) on batiste and linen.

leaves.label: Muhu Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery of the Estonian island of Muhu, with bold floral motifs and birds in bright pinks, greens and oranges on black wool.
leaves.weak: attestation weak (TATTER workshop page)

leaves.label: Matyó Embroidery
leaves.defn: The embroidery of the Matyó community of Mezőkövesd in Hungary, with dense roses and peonies in bright satin stitch (UNESCO 2012).
leaves.aliases: Folk art of the Matyó;Mezőkövesd embroidery

leaves.label: Zmijanje Embroidery
leaves.defn: Dark-blue wool embroidery on women's dress and household linen of the Zmijanje villages near Banja Luka (UNESCO 2014).

leaves.label: Macedonian Embroidery
leaves.defn: Embroidery of North Macedonia on women's shirts and sleeves in dense red, black and gold geometric motifs.

leaves.label: Kosovo-Style Embroidery
leaves.defn: Serbian embroidery in the Kosovo style, inscribed in the Serbian ICH inventory.

leaves.label: Altiță
leaves.defn: Embroidery on the shoulder band (altiță) of the Romanian and Moldovan traditional blouse (ie), the defining ornament of the costume (UNESCO 2022).

leaves.label: Syrian-Armenian Embroidery
leaves.defn: The embroidery culture of the Syrian-Armenian community of Armenia (Marash and Aintab traditions), inscribed in Armenia's ICH list.
leaves.aliases: Embroidery culture of the Syrian-Armenian community

leaves.label: Armenian Needlelace
leaves.defn: Knotted needle lace of Armenia and the Armenian diaspora, made with a needle in rows of knots for collars and covers.

leaves.label: Tatar Leather Mosaic
leaves.defn: The Kazan Tatar technique (kayuly kün) of stitching coloured morocco pieces into mosaic patterns with gold thread, for boots (ichigi) and slippers.

leaves.label: Orenburg Shawl
leaves.defn: Knitted lace shawls of goat down from the Orenburg region, including the fine gossamer 'web' shawl that passes through a ring.

leaves.label: Vologda Lace
leaves.defn: Bobbin tape lace of Vologda with continuous tape patterns on a net ground (from the 19th century).

leaves.label: Yelets Lace
leaves.defn: Fine bobbin tape lace of Yelets (Lipetsk region), with small motifs on delicate grounds.

leaves.label: Rauma Lace
leaves.defn: Bobbin lace of the town of Rauma in Finland, made since the 18th century with fine linen thread.

leaves.label: Lace-Making in Heinämaa
leaves.defn: The bobbin lace tradition of the village of Heinämaa in Finland.

leaves.label: Knipelēšana
leaves.defn: Latvian bobbin lace-making tradition.

leaves.label: Idrija Lace
leaves.defn: Bobbin tape lace of Idrija (Slovenia), made since the 17th century with a continuous tape (UNESCO 2018).

leaves.label: Lacemaking in Croatia
leaves.defn: The lace traditions of Croatia — needle lace of Pag, bobbin lace of Lepoglava and Sveta Marija, aloe-thread lace of Hvar (UNESCO 2009).

leaves.label: Venetian Lace
leaves.defn: The needle laces of Venice, 16th-18th century, from reticella and punto in aria to the sculptural gros point and rose point that dominated European fashion before French point d'Alençon: punto in aria collars, gros point de Venise flounces, rose point cravat ends.
leaves.aliases: Point de Venise;punto Venezia;Venetian needle lace;gros point de Venise
leaves.weak: Evidence: Rijksmuseum "Italian, Venice" 108 textile objects (lace flounces); Cooper Hewitt 46 needle laces made in Venice plus 20 punto in aria and about 50 reticella; Met "Italian, Venice / textiles" 518 (2 Timeline wor

leaves.label: Quilting
leaves.defn: The British and American tradition of pieced (patchwork), appliquéd and whole-cloth quilts from the 18th century, named by pattern, region and type: Baltimore album quilts, Log Cabin and Star of Bethlehem quilts, crazy quilts, Harriet Powers's Bible quilts.
leaves.see: H4-46 Amish Quilts;H4-91 Quilts of Gee's Bend;H4-41 Star Quilts;H4-38 Seminole Patchwork;H4-13 Ralli Quilt;H4-42 Tivaevae

leaves.label: Quilts of Gee's Bend
leaves.defn: Quilts made by the women of Gee's Bend, Alabama, since the 19th century: Annie Mae Young's work-clothes quilts, Mary Lee Bendolph's quilts.

leaves.label: Central Asian Ikat
leaves.defn: warp-ikat silks and silk-cotton (adras, atlas) of Bukhara, Samarkand and the Fergana Valley (abrband, 'cloud-binding').

leaves.label: Qalamkar
leaves.defn: block-printed and painted cotton of Isfahan.

leaves.label: Indian Chintz
leaves.defn: Mordant-painted and resist-dyed cottons made on the Coromandel Coast and in Gujarat for export to Europe and Asia, 17th–18th century: palampores, Golconda floorspreads, petticoat panels for the Dutch market.

leaves.label: Kalamkari
leaves.defn: Pen-drawn and block-printed mordant-dyed cotton of Andhra Pradesh, in the Srikalahasti temple-cloth and Machilipatnam block-print styles: temple hangings, Persian-market prayer cloths.

leaves.label: Ajrakh
leaves.defn: Indigo and madder resist block-printed cotton of Sindh and Kutch, printed on both faces.

leaves.label: Bandhani
leaves.defn: Tie-dyed textiles of Gujarat and Rajasthan made by binding thousands of tiny points: gharchola, odhni.

leaves.label: Leheriya
leaves.defn: Diagonally tied and dyed wave-patterned turbans and saris of Rajasthan.

leaves.label: Patola
leaves.defn: Double-ikat silk saris of Patan in Gujarat, traded to Southeast Asia as heirloom cloths.

leaves.label: Rogan Art
leaves.defn: Cloth painted with a thickened castor-oil paste drawn from a stylus, practised at Nirona in Kutch.

leaves.label: Indonesian Batik
leaves.defn: Wax-resist dyed cloth of Java (UNESCO 2009), drawn by canting (tulis) or stamped (cap), in the court styles of Yogyakarta and Surakarta and the coastal pesisir styles of Pekalongan, Lasem and Cirebon: parang rusak kain, batik Belanda, Hokokai batik.

leaves.label: Malaysian Batik
leaves.defn: Block-printed and hand-drawn batik of the east-coast Malay states, Kelantan and Terengganu, with large floral designs.

leaves.label: Indonesian Ikat
leaves.defn: Warp-ikat cotton cloths of the eastern islands and of Sumatra, Borneo and Sulawesi, tied and dyed in morinda and indigo: Sumba hinggi mantles, Toraja sacred cloths, Savu and Flores sarongs.

leaves.label: Geringsing
leaves.defn: The double-ikat cotton cloths of Tenganan Pegeringsingan in Bali, worn for protection in rites.

leaves.label: Tais
leaves.defn: Handwoven textiles of Timor-Leste (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2021), in ikat, supplementary weft and tapestry.

leaves.label: Pua Kumbu
leaves.defn: The ceremonial warp-ikat blankets of the Iban of Sarawak and Kalimantan, woven by women with spirit and ancestor figures.

leaves.label: T'nalak
leaves.defn: Abaca warp-ikat cloth of the T'boli of South Cotabato, its designs dreamed by the weaver.

leaves.label: Telepuk
leaves.defn: Malay cloth stamped with gold leaf from carved wooden blocks for court and wedding dress.

leaves.label: Yūzen
leaves.defn: Paste-resist dyeing with a fine rice-paste line and painted dyes, attributed to Miyazaki Yūzensai of Kyoto (late 17th century): Kyō-yūzen and Kaga-yūzen kimono.

leaves.label: Katazome
leaves.defn: Japanese stencil dyeing with paste applied through cut paper stencils (katagami), and the stencils themselves as collected objects: Ise-katagami, komon small-pattern kimono.

leaves.label: Bingata
leaves.defn: Okinawan stencil- and freehand paste-resist cloth dyed in bright pigments, made for the Ryukyu court and gentry.

leaves.label: Tsutsugaki
leaves.defn: Freehand paste-resist dyeing with a cone (tsutsu), mostly indigo, for festive covers, futon covers and banners (Edo to early 20th century).

leaves.label: Shibori
leaves.defn: Japanese shaped-resist dyeing by binding, stitching, folding and capping cloth: kanoko dots, arimatsu-narumi shibori, the Momoyama tsujigahana robes.

leaves.label: Kasuri
leaves.defn: Japanese ikat: cotton, ramie and silk cloth woven from resist-dyed threads, in regional centres: Kurume, Iyo, Bingo, Miyako-jōfu.

leaves.label: Bai Tie-Dye
leaves.defn: Indigo tie-dyed cotton (zharan) of the Bai of Dali and Zhoucheng in Yunnan.
leaves.weak: encyclopedia entry (national ICH 2006); no Wikipedia article

leaves.label: Geumbak
leaves.defn: Korean gold-leaf stamping of textiles with carved woodblocks, for royal and bridal dress; makers designated geumbakjang.

leaves.label: Bògòlanfini
leaves.defn: Mud-dyed cotton cloth of the Bamana of Mali, strip-woven by men and painted by women with fermented mud on a leaf-dye ground.

leaves.label: Adire
leaves.defn: Indigo resist-dyed cloth of Yoruba women: adire eleko (starch resist), adire oniko (tied), adire alabere (stitched).

leaves.label: Adinkra Cloth
leaves.defn: Asante funerary and prestige cloth stamped with calabash stamps of named adinkra symbols, centred on Ntonso.

leaves.label: Ndop Cloth
leaves.defn: Indigo stitch-resist royal display cloth of the Cameroon Grassfields (Bamileke, Bamum), strip-woven and patterned in white.

leaves.label: Kanga
leaves.defn: Printed cotton cloths of the Swahili coast worn in pairs, with a border, central field and a printed Swahili proverb (jina): kanga, kitenge.

leaves.label: Rebozo
leaves.defn: The Mexican woman's shawl, at its finest in warp-ikat (jaspe) cotton and silk with knotted fringe from Santa María del Río and Tenancingo.

leaves.label: Blaudruck
leaves.defn: Resist block printing and indigo dyeing of linen and cotton, carried on by family dye-works of Central Europe (UNESCO 2018, Austria, Czechia, Germany, Hungary, Slovakia): Burgenland blueprint, Mühlviertel indigo printing.

leaves.label: Staphorster Stipwerk
leaves.defn: Dot printing of Staphorst in Overijssel: coloured patterns stamped with pin-headed stamps on cloth for the village dress (kraplap, caps).

leaves.label: Pavlovo Posad Shawl
leaves.defn: Printed woollen shawls of Pavlovo Posad (Moscow region) since the 1860s, with dense roses and borders, first block-printed then screen-printed.

leaves.label: Kelaghayi
leaves.defn: Silk headscarves of Azerbaijan (Sheki, Basqal) printed by wooden stamps with resist and natural dyes, with buta motifs (UNESCO 2014).

leaves.label: African Wax Prints
leaves.defn: Roller-printed cotton with a batik-like resin resist made in the Netherlands (Vlisco, from 1846), Britain and later West Africa for West and Central African markets, with named and commemorative designs: Vlisco Dutch wax samples, commemorative portrait cloths, Ankara fancy prints.

leaves.label: Kyrgyz and Kazakh Felt
leaves.defn: the mosaic felt carpets (shyrdak), pressed felt (ala-kiyiz, tus kiiz) and embroidered felt of the Kyrgyz and Kazakh (UNESCO 2012).

leaves.label: Palestinian Costume
leaves.defn: the embroidered thobes and headdresses of Palestinian women, distinct by village and region.

leaves.label: Ottoman Court Dress
leaves.defn: the kaftans and garments of the Ottoman sultans and court, kept in the Topkapı Palace treasury.
src: Wikidata Q7109946 (fashion in the Ottoman Empire)

leaves.label: Possum-Skin Cloak
leaves.defn: Cloaks of sewn possum pelts incised on the skin side with clan and Country designs, worn by the Aboriginal peoples of south-eastern Australia and revived since the 1990s: Lake Condah and Maiden's Punt cloaks, revival cloaks.

leaves.label: Gákti
leaves.defn: The dress of the Sámi, a tunic of wool or reindeer skin trimmed with woven bands and coloured cloth whose cut and colours mark region and family: Kautokeino gákti, four-winds hat.

leaves.label: Bunad
leaves.defn: The regional folk costumes of Norway, revived and standardised from local dress since the late 19th century, with embroidered bodices, aprons and silver brooches (sølje): Vest-Telemark bunad, Hardanger bunad.
leaves.see: H7-6 Swedish Folk Costume;H7-7 Tracht;H4-49 Hardanger Embroidery

leaves.label: Swedish Folk Costume
leaves.defn: The parish costumes of Sweden, worn and revived as signs of local and national identity, with embroidered bodices, pockets and headdresses: Dalarna costumes, Leksand and Rättvik dress.

leaves.label: Tracht
leaves.defn: The regional folk dress of the German-speaking Alps and southern Germany, made and worn in local forms with their own headdresses, bodices and embroidery: Bregenzerwald Juppe, Lake Constance Radhaube, Gailtal costume.

leaves.label: Traditional Albanian Clothing
leaves.defn: The regional folk costume of the Albanians, with distinct ensembles by region and community: xhubleta bell-shaped skirt, fustanella, xhamadan vests.

leaves.label: Croatian National Costume
leaves.defn: The regional folk costumes of Croatia, from Slavonian gold-embroidered dress to Dalmatian and Zagorje ensembles.

leaves.label: Macedonian Traditional Clothing
leaves.defn: The regional folk costumes of North Macedonia, with heavily embroidered women's shirts and sleeveless coats.

leaves.label: Erzya Costume
leaves.defn: The traditional dress of the Erzya (Mordvin) people, with embroidered white shirts (panar), pulai hip ornament and headdresses.

leaves.label: Kimono
leaves.defn: The Japanese T-shaped wrapped robe as a dress tradition, from the Momoyama and Edo kosode to the Meiji and modern kimono, with its named garment types and their dyed, woven and embroidered decoration: Edo-period kosode with Ōmi hakkei design, furisode, uchikake wedding robes, katabira summer robes.
leaves.see: H5-18 Yūzen;H5-19 Katazome;H5-22 Shibori;H3 Woven Silks & Figured Textiles

subs.label: Basketry, Barkcloth & Fibre Arts
subs.axis: Axis: tradition. Coiled, twined and plaited basketry, matting and barkcloth (tapa).

leaves.label: Dumbara Mats
leaves.defn: Hana-fibre mats with symbolic motifs woven by the kinnara community of the Dumbara valley in Sri Lanka (UNESCO 2021).

leaves.label: Noken
leaves.defn: Knotted and woven string bags of bark fibre and orchid stem made by women of Papua (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2012).

leaves.label: Daluang
leaves.defn: Javanese beaten-bark paper (dluwang) of paper mulberry, made in Ponorogo and Garut and used for pesantren and wayang beber manuscripts.

leaves.label: Kumihimo
leaves.defn: Japanese braided silk cords made on stands (marudai, takadai), for sword mounts, armour lacing and obijime.

leaves.label: Maedeup
leaves.defn: Korean decorative knotting in silk cord, with tassels for norigae pendants and ritual objects; makers designated maedeupjang.

leaves.label: Chaesang
leaves.defn: Korean boxes of dyed bamboo strips woven in patterns; makers designated chaesangjang.

leaves.label: Wanchojang
leaves.defn: Korean weaving of sedge (wanchoe) into patterned mats (hwamunseok), baskets and cushions, especially of Ganghwa island.

leaves.label: Ugandan Barkcloth
leaves.defn: Barkcloth beaten from the inner bark of the mutuba fig by Baganda craftsmen, terracotta-coloured, for royal and funerary use (UNESCO 2008).

leaves.label: Mbuti Barkcloth
leaves.defn: Barkcloth of the Mbuti of the Ituri forest, prepared by men and painted by women with linear and dotted designs in gardenia and charcoal.

leaves.label: Agaseke
leaves.defn: Coiled lidded baskets of Rwanda with conical lids and geometric patterns, made by women.

leaves.label: Panama Hat
leaves.defn: Hats plaited from toquilla palm straw in Ecuador (Montecristi, Cuenca), inscribed by UNESCO in 2012.

leaves.label: Pomo Basketry
leaves.defn: Coiled and twined baskets of the Pomo of northern California, among them the feathered and beaded gift baskets and the art baskets made for sale by named weavers.

leaves.label: California Indian Basketry
leaves.defn: Twined and coiled basketry of the Native peoples of California and the adjoining Great Basin edge other than the Pomo: Hupa, Karuk and Yurok overlay-twined caps, Yokuts bottleneck baskets, Cahuilla coiled baskets, Washoe degikup.

leaves.label: Spruce-Root Basketry
leaves.defn: Fine twined baskets and hats of split spruce root with false-embroidery grass designs, made by Tlingit and Haida women of the northern Northwest Coast.
leaves.see: H2-11 Chilkat Weaving;H8-15 Unangan Grass Basketry

leaves.label: Unangan Grass Basketry
leaves.defn: Very finely twined wild-rye-grass baskets, wallets and lidded jars of the Unangan (Aleut), above all the Attu baskets with silk false embroidery made for sale after 1867.

leaves.label: Plateau Cornhusk Bags
leaves.defn: Flat twined bags of Indian hemp with cornhusk false embroidery made by Nez Perce, Yakama, Umatilla and other Columbia Plateau women for root storage and exchange.

leaves.label: Plateau Imbricated Basketry
leaves.defn: Coiled cedar-root baskets imbricated with bear grass and cherry bark made by Klickitat, Nlaka'pamux and other Interior Salish weavers: berry baskets, lidded trunks.

leaves.label: Apache Basketry
leaves.defn: Coiled willow and devil's-claw ollas and trays and pitched twined water jars of the Western, Jicarilla and Mescalero Apache, with figures of people and animals.

leaves.label: Pima Basketry
leaves.defn: Coiled willow, cattail and devil's-claw baskets of the Akimel O'odham (Pima) and Tohono O'odham (Papago), the latter also in yucca and bear grass, with fret and squash-blossom designs.

leaves.label: Hopi Basketry
leaves.defn: Basketry of the Hopi mesas: coiled galleta-grass and yucca plaques of Second Mesa and wicker plaques of rabbitbrush of Third Mesa, often with katsina figures.

leaves.label: Rivercane Basketry
leaves.defn: Plaited baskets of split rivercane dyed with walnut and bloodroot, made by Cherokee, Chitimacha, Choctaw and Koasati weavers of the Southeast, including the double-woven baskets.

leaves.label: Wabanaki Basketry
leaves.defn: Woven brown-ash splint and braided sweetgrass baskets of the Wabanaki (Passamaquoddy, Penobscot, Maliseet, Mi'kmaq) of Maine and the Maritimes, from work baskets to fancy 'curly' baskets.

leaves.label: Birchbark Biting
leaves.defn: Designs bitten into thin folded sheets of birchbark by Anishinaabe, Cree and Algonquin women, used as patterns for quill and bead embroidery and as works in themselves.

leaves.label: Tapa Cloth
leaves.defn: Barkcloth beaten from paper-mulberry and other inner bark across the Pacific and painted, stencilled, rubbed or printed with designs: Samoan siapo, Tongan ngatu, Fijian masi, Hawaiian kapa, Niuean hiapo, Omie and Maisin barkcloth.

leaves.label: ʻIe Tōga
leaves.defn: The finely plaited pandanus fine mats of Samoa, and the fine mats of Tonga and Tuvalu, exchanged as the highest valuables at life-crisis ceremonies: ʻie tōga, Tongan kie and taʻovala.

leaves.label: Aboriginal Fibre Art
leaves.defn: The coiled, looped, twined and plaited fibre work of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women and men, from string bags and baskets to contemporary fibre sculpture: dillybags, Arnhem Land pandanus baskets, rainforest bicornual baskets, Tjanpi grass sculpture, ghost-net sculpture.

leaves.label: Lalava
leaves.defn: Decorative coconut-fibre (sennit, magimagi) lashing of Tonga, Fiji and Samoa, binding the beams of houses and the hulls of canoes in red and black geometric patterns, now also made as freestanding works.

leaves.label: Sweetgrass Baskets
leaves.defn: Coiled baskets of sweetgrass, bulrush and pine needle sewn with palmetto by the Gullah Geechee of the South Carolina Lowcountry, a West African coiling tradition: fanner baskets, sewing baskets.

leaves.label: Panier de Mayun
leaves.defn: The willow and bramble baskets of Mayun in the Brière marshes (Loire-Atlantique).

leaves.label: Bastabinne
leaves.defn: Swedish baskets plaited from strips of spruce bast.

leaves.label: Birch-Bark Crafts
leaves.defn: Containers, boxes, footwear and objects of folded, woven, sewn and carved birch bark made across Finland, Karelia and Russia: tuohikontti backpacks, tuesok boxes, woven bast shoes.

leaves.label: Shemogodsk Carving
leaves.defn: Openwork carving of birch bark from the Shemoksa river near Veliky Ustyug since the early 19th century, called 'northern lace', on boxes and tuesoks.

leaves.label: Pärekori
leaves.defn: Finnish baskets plaited from pulled wood shingles (päre).
leaves.aliases: shingle basket;making of shingle baskets from pulled shingles

leaves.label: Clubrush Work of Kruunupyy
leaves.defn: Weaving of clubrush (bulrush) into mats and objects in Kruunupyy (Kronoby), Finland.

leaves.label: Himmeli
leaves.defn: Geometric hanging mobiles of straw tubes threaded together, made at Christmas in Finland and the Baltic (Lithuanian sodai).

leaves.label: Straw Weaving in Belarus
leaves.defn: Belarusian straw weaving of ritual and decorative objects — figures, baskets, spiders (paŭki) and boxes (UNESCO 2025).

leaves.label: Turiisk Straw Plaiting
leaves.defn: Straw plaiting tradition of Turiisk hromada in Volyn Oblast (Ukraine).

leaves.label: Iza Vine Weaving
leaves.defn: Willow-vine basket and furniture weaving of the village of Iza in Zakarpattia (Ukraine).

leaves.label: Shchitky Reed Weaving
leaves.defn: Reed weaving tradition of Shchitky and Pysarivka (Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine).

leaves.label: Zulu Beadwork
leaves.defn: Glass-bead regalia of the Zulu of KwaZulu-Natal in brick stitch, with colour codes by region and age: ucu necklaces, love-letter panels (incwadi), beaded aprons and skirts.

leaves.label: Maasai Beadwork
leaves.defn: Beaded collars, earrings and headdresses of the Maasai of Kenya and Tanzania: flat disc collars, wedding necklaces.

leaves.label: Yoruba Beadwork
leaves.defn: Beaded regalia of Yoruba kings and Ifa priests: beaded crowns with veils (ade), diviners' bags, beaded staffs.

leaves.label: Mexican Featherwork
leaves.defn: Feather mosaic of Mesoamerica and colonial New Spain (amanteca), from Aztec shields and headdresses to Christian feather paintings: Moctezuma's headdress, Mass of Saint Gregory (1539).

leaves.label: Porcupine Quillwork
leaves.defn: Embroidery with flattened dyed porcupine quills on hide and birchbark across the Plains, Subarctic and Northeast: Lakota quilled robes and shirts, Mi'kmaq and Odawa quilled birchbark boxes, Dene quilled bands.

leaves.label: Plains Beadwork
leaves.defn: Glass-bead embroidery of the peoples of the Great Plains and Plateau in lane-stitch and overlay techniques, in tribal styles: Lakota fully beaded vests and cradleboards, Crow (Apsáalooke) horse gear, Blackfeet and Cree floral beadwork.
leaves.see: H9-5 Porcupine Quillwork;H9-7 Haudenosaunee Raised Beadwork

leaves.label: Haudenosaunee Raised Beadwork
leaves.defn: Raised (embossed) glass beadwork on velvet by Mohawk, Tuscarora and Seneca women, above all the 'whimsies' (pincushions, frames, purses) sold at Niagara Falls from the mid-19th century.

leaves.label: Wampum
leaves.defn: Tubular beads of white whelk and purple quahog shell strung and woven into belts and strings by the Haudenosaunee and Algonquian peoples of the Northeast to record treaties and council business: Hiawatha Belt, Two Row Wampum.

leaves.label: Hawaiian Featherwork
leaves.defn: The featherwork of the Hawaiian chiefs: red and yellow honeyeater and ʻiʻiwi feathers knotted to olonā netting as emblems of rank and divinity: ʻahu ʻula cloaks and capes, mahiole helmets, lei hulu, feathered god images.

leaves.label: Kahu Huruhuru
leaves.defn: Māori feather cloaks: muka cloaks finger-woven (whatu) with feathers of kiwi, kererū, kākā and other birds set in the weft, the highest-ranking cloaks of the 19th century onward: kahu kiwi, kahu kererū.
leaves.weak: attest by the redirect Kahu huruhuru to its section

fams.label: Woodwork, Lacquer & Furniture
fams.test: made of wood, or of lacquer and papier-mâché: carved and inlaid woodwork, lacquerware and furniture.
key: 1. Lacquer or lacquered papier-mâché? → I2. 2. Furniture? → I3. 3. Otherwise carved, turned or inlaid wood → I1.
4. A musical instrument? → I4.

leaves.label: Mashrabiya
leaves.defn: screens of turned wooden spindles in latticework, for windows and balconies of Cairo and the Arab world.

leaves.label: Khatam
leaves.defn: Persian micro-marquetry of wood, bone and metal assembled in geometric patterns (Shiraz, Isfahan).
