leaves.defn: Engraved and painted rock art of the Sahara from the Holocene to historical times, by stylistic phases: Bubaline engravings, Round Head paintings, Bovidian (pastoral) paintings, Dabous giraffes.

leaves.label: San Rock Art
leaves.defn: Painted and engraved rock art of the San (Bushmen) of southern Africa, over tens of thousands of years: Drakensberg eland paintings, Twyfelfontein engravings, Tsodilo paintings.

leaves.label: Sasanian Rock Reliefs
leaves.defn: Royal reliefs carved on cliff faces in Fars and western Iran by the Sasanian kings, 3rd–7th century, following Achaemenid precedent: Naqsh-e Rostam investitures, Bishapur triumph of Shapur I, Taq-e Bostan.

leaves.label: Hittite Rock Reliefs
leaves.defn: Reliefs of gods and kings carved on rock in Hittite Anatolia, 14th–13th century BC: Yazılıkaya, Fraktin, Hanyeri, Taşçı.
src: Wikidata Q46053759 (list of Hittites reliefs and inscriptions)

leaves.label: Gobustan Rock Art
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of hunters, dancers, animals and reed boats pecked into the rocks of Gobustan in Azerbaijan from the late Upper Palaeolithic onward (UNESCO 2007).

leaves.label: Rock Art in the Hail Region
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of humans, animals and inscriptions at Jubbah and Shuwaymis in the Ha'il region of Saudi Arabia, spanning some 10,000 years (UNESCO 2015).
leaves.aliases: Hail rock art;Jubbah and Shuwaymis petroglyphs

leaves.label: Cueva de las Manos
leaves.defn: Stencilled hands and hunting scenes of guanacos painted in the Río Pinturas caves of Patagonia from c. 9300 BP (UNESCO 1999).
leaves.see: L1-17 Serra da Capivara Rock Art

leaves.label: Serra da Capivara Rock Art
leaves.defn: The painted rock shelters of Serra da Capivara (Piauí), with Nordeste-tradition hunting, dancing and sexual scenes (UNESCO 1991): Pedra Furada, Toca do Boqueirão.
leaves.see: L1-16 Cueva de las Manos;L1-19 Chiribiquete Rock Paintings
src: Wikidata Q267394 (Serra da Capivara National Park)

leaves.label: Toro Muerto Petroglyphs
leaves.defn: Thousands of petroglyphs pecked on volcanic boulders at Toro Muerto (Arequipa) with dancers, camelids and birds, with related Andean sites: Toro Muerto, Toquepala Caves, Miculla.

leaves.label: Chiribiquete Rock Paintings
leaves.defn: Red-ochre paintings of jaguars, hunters and dancers on the tepuis of Chiribiquete in the Colombian Amazon (UNESCO 2018).
leaves.see: L1-17 Serra da Capivara Rock Art

leaves.label: Pecos River Style
leaves.defn: Large polychrome pictographs of shamanic figures painted in the rock shelters of the Lower Pecos Canyonlands of Texas and Coahuila (c. 2700 BCE onward): White Shaman Shelter, Fate Bell Shelter, Panther Cave.

leaves.label: Barrier Canyon Style
leaves.defn: Archaic pictographs of tall tapering ghost-like figures on the Colorado Plateau of Utah: Great Gallery, Horseshoe Canyon, Sego Canyon.

leaves.label: Chumash Rock Painting
leaves.defn: Polychrome pictographs of circles, wheels and beings painted in caves of the Chumash territory of southern California (c. 1000–1800): Painted Cave, Painted Rock (Carrizo Plain), Burro Flats.

leaves.label: Coso Rock Art
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of bighorn sheep, hunters and patterned-body figures in the Coso Range of the Mojave Desert, the largest concentration in North America.

leaves.label: Writing-on-Stone Rock Art
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs and pictographs of the Plains, incised in the sandstone of the Milk River valley, Alberta, including biographic warrior scenes (Áísínai'pi, UNESCO 2019).

leaves.label: Rock Paintings of the Sierra de San Francisco
leaves.defn: The Great Murals of Baja California: life-size red and black human and animal figures painted in the rock shelters of the Sierra de San Francisco and Sierra de Guadalupe (UNESCO 1993).

leaves.label: Arnhem Land Rock Art
leaves.defn: The painted rock shelters of the western Arnhem Land plateau and Kakadu, from Dynamic figures to the recent x-ray and contact paintings: Ubirr, Burrungkuy (Nourlangie), Nanguluwur, Injalak Hill.

leaves.label: Gwion Gwion Rock Paintings
leaves.defn: The fine-line figure paintings of the north-west Kimberley, slender tasselled human figures of great age.

leaves.label: Murujuga Rock Art
leaves.defn: The petroglyphs of the Burrup Peninsula and Dampier Archipelago (Murujuga), over a million engravings made across tens of thousands of years.

leaves.label: Sydney Rock Engravings
leaves.defn: The outline engravings on Hawkesbury sandstone in the Sydney basin: animals, ancestral beings and people: Ku-ring-gai Chase sites.

leaves.label: Quinkan Rock Art
leaves.defn: The painted shelters around Laura on Cape York with the Quinkan spirit figures.

leaves.label: Panaramitee Style
leaves.defn: The widespread Australian engraving style of tracks, circles and dots ('track and circle'), among the oldest rock art of the continent: Ewaninga, Panaramitee.

leaves.label: Māori Rock Art
leaves.defn: The charcoal and red-ochre drawings in limestone shelters of South Canterbury and North Otago: Takiroa, Awamoko.
leaves.weak: Māori rock art redirects to Māori culture#Painting

leaves.label: Franco-Cantabrian Cave Art
leaves.defn: Upper Palaeolithic painted and engraved cave art of south-western France and northern Spain, c. 40,000–11,000 BP: Chauvet, Lascaux, Altamira, Font-de-Gaume.

leaves.label: Côa Valley and Siega Verde Rock Art
leaves.defn: Open-air Upper Palaeolithic engravings of animals on schist outcrops in the Côa valley (Portugal) and at Siega Verde (Spain), c. 25,000–10,000 BP: Canada do Inferno, Penascosa, Ribeira de Piscos.
src: Wikidata Q552106 (Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley)

leaves.label: Levantine Rock Art
leaves.defn: Post-Palaeolithic naturalistic rock painting of eastern Spain, c. 8000–3500 BC, with hunting, warfare and gathering scenes in shelters: Cova dels Cavalls, Roca dels Moros (Cogul), Valltorta.
leaves.aliases: Rock Art of the Mediterranean Basin on the Iberian Peninsula;Levantine art

leaves.label: Iberian Schematic Art
leaves.defn: Schematic rock painting and engraving of the Iberian peninsula, c. 5000–1000 BC, associated with the first farming and metal-using cultures: anthropomorphs and idols, Galician petroglyphs of Os Mouchos and Portela da Laxe.

leaves.label: Cup and Ring Marks
leaves.defn: Neolithic and Bronze Age carvings of cups and concentric rings on outcrops and standing stones of Atlantic Europe, above all Britain and Ireland: Cochno Stone, Achnabreck, Roughting Linn.

leaves.label: Rock Carvings in Tanum
leaves.defn: Bronze Age rock carvings of Bohuslän in western Sweden, c. 1700–500 BC, with ships, warriors, ploughing scenes and weddings: Vitlycke panel, Aspeberget, Fossum.

leaves.label: Rock Carvings at Alta
leaves.defn: Rock carvings of hunter-fisher communities at Alta in Finnmark, c. 5000 BC – AD 0, with reindeer, elk, boats and bear hunts: Hjemmeluft, Bergbukten, Amtmannsnes.

leaves.label: Petroglyphs of Lake Onega and the White Sea
leaves.defn: Neolithic petroglyphs of Russian Karelia, c. 4000–2000 BC, on the shores of Lake Onega (swans, solar signs, the 'demon') and at Zalavruga on the White Sea (hunting and boat scenes).
src: Wikidata Q64808630 (Petroglyphs of Lake Onega and the White Sea)

leaves.label: Ural Pictograms
leaves.defn: Red-ochre rock paintings (pisanitsy) on river cliffs of the Urals, Neolithic to Iron Age, with animals, figures and signs: Ignatievskaya Cave, Tagil pisanitsa.

leaves.label: Rock Drawings in Valcamonica
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of the Camunni in the Val Camonica (Lombardy), from the Epipalaeolithic to the Iron Age and beyond: Bedolina Map, Camunian rose, Naquane.

leaves.label: Umayyad Wall Painting
leaves.defn: the figural wall paintings of the Umayyad desert palaces, above all the bath of Qusayr 'Amra (8th century).

leaves.label: Persian Wall Painting
leaves.defn: the palace murals of Safavid and Qajar Iran (Chehel Sotoun, Ali Qapu, Hasht Behesht).

leaves.label: Al-Qatt Al-Asiri
leaves.defn: the geometric wall decoration painted by women inside the houses of the Asir region of Saudi Arabia (UNESCO 2017).

leaves.label: Ajanta Paintings
leaves.defn: Buddhist cave murals of Ajanta (2nd century BCE–5th century CE), the classical model for Indian wall painting: Padmapani, Mahajanaka Jataka.

leaves.label: Sigiriya Frescoes
leaves.defn: The 5th-century paintings of women on the rock face of Kashyapa's palace at Sigiriya.

leaves.label: Kerala Mural Painting
leaves.defn: Temple and palace murals of Kerala (9th–19th century) in five colours: Mattancherry Palace Ramayana, Padmanabhapuram murals.

leaves.label: Kandyan Period Painting
leaves.defn: Buddhist temple murals of the Kandyan kingdom (1592–1815) in red and yellow narrative registers: Dambulla cave paintings, Degaldoruwa jatakas.

leaves.label: Shekhawati Frescoes
leaves.defn: Painted havelis, temples and forts of Shekhawati in Rajasthan, 18th–20th century, mixing Rajput, colonial and popular imagery.

leaves.label: Pithora Painting
leaves.defn: Ritual wall paintings of horses and deities by the Rathwa and Bhil of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.

leaves.label: Saura Painting
leaves.defn: Ritual wall paintings (ittal) of the Sora of Odisha dedicated to Idital.

leaves.label: Sohrai and Khovar Painting
leaves.defn: Harvest (sohrai) and marriage-chamber (khovar) wall paintings of Hazaribagh, Jharkhand.

leaves.label: Rangoli
leaves.defn: Ritual floor drawing in powder and rice paste across South Asia: kolam, alpana, kalamezhuthu.

leaves.label: Tibetan Buddhist Wall Paintings
leaves.defn: The secco murals of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries and temples across the Himalaya, from the Kashmiri-style programmes of Tabo and Alchi to Shalu, the Gyantse Kumbum and Guge: Alchi Sumtsek, Tabo assembly hall, Shalu murals.

leaves.label: Dunhuang Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist cave temples of the Mogao Caves at Dunhuang (4th–14th century): Cave 217 Pure Land, Jataka narratives, donor portraits.

leaves.label: Kizil Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist caves of the kingdom of Kucha (Kizil, Kumtura and neighbouring sites), 4th–8th century, in rhomboid narrative grids and lapis blue: Cave of the Sixteen Sword-Bearers, Buddha in Nirvana.

leaves.label: Bezeklik Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Uyghur Buddhist caves of Bezeklik and the Turfan oasis (Qocho) under the Uyghur kingdom (9th–13th century): pranidhi scenes, Uyghur donor princes.
leaves.aliases: Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves murals;Uyghur Buddhist wall painting

leaves.label: Sogdian Wall Painting
leaves.defn: The secular and religious murals of Sogdian houses, temples and palaces (5th–8th century) at Panjikent, Afrasiyab and Varakhsha: Rustam cycle, Hall of the Ambassadors, Red Hall of Varakhsha.

leaves.label: Bagan Murals
leaves.defn: The tempera wall paintings of the temples of Bagan (11th–13th century) and their Inwa and Konbaung successors: Abeyadana, Lokahteikpan Jatakas, Ananda temple.

leaves.label: Thai Mural Painting
leaves.defn: Tempera wall paintings of Thai Buddhist ordination halls and viharas, late Ayutthaya to early Rattanakosin and Lanna: Wat Phra Kaew Ramakien, Wat Pho, Wat Phumin, Wat Chong Nonsi.

leaves.label: Yongle Palace Murals
leaves.defn: The Daoist murals of the Yongle Palace in Shanxi (14th century), with the procession of deities in the Hall of Three Purities, and the Buddhist murals of the Fahai Temple near Beijing (1443).

leaves.label: Takamatsuzuka Tomb Murals
leaves.defn: Painted plaster walls of the late 7th-century tombs of Asuka (Takamatsuzuka and Kitora), with court ladies, the Four Directional Animals and star charts.

leaves.label: Goguryeo Tomb Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Goguryeo tombs near Pyongyang and Ji'an (4th–7th century): hunting scenes, dancers and the Four Guardians (UNESCO 2004).

leaves.label: Dancheong
leaves.defn: Korean polychrome painting of wooden buildings, temples and palaces in blue, red, yellow, white and black patterns; masters designated dancheongjang.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Church Painting
leaves.defn: Wall painting of Ethiopian churches, on plaster and on canvas glued to walls: Debre Berhan Selassie ceiling of winged faces, Lake Tana monastery murals, Lalibela paintings.

leaves.label: Litema
leaves.defn: Incised and painted mud-wall decoration of Basotho homesteads in Lesotho and the Free State, renewed by women.

leaves.label: Ndebele House Painting
leaves.defn: Geometric mural painting of the Southern Ndebele of South Africa on homestead walls, by women (Esther Mahlangu).

leaves.label: Imigongo
leaves.defn: Rwandan relief panels of cow dung in black, white and red spirals and zigzags, from house walls to boards.

leaves.label: Egyptian Tomb Painting
leaves.defn: Wall painting in the tombs and temples of pharaonic Egypt, in tempera on plaster: Meidum Geese, Tomb of Nebamun, Tomb of Nefertari, Theban nobles' tombs.

leaves.label: Minoan Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Fresco painting of Bronze Age Crete and the Minoanised Aegean, c. 1700–1450 BC: Bull-Leaping Fresco from Knossos, Akrotiri Spring Fresco, Fisherman of Thera.
leaves.aliases: Minoan frescoes;Aegean wall painting;Wall Paintings of Thera

leaves.label: Etruscan Tomb Painting
leaves.defn: Painted chamber tombs of Etruria, 7th–2nd century BC, chiefly at Tarquinia and Cerveteri: Tomb of the Leopards, Tomb of the Triclinium, François Tomb at Vulci.

leaves.label: Ancient Greek Painting
leaves.defn: Surviving Greek wall painting, mostly from tombs of the 5th–3rd century BC in Macedonia, Thrace and Magna Graecia: Tomb of Philip II at Vergina, Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak, Tomb of the Diver at Paestum.
leaves.weak: Ancient Greek painting redirects to Ancient Greek art

leaves.label: Pompeian Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Roman wall painting of the Vesuvian cities and Rome, classed by August Mau in four Pompeian Styles, 2nd century BC – AD 79: Villa of the Mysteries, Villa of Poppaea at Oplontis, House of the Vettii.

leaves.label: Catacomb Painting
leaves.defn: Early Christian and Jewish funerary and devotional wall painting of the 2nd–5th century, above all in the catacombs of Rome and at Dura-Europos: Catacomb of Priscilla, Via Latina catacomb, Dura-Europos synagogue.

leaves.label: Byzantine Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Fresco programmes of Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches, 6th–15th century: Cappadocian rock-cut churches, painted churches of Troödos, Panselinos at the Protaton, Mystras.

leaves.label: Faras Wall Paintings
leaves.defn: Wall paintings of the cathedral of Faras in the Nubian kingdom of Makuria, 8th–14th century, removed in 1961–64 to Warsaw and Khartoum: Bishop Petros with St Peter, Saint Anne, Nativity.
src: Wikidata Q24323243 (Faras Gallery of the National Museum in Warsaw)

leaves.label: Maya Mural Painting
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Maya from the Preclassic to the Postclassic: San Bartolo murals, Bonampak Room 2 battle, Calakmul market murals.

leaves.label: Teotihuacan Mural Painting
leaves.defn: The fresco painting of the apartment compounds of Teotihuacan (c. 200–650 CE): Tepantitla Great Goddess, Tetitla, Atetelco.

leaves.label: Cacaxtla Murals
leaves.defn: The Epiclassic murals of Cacaxtla (Tlaxcala, c. 650–900 CE), mixing Maya and central Mexican styles: Battle Mural, Bird Man.
leaves.see: L2-36 Maya Mural Painting;L2-37 Teotihuacan Mural Painting

leaves.label: Moche Murals
leaves.defn: Painted and modelled mud-plaster friezes of Moche temples: Huaca de la Luna Ai Apaec friezes, El Brujo.

leaves.label: Mexican Muralism
leaves.defn: The public mural movement of post-revolutionary Mexico (1920s–1970s) led by Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros: Rivera's National Palace murals, Orozco's Hospicio Cabañas, Siqueiros' Polyforum.
leaves.see: L2-41 Chilean Muralism;L2-42 Murals of Revolutionary Nicaragua

leaves.label: Chilean Muralism
leaves.defn: Chilean public mural painting from the 1940s, from Siqueiros' Chillán murals to the brigade painting of the Brigada Ramona Parra.

leaves.label: Murals of Revolutionary Nicaragua
leaves.defn: Public murals painted in Sandinista Nicaragua (1979–1990) by Nicaraguan and international brigades.

leaves.label: Romanesque Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Fresco programmes of Romanesque churches, c. 1000–1200: Sant Climent de Taüll, Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, San Isidoro, León, Sant'Angelo in Formis.
leaves.weak: Romanesque wall painting redirects to Romanesque art#Wall painting; routed in_situ row 'mural - United States (medieval)' (Spanish Romanesque frescoes in US museums) attaches here

leaves.label: Gothic Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Wall painting in Gothic churches and palaces, 13th–15th century, north of the Alps and in the Adriatic: Albi Cathedral, Saint-Sernin, Beram and Hrastovlje Danse macabre, Albertus Pictor's Swedish churches.

leaves.label: Painted Churches of Northern Moldavia
leaves.defn: The 15th–16th-century churches of Bukovina painted inside and out with Byzantine-derived cycles under Stephen the Great and Petru Rareș: Voroneț Last Judgement, Humor, Sucevița, Moldovița.
leaves.weak: enwiki Painted churches of northern Moldavia redirects to Churches of Moldavia; UNESCO 598

leaves.label: Scottish Renaissance Painted Ceilings
leaves.defn: Tempera-painted timber ceilings of Scottish houses and castles, c. 1550–1650, with emblems, grotesques and heraldry: Prestongrange, Aberdour Castle, Culross Palace.

leaves.label: Murals in Northern Ireland
leaves.defn: Loyalist and republican political murals painted on gable walls in Northern Ireland since the early 20th century and above all from the 1970s: Falls Road murals, Bogside Artists, King Billy murals.

leaves.label: Samchyky Painting
leaves.defn: The decorative painting of the walls and interiors of houses in Samchyky village (Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine), with unique floral patterns.

leaves.label: Illusionistic Ceiling Painting
leaves.defn: Ceiling and vault painting in fresco that opens the architecture to a painted sky by foreshortening (di sotto in sù) and painted architecture (quadratura), from Mantegna to the Baroque and Rococo: Mantegna's Camera degli Sposi oculus, Pietro da Cortona's Barberini ceiling, Pozzo's Sant'Ignazio, Tiepolo's Würzburg staircase.
leaves.aliases: quadratura;di sotto in sù;sotto in su;Baroque ceiling painting
leaves.see: L2-50 Italian Renaissance Fresco;A5-25 Baroque Painting;A5-29 Rococo;B2-9-44 Gothic Wall Painting
leaves.weak: 'Quadratura' and 'Di sotto in sù' redirect to sections of this article; specialist quadraturisti move here, history painters who also painted ceilings stay in their A5 leaves (P9)

leaves.label: Italian Renaissance Fresco
leaves.defn: The fresco cycles painted on the walls and vaults of Italian chapels, churches and palaces from Giotto to the High Renaissance, studied where they stand: Arena (Scrovegni) Chapel, Brancacci Chapel, Sistine Chapel ceiling, Raphael Rooms.
leaves.see: A5-20 Italian Renaissance Painting;A5-16 Gothic Painting;B2-9-44 Gothic Wall Painting;L2-49 Illusionistic Ceiling Painting
leaves.weak: ATTESTATION WEAK: no Wikipedia or Wikidata title for the cycle tradition; attested only through Wikipedia 'Fresco' (Italian Renaissance section) and the cycle articles (Scrovegni Chapel, Sistine Chapel ceiling); resolves

leaves.label: Street Art
leaves.defn: Unsanctioned and commissioned art in public space from the 1970s: graffiti writing, stencil, paste-up and mural: Banksy's Girl with Balloon, Os Gêmeos's murals, JR's Women Are Heroes.

leaves.label: Umayyad Mosaics
leaves.defn: the glass wall mosaics of the Dome of the Rock and the Great Mosque of Damascus (7th–8th century), made by Byzantine-trained craftsmen.

leaves.label: Zellige
leaves.defn: geometric mosaic of hand-cut glazed tiles set in plaster, the wall and floor revetment of Morocco and al-Andalus.

leaves.label: Moʿaraq (Cut-Tile Mosaic)
leaves.defn: the tile revetment of Iranian and Central Asian architecture: cut-tile mosaic (mo'arraq) of the Timurid and Safavid periods, haft-rangi (seven-colour) tiles and banna'i brick-and-tile.
leaves.see: E2-2 Kashan Lustreware; L3-4 Kashi Kari.

leaves.label: Kashi Kari
leaves.defn: the tile-mosaic revetment of Mughal and Punjabi buildings (Lahore, Multan, Thatta).

leaves.label: Aina-kari
leaves.defn: mirror mosaic: cut mirror glass set in plaster on walls and ceilings of Iranian palaces and shrines.

leaves.label: Hellenistic Mosaics
leaves.defn: Greek floor mosaics from the 5th to the 1st century BC, from pebble mosaics to tessellated opus vermiculatum: Pella stag hunt, Alexander Mosaic, Sosos's unswept floor.
leaves.weak: pool QID Q3827470; Hellenistic mosaics redirects to Hellenistic art

leaves.label: Roman Mosaics
leaves.defn: Floor and wall mosaics of the Roman world, 1st century BC – 5th century AD, with strong regional schools in North Africa, Antioch and Sicily: Nile mosaic of Palestrina, Antioch mosaics, Villa Romana del Casale, Bardo mosaics.

leaves.label: Byzantine Mosaics
leaves.defn: Glass and stone wall mosaics of Byzantine churches and of the workshops they trained, 5th–14th century: San Vitale, Ravenna, Hagia Sophia, Daphni and Hosios Loukas, Monreale, San Marco.

leaves.label: Azulejo
leaves.defn: Painted tin-glazed tile panels covering walls of churches, palaces and streets in Portugal, Spain and Brazil from the 16th century: Palace of the Marquises of Fronteira, São Bento station, Valencian ceramic retables.

leaves.label: Trencadís
leaves.defn: Mosaic of broken tile and crockery shards laid on curved surfaces, the cladding of Catalan Modernisme (Gaudí, Jujol): Park Güell, Casa Batlló, Hospital de Sant Pau.

leaves.label: Portuguese Pavement
leaves.defn: Patterned pavement of black basalt and white limestone setts laid by hand in Portugal and its former colonies since the 19th century: Rossio waves, Copacabana promenade.

leaves.label: Soviet Mosaics
leaves.defn: Monumental mosaics on public buildings, metro stations and housing of the Soviet Union and its republics, 1920s–1991, a state programme of monumental art: Kyiv and Donetsk school mosaics, Yerevan facade mosaics.
leaves.weak: no English Wikipedia article; modern and tradition-led (anonymous collective commissions)

leaves.label: Steppe Geoglyphs
leaves.defn: The earthen and stone ground figures of the Turgai Trough in northern Kazakhstan (Neolithic–Iron Age), at least 260 squares, rings and crosses: Ushtogay Square, Turgay triradial swastika.

leaves.label: Gozan no Okuribi
leaves.defn: The five bonfire characters and figures (Daimonji, Myōhō, the boat and the torii) lit on the hills around Kyoto on 16 August, laid out as fixed hillside figures.

leaves.label: Nazca Lines
leaves.defn: Geoglyphs scraped into the desert of the Nazca and Palpa pampas (c. 500 BCE–500 CE), with straight lines and animal figures (UNESCO 1994): Hummingbird, Monkey, Condor, Palpa figures.

leaves.label: Pintados Geoglyphs
leaves.defn: Hillside geoglyphs of the Atacama made by removing or piling stones (c. 600–1500 CE): Cerro Pintados panels, Atacama Giant, Chug-Chug.

leaves.label: Acre Geoglyphs
leaves.defn: Geometric ditched enclosures of the south-western Amazon (Acre, Brazil), c. 0–1300 CE.

leaves.label: Effigy Mounds
leaves.defn: Earthen mounds raised in the shapes of animals and serpents in the Eastern Woodlands: Serpent Mound, the bear and bird mounds of Effigy Mounds National Monument.

leaves.label: Blythe Intaglios
leaves.defn: Giant human and animal figures scraped into the desert pavement near Blythe on the lower Colorado River.

leaves.label: Hill Figures
leaves.defn: Figures cut into hillsides to expose the chalk or limestone beneath, mainly in southern England, from the Bronze Age (Uffington) to the 18th–19th-century white horses: Uffington White Horse, Cerne Abbas Giant, Long Man of Wilmington.

leaves.label: Deq
leaves.defn: the facial and hand tattooing of Kurdish, Arab and Amazigh women.

leaves.label: Godna
leaves.defn: Tattooing of the tribal communities of central and eastern India (Baiga, Gond, Oraon), also transferred to painting on paper.

leaves.label: Mehndi
leaves.defn: Henna body painting of South Asia for weddings and festivals.

leaves.label: Sak Yant
leaves.defn: Thai, Khmer, Lao and Burmese protective yantra tattooing of sacred diagrams and Khom script, applied by monks and ajarn with a steel rod.

leaves.label: Mentawai Tattooing
leaves.defn: The full-body line tattooing (titi) of the Mentawai of Siberut, west of Sumatra.

leaves.label: Batok
leaves.defn: The traditional tattooing of the Philippines, from the Visayan pintados to the Kalinga and Bontoc warrior tattoos.

leaves.label: Irezumi
leaves.defn: Japanese tattooing, above all the Edo-period full-body designs inspired by ukiyo-e heroes, with the Okinawan women's hand tattoos (hajichi) and Ainu lip tattoos as kinds.

leaves.label: African Scarification
leaves.defn: Cicatrisation and keloid scarification as body art across Africa, with named regional marks: Yoruba facial marks (ila), Nuba and Dinka marks.

leaves.label: Kakiniit
leaves.defn: Inuit women's facial and body tattooing, sewn or pricked with soot-blackened sinew, revived in Nunavut and Greenland since the 2000s.

leaves.label: Tā Moko
leaves.defn: Māori tattooing, chiselled (uhi) into the skin in curvilinear designs that mark descent and rank: moko on men's faces, moko kauae for women.

leaves.label: Polynesian Tattooing
leaves.defn: The tattoo traditions of Polynesia worked with toothed combs and a mallet: Samoan peʻa and malu, Marquesan full-body tattoo, Tahitian tatau, Fijian veiqia.
leaves.weak: Peʻa attests the Samoan core; Polynesian tattoo redirects to History of tattooing#Polynesia

leaves.label: Sailor Tattoos
leaves.defn: The Western tattoo tradition of sailors and its prison and street derivatives, which grew into the American traditional style of bold outlines and limited colour (Sailor Jerry): swallows, anchors, pin-ups.

subs.label: Floor & Sand Painting
subs.axis: Axis: tradition. Ephemeral designs drawn on the floor or ground in powder, sand or rice paste (rangoli, kolam, Navajo dry painting).

leaves.label: Sona
leaves.defn: Sand drawings (lusona, pl. sona) of the Chokwe and neighbouring peoples of eastern Angola: continuous lines around a grid of dots, illustrating stories.

leaves.label: Navajo Sandpainting
leaves.defn: Dry paintings of coloured sands, pollen and charcoal made by Diné medicine men for healing chants and erased after use, and their permanent versions glued on board for sale since the 1930s.

leaves.label: Corpus Christi Flower Carpets
leaves.defn: Carpets of flowers laid on the streets of Polish villages (Spycimierz and others) for the Corpus Christi processions (UNESCO 2021).
leaves.aliases: Flower carpets tradition for Corpus Christi processions

fams.label: New Media, Installation & Performance
fams.test: time-based, installed or performed work: video, sound, installation, performance, digital and net art. Photographers and artists are kinds of their school or movement.

subs.label: Installation, Conceptual & Performance Art
subs.axis: Axis: movement (conceptual art, Fluxus, Arte Povera, land art, performance).

leaves.label: Installation Art
leaves.defn: Art that makes or transforms a space to be entered or experienced, from the 1960s: Kabakov's The Man Who Flew into Space, Kusama's Infinity Mirror Rooms.

leaves.label: Conceptual Art
leaves.defn: Art since the mid-1960s in which the idea is the work: Kosuth's One and Three Chairs, Sol LeWitt's Wall Drawings, On Kawara's Date Paintings.

leaves.label: Fluxus
leaves.defn: The international intermedia network of the 1960s around George Maciunas: event scores, actions and multiples: Yoko Ono's Cut Piece, Fluxkits.
leaves.see: T194 Conceptual Art;T196 Mail Art;T200 Performance Art

leaves.label: Mail Art
leaves.defn: Art sent and exchanged through the postal system from the 1960s (Ray Johnson's New York Correspondence School): Johnson's moticos, artistamps.

leaves.label: Arte Povera
leaves.defn: The Italian movement (1967) of "poor" materials and process: Pistoletto's Venus of the Rags, Merz's igloos, Kounellis's live horses.

leaves.label: Land Art
leaves.defn: Art made in and of the landscape from the late 1960s: Smithson's Spiral Jetty, De Maria's Lightning Field, Goldsworthy's works.

leaves.label: Viennese Actionism
leaves.defn: The radical Austrian performance movement of the 1960s: Nitsch's Orgien Mysterien Theater, Schwarzkogler's actions.

leaves.label: Performance Art
leaves.defn: Art made by the artist's live action before an audience, from the 1960s: Abramović's Rhythm 0, Beuys's I Like America and America Likes Me.

subs.label: Video & New Media Art
subs.axis: Axis: medium-led movement (video art, new media and net art).

leaves.label: Generative Art
leaves.defn: Art made wholly or partly by an autonomous system — an algorithm, program or machine — from the plotter drawings of the 1960s computer-art pioneers to code-based generative work: Nees's Schotter, Molnár's (Dés)Ordres, Mohr's P-197, Casey Reas's Process works.
leaves.see: M2-2 New Media Art;M2-3 AI Art;A5-87 Concrete Art

leaves.label: Internet Art
leaves.defn: Art made for and distributed through the Internet from the mid-1990s (net.art), its browser, e-mail and website works and the post-internet generation: Lialina's My Boyfriend Came Back from the War, JODI's wwwwwwwww.jodi.org, Ćosić's ASCII History of Moving Images.
leaves.aliases: net art;net.art;web art;NFT art;crypto art;pixel art
leaves.see: M2-2 New Media Art;M1-4 Mail Art
leaves.weak: 'Net art' redirects to Internet art; remove 'Internet art' from the M2-2 aliases; post-internet is a kind

leaves.label: AI Art
leaves.defn: Art made with machine-learning and other AI systems, from Harold Cohen's AARON (1973) to GAN and diffusion-model works: Cohen's AARON drawings, Klingemann's Memories of Passersby I, Anadol's Unsupervised, Ridler's Mosaic Virus.
leaves.see: M2-1 Generative Art;M2-2 New Media Art
leaves.weak: 'Artificial intelligence art' redirects to AI art; remove 'AI art' from the M2-2 aliases

leaves.label: Video Art
leaves.defn: Art made with video from the mid-1960s: Nam June Paik's TV Buddha, Bill Viola's The Crossing, Joan Jonas's Vertical Roll.

leaves.label: New Media Art
leaves.defn: Art made with digital, networked and computational technologies: Cory Arcangel's Super Mario Clouds, Rafael Lozano-Hemmer's Pulse Room.

familyKey: 1. Is it a building or a designed built whole (a garden, a complex), placed by its style? → K Architecture. Ornament carved, painted or tiled on a building and studied where it stands is asked next (2); loose architectural fragments in a museum go by their material (D, E, I).
2. Is it made on or into a fixed surface and studied where it stands: rock art, wall painting, in-situ mosaic and tile revetment, a geoglyph, or art on the living body? → L Art in Place.
3. Is it a photograph or made with a camera? → J Photography. Is it time-based, installed or performed (video, installation, performance, digital)? → M New Media, Installation & Performance.

4. Is the written or decorated book the work: calligraphy, illumination (ornament), binding, paper decoration, or a manuscript tradition studied as the book? → C Book Arts & Calligraphy. Pictures in a manuscript belong to a painting tradition and go on to 6 (precedence P1).
5. Is it a drawing made as an end in itself or as a design, or a print pulled from a matrix? → B Drawings & Prints.
6. Is it a picture made with paint or ink on a movable flat support (paper, vellum, panel, canvas, cloth, silk)? → A Painting.

7. Is it carved, modelled or cast as an image or as carving for its own sake: statues, reliefs, carved stucco, ivory, bone, jade, rock crystal and hardstone, masks and puppets? → D Sculpture & Carving. A vessel carved from rock crystal or jade stays here; a cast metal vessel is G.

8. Otherwise place it by its material: fired clay → E Ceramics; glass → F Glass; metal (vessels, instruments, arms, jewellery) → G Metalwork, Arms & Jewellery; fibre (carpets, woven, embroidered, dyed and felted textiles, dress) → H Textiles, Carpets & Dress; wood, lacquer and papier-mâché, furniture → I Woodwork, Lacquer & Furniture.
Inside a family, run the family's own key (on each family card), then choose the leaf whose definition fits; a leaf's kinds are its named sub-schools, centres, workshops, sub-types and makers.
precedence: Pictures painted in a manuscript or for an album go to A1 Manuscript & Album Painting when the tradition is studied as painting (Persian, Ottoman, Mughal, Deccan, Arab); the book as an object — its script, illumination ornament and binding — goes to C. An illustrated manuscript is placed by what makes it notable: its pictures → A1, its script or illumination → C.

A tile is placed by its ware in E Ceramics (Iznik tiles under Iznik Pottery; Kashan lustre tiles under Kashan Lustreware). A revetment assembled on site as a named technique — cut-tile mosaic, zellige, kashi kari, mirror mosaic — is L3, because the work is the wall.

Carved stucco, stone and wood that survive as museum fragments go to their material family (D1 carving, I1 woodwork). The building that carries them is K; a named in-situ programme of painting or mosaic is L.
Lustre is a surface technique, not a sub-family: a lustreware is placed by its body (earthenware lustre → E1; fritware lustre → E2) and then by its named ware.
A vessel carved from rock crystal, jade or other hardstone is D3 (the carving is the work), not glass or metalwork, even when mounted in metal.

A dynasty, reign, empire or period (Mamluk, Safavid, Qajar, Akbar's reign) is a period tag, never a node. The node is the tradition the work belongs to in its medium: Mamluk enamelled glass (F3), Mamluk metalwork (G1), Mamluk carpets (H1), Mamluk architecture (K).

A city, production centre, country or culture label (Iznik, Kashan, Tabriz, 'Iranian', 'Syrian') is a place tag. A centre becomes a kind under a leaf only when the field names a distinct school or ware after it (Herat school, Kashan lustreware, Ushak carpets).

A revival built outside the original tradition (Moorish Revival synagogues, Neo-Mamluk, the First National Architectural Movement) is a leaf in K Historicist & National Revivals, never a kind of the style it revives.

A named maker is a kind under the leaf of the tradition they worked in, linked to their school or atelier where one is recorded. A maker active in two traditions is placed where most of their recorded work sits, with a see-also to the other (Mir Sayyid Ali and Abd al-Samad: Persian schooling, Mughal atelier → Mughal Painting).

A folk or vernacular craft that the field names on its own (suzani, kilim, Berber jewellery) is its own leaf in the medium family; a court or urban tradition of the same medium is a separate leaf. Garment types (abaya, shemagh, ghutra) are not art traditions: they belong to the Possession Taxonomy.

In artist-led cells a painter, sculptor or printmaker goes to the movement or school their work is attested in; with no attested movement, to the period-style leaf of their medium (Baroque Painting, Romantic Painting ...), never to a country.

A culture is never a leaf by itself: its leaves are its traditions in each medium (Yoruba sculpture, Yoruba beadwork), so one culture can hold several leaves across families. A culture known for one medium only gets one leaf there.

An archaeological culture known for one dominant medium (Nok terracottas, Jōmon pottery) is a leaf in that medium; its other finds are kinds or see-also, not separate leaves, unless the field names them.

A gathered culture row (Ewe, Mende, Asante) is a kind of the tradition that holds most of its objects when one medium tradition of that people has a leaf; otherwise it is a place tag (P12). A named carving school, provincial painting school or centre (Te Arawa, Murshidabad, Swat) is a kind of its leaf.

With no attested movement, an artist goes to the period-style leaf of their medium by birth year: academic and salon art for those trained in the academies before the modern movements (born before c. 1850), Modern Art (born c. 1850–1944), Contemporary Art (born 1945 or later). The artist's own medium decides, not the medium recorded in the source when it is plainly wrong (a photographer recorded as a painter is a photographer).
Period leaves for architects, designers and photographers

P15 applies to every medium: an architect with no attested style goes to the period architecture leaf of their birth (Neoclassical, Modern, Contemporary Architecture); a designer to the decorative-arts style of their working years (I3: Art Nouveau to Contemporary Design); a photographer to the photographic school of their working years (Pictorialism, Straight, Modernist, Documentary, Contemporary Photography). A designer or architect known first for one medium is placed by that medium.
modifiers: Period and dynasty — a filter on every kind and leaf (Umayyad, Abbasid, Fatimid, Seljuq, Ilkhanid, Mamluk, Timurid, Safavid, Ottoman, Mughal, Qajar ...). Never a node (P6).
Region and place — the 20-region grid of the gathering, plus production centre and country as tags (P7).

Ornament and motif — girih (geometric strapwork), arabesque (islimi), muqarnas, saz leaves, cintamani: a tag across media, never a leaf, since one motif runs through tiles, carpets, metalwork and buildings (open question Q6).
Holding institution and collection — evidence, never a node.
Patron and reign — a tag (Akbar, Shah Tahmasp, Süleyman); a royal atelier is a kind only when it is a recorded workshop (Imperial Mughal atelier, the Ottoman nakkaşhane).

Object type — bowl, ewer, tile, folio, page: an attribute of representative works, not a node. A leaf is a tradition, not an object type, except where the field treats the type as a tradition (astrolabes).
Inscription and script on objects — an attribute; calligraphy as an art (C1) is placed by script.
Subject and genre — portrait, landscape, still life, history painting, genre scene, religious image: a tag on works and kinds, never a node.

Technique and process — oil, tempera, fresco, watercolour, gouache, acrylic; woodcut, engraving, etching, lithography, screen print; daguerreotype, albumen, gelatin silver, colour and black-and-white photography: tags, never nodes (a fresco cycle is Art in Place by its site, an etching is a print by its school).
Abstraction and figuration — abstract art is a tag across movements (Abstract Expressionism, Suprematism, Dansaekhwa …), not a leaf of its own.
Building type — skyscraper, mosque, temple, castle, palace, house, garden pavilion: a tag on architecture kinds; styles are the leaves.
Folk and popular art — a filter that gathers the folk leaves of every medium (Mexican folk art = the Mexican folk leaves in A6, D5, E1, C4, H …).

fams.label: Feature Film
fams.test: a film of more than 40 minutes made as a single work for cinema, festival, television or streaming release; not anime.
key: 1. Non-fiction (documentary, concert film, nature film, essay film)? → A13 Documentary.
2. Animated, and not Japanese animation? → A15 Animated Feature (F17).

3. Does it belong to a named genre cycle — a narrow leaf of A2–A12, A17 or A18 (chanbara, kaidan, J-horror, yakuza, film noir, giallo, poliziottesco, blaxploitation, heroic bloodshed, wuxia, spaghetti western, pink film, kaiju, masala film ...)? → that leaf (F1, F2, F13). Otherwise, is it an attested member of a named film movement (Italian neorealism, the French New Wave, New Hollywood ...)? → A1 Movements & Schools.
4. Avant-garde, working outside narrative convention (abstract, structural, surrealist)? → A16 Experimental & Avant-Garde.
5. Is erotic display or sexual obsession the film's reason to exist? → A12 Erotic Film. A violent exploitation cycle with erotic elements is not: it goes on.
6. Does it aim first to frighten (ghosts, monsters, killers, gore)? → A4 Horror (F3).

7. Superheroes? → A6-3 (F15). Speculative science — the future, technology, space, aliens, giant monsters? → A5 Science Fiction & Monster (F5). Magic, myth, fairy tale or a quest in perilous places? → A6 Fantasy & Adventure.
8. The American frontier? → A17 Western (F20). Set in a past era that defines it, a real life, or about war? → A7 Historical, Period & War (F4, F11, F14).
9. Made first for children, or built on Christmas? → A19 Children's & Family (F18).
10. Espionage? → A3-7 Spy Film (F16). Criminals or police at the centre? → A2 Crime. Suspense, conspiracy or puzzle? → A3 Thriller & Mystery (F6).
11. Fights, chases and stunts carry it? → A8 Action & Martial Arts.
12. Songs or dance carry the story? → A11 Musical & Music. Laughter first? → A10 Comedy. A love story? → A9 Romance. Otherwise → A14 Drama (F7, F19).

subs.label: Movements & Schools
subs.axis: Axis: the named movement (membership attested in its reference sources).

leaves.label: Japanese New Wave
leaves.defn: the Nūberu bāgu: films of Ōshima, Imamura, Yoshida, Shinoda, Teshigahara, Hani and their peers (c. 1959–1975) that broke with studio humanism through politics, sexuality and formal rupture (Cruel Story of Youth, Woman in the Dunes, Death by Hanging). Members with a genre-cycle home (Harakiri, Kwaidan, Branded to Kill) sit in that cycle and carry the movement as a tag (D1).

leaves.label: German Expressionism
leaves.defn: the Weimar film movement of distorted sets, chiaroscuro and haunted protagonists, c. 1919–1931 (The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, Nosferatu, Metropolis, M).
leaves.see: A4-13 Gothic Horror; A2-5 Film Noir & Neo-Noir.

leaves.label: Soviet Montage
leaves.defn: the Soviet cinema of the 1920s built on montage theory — Eisenstein, Pudovkin, Vertov, Dovzhenko (Battleship Potemkin, Strike, Mother, Earth).

leaves.label: French Impressionist Cinema
leaves.defn: the French avant-garde narrative cinema of the 1920s — Gance, L'Herbier, Epstein, Dulac — built on subjective camera and rhythmic cutting (La Roue, Coeur fidèle, The Fall of the House of Usher).

leaves.label: Poetic Realism
leaves.defn: French films of the 1930s of doomed working-class lovers in fog-bound ports and back streets — Carné, Prévert, Renoir, Duvivier, Vigo (Port of Shadows, Le jour se lève, L'Atalante).

leaves.label: Italian Neorealism
leaves.defn: Italian films of 1943–1952 shot on location with non-professional actors about the poor and the war's aftermath — Rossellini, De Sica, Visconti, early Fellini (Rome, Open City, Bicycle Thieves, La terra trema, Umberto D.).

leaves.label: French New Wave
leaves.defn: the Nouvelle Vague of 1958–1968: Cahiers critics turned directors — Godard, Truffaut, Chabrol, Rohmer, Rivette, Varda — with location shooting, jump cuts and personal subjects (The 400 Blows, Breathless, Jules and Jim, Cléo from 5 to 7).

leaves.label: Left Bank
leaves.defn: the Rive Gauche group beside the New Wave — Resnais, Marker, Varda, Robbe-Grillet, Duras — literary, political and formally experimental (Hiroshima mon amour, Last Year at Marienbad).

leaves.label: British New Wave
leaves.defn: British films of 1959–1963 of working-class life in the industrial North, from the Angry Young Men and kitchen-sink writers (Saturday Night and Sunday Morning, A Taste of Honey, This Sporting Life).
leaves.aliases: kitchen sink realism; British social realism

leaves.label: Czechoslovak New Wave
leaves.defn: Czech and Slovak films of 1963–1969 — Forman, Chytilová, Menzel, Němec, Jireš — absurdist, satirical and humane (Daisies, Closely Watched Trains, The Firemen's Ball, Marketa Lazarová).
leaves.aliases: Czech New Wave; Československá nová vlna

leaves.label: Polish Film School
leaves.defn: Polish films of 1956–1963 about the war and its moral wreckage — Wajda, Munk, Kawalerowicz, Has (Kanał, Ashes and Diamonds, Eroica).

leaves.label: Yugoslav Black Wave
leaves.defn: the critical, dark and sexually frank Yugoslav films of 1963–1972 — Makavejev, Petrović, Žilnik, Pavlović (WR: Mysteries of the Organism, I Even Met Happy Gypsies).

leaves.label: Cinema Novo
leaves.defn: the Brazilian movement of the 1960s–70s — Glauber Rocha, Nelson Pereira dos Santos, Joaquim Pedro de Andrade — 'an idea in the head and a camera in the hand' (Black God, White Devil, Vidas Secas, Entranced Earth, Macunaíma).

leaves.label: Third Cinema
leaves.defn: the Latin American and Third World militant cinema of the late 1960s–70s set against Hollywood and auteur cinema (The Hour of the Furnaces, Memories of Underdevelopment, The Battle of Algiers).

leaves.label: New Hollywood
leaves.defn: the American director-driven cinema of c. 1967–1980 — Penn, Altman, Coppola, Scorsese, Ashby, Malick — in the wake of the studio system (Bonnie and Clyde, Easy Rider, Five Easy Pieces, Nashville).

leaves.label: New German Cinema
leaves.defn: West German auteur cinema of 1962–1982 after the Oberhausen Manifesto — Fassbinder, Herzog, Wenders, Schlöndorff, von Trotta, Kluge (Aguirre, the Wrath of God, Ali: Fear Eats the Soul, Kings of the Road).
leaves.aliases: Neuer Deutscher Film; Young German Cinema

leaves.label: Parallel Cinema
leaves.defn: Indian art cinema from the 1950s — Satyajit Ray, Ritwik Ghatak, Mrinal Sen, Adoor Gopalakrishnan, Shyam Benegal — realist and outside the song-and-dance mainstream (Pather Panchali, The Cloud-Capped Star, Ankur).

leaves.label: Iranian New Wave
leaves.defn: Iranian art cinema from the late 1960s and its post-revolutionary flowering — Kiarostami, Makhmalbaf, Panahi, Majidi — with child protagonists, non-actors and fiction-documentary blends (The Cow, Close-Up, Taste of Cherry, Children of Heaven).
leaves.aliases: Iranian New Wave cinema; Moj-e No

leaves.label: Taiwan New Cinema
leaves.defn: the Taiwanese New Wave of 1982–1990 — Hou Hsiao-hsien, Edward Yang — long takes and everyday history (A City of Sadness, A Brighter Summer Day, The Time to Live and the Time to Die).

leaves.label: Hong Kong New Wave
leaves.defn: the Hong Kong directors of 1979–1990 trained in television — Tsui Hark, Ann Hui, Patrick Tam, Allen Fong — and the 'second wave' of Wong Kar-wai and Stanley Kwan (Boat People, Days of Being Wild, Rouge).
leaves.aliases: HK New Wave; Hong Kong second wave

leaves.label: Fifth Generation
leaves.defn: the first class after the Cultural Revolution at the Beijing Film Academy — Chen Kaige, Zhang Yimou, Tian Zhuangzhuang — allegorical rural epics of the 1980s–90s (Yellow Earth, Red Sorghum, Raise the Red Lantern, Farewell My Concubine).

leaves.label: Sixth Generation
leaves.defn: Chinese independent urban realism of the 1990s–2000s — Jia Zhangke, Wang Xiaoshuai, Lou Ye, Zhang Yuan (Platform, Beijing Bicycle, Suzhou River, Still Life).

leaves.label: Dogme 95
leaves.defn: the Danish manifesto films made under the 'Vow of Chastity' — hand-held, location sound, no effects (The Celebration, The Idiots, Italian for Beginners).

leaves.label: Romanian New Wave
leaves.defn: Romanian minimalist realism from the 2000s — Puiu, Mungiu, Porumboiu, Muntean — long takes of bureaucracy and the moral afterlife of communism (The Death of Mr. Lazarescu, 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, 12:08 East of Bucharest).

leaves.label: Berlin School
leaves.defn: the German art cinema from the late 1990s — Petzold, Arslan, Schanelec, Ade, Köhler — detached, precise and observational (Barbara, Toni Erdmann, Phoenix).

leaves.label: New Queer Cinema
leaves.defn: the independent queer films of the early 1990s named by B. Ruby Rich — Haynes, Araki, Van Sant, Kalin, Jarman (Poison, My Own Private Idaho, The Living End, Paris Is Burning as documentary).

leaves.label: Mumblecore
leaves.defn: American micro-budget films of the 2000s with naturalistic acting and improvised dialogue about twenty-somethings — the Duplass brothers, Swanberg, Bujalski, early Gerwig (Funny Ha Ha, Hannah Takes the Stairs, The Puffy Chair).

leaves.label: L.A. Rebellion
leaves.defn: the Black filmmakers of UCLA, late 1960s–1980s — Charles Burnett, Haile Gerima, Julie Dash, Billy Woodberry (Killer of Sheep, Bush Mama, Daughters of the Dust).
leaves.aliases: Los Angeles School of Black Filmmakers

leaves.label: Australian New Wave
leaves.defn: the revival of Australian feature production c. 1970–1985 — Weir, Armstrong, Beresford, Schepisi (Picnic at Hanging Rock, Walkabout, Breaker Morant, My Brilliant Career).

leaves.label: Greek Weird Wave
leaves.defn: Greek films of the late 2000s–2010s — Lanthimos, Tsangari, Avranas — deadpan, absurd and alienated (Dogtooth, Attenberg, Alps).

leaves.label: New Argentine Cinema
leaves.defn: Argentine independent cinema from the mid-1990s — Martel, Trapero, Caetano, Alonso (Pizza, Beer, and Cigarettes, La Ciénaga, Nine Queens excepted as heist).

leaves.label: Cinéma du look
leaves.defn: French films of the 1980s with a glossy, youthful style from advertising and music video — Beineix, Besson, Carax (Diva, Subway, The Lovers on the Bridge, Betty Blue).

leaves.label: Slow Cinema
leaves.defn: contemplative art cinema of long takes, minimal story and observed duration, as named by critics from the 2000s: films of its core practitioners in that mode — Tarr, Tsai Ming-liang, Lav Diaz, Weerasethakul, Alonso, Reygadas, Costa, Ceylan, Angelopoulos — and Jeanne Dielman (Sátántangó, Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives). Precursors (Tarkovsky, Bresson, Ozu, Antonioni) carry it as see-also only; a film of a core director whose own genre is clear goes there.

leaves.label: Cinema Marginal
leaves.defn: the Brazilian underground of 1968–1973 that broke with Cinema Novo — Sganzerla, Bressane, Reichenbach (The Red Light Bandit, Killed the Family and Went to the Movies).
leaves.aliases: Cinema de Boca do Lixo; Udigrudi

leaves.label: Korean New Wave
leaves.defn: the socially critical South Korean films of the 1980s–90s after the end of military censorship — Park Kwang-su, Jang Sun-woo, Lee Chang-dong's debut (Chilsu and Mansu, A Single Spark, Green Fish).

leaves.label: No Wave Cinema
leaves.defn: the underground film scene of downtown New York, c. 1976–1985, beside No Wave music — Amos Poe, Beth B, Vivienne Dick, early Jarmusch (Smithereens, Born in Flames, Stranger Than Paradise, Permanent Vacation).
leaves.see: A1-36 New American Cinema; A16-1 Experimental Film.

leaves.label: Cinema of Moral Anxiety
leaves.defn: Polish films of 1976–1981 on moral compromise under late communism — Kieślowski, Zanussi, Holland, Wajda (Camera Buff, Man of Marble, Camouflage).

leaves.label: Portuguese New Cinema
leaves.defn: the Novo Cinema of the 1960s–70s that broke with the Estado Novo's studio films — Paulo Rocha, Fernando Lopes, António de Macedo (The Green Years, Change of Life, Belarmino).

leaves.label: Second Golden Age of Philippine Cinema
leaves.defn: the Filipino auteur cinema of the 1970s–early 80s under martial law — Lino Brocka, Ishmael Bernal, Mike de Leon (Manila in the Claws of Light, Insiang, Himala).

leaves.label: New American Cinema
leaves.defn: the American independent and underground film movement of the late 1950s–60s around the New American Cinema Group and the Film-Makers' Cooperative — Cassavetes, Frank, Mekas, Clarke (Shadows, Pull My Daisy, The Connection).
leaves.aliases: New American Cinema Group; American underground film
leaves.see: A1-15 New Hollywood; A16-1 Experimental Film.

subs.label: Crime
subs.axis: Axis: whose side the story takes and its milieu.

leaves.label: Yakuza Film
leaves.defn: yakuza eiga: films of the Japanese gangster world, from the chivalrous ninkyō films of 1960s Toei to the documentary-style jitsuroku films (Battles Without Honor and Humanity) and the V-cinema and Kitano cycles (Sonatine).
leaves.aliases: yakuza eiga; ninkyō eiga; jitsuroku eiga

leaves.label: Gangster Film
leaves.defn: films centred on organised criminals and their rise and fall outside the named national cycles.

leaves.label: Police & Detective Film
leaves.defn: films centred on police or detectives working a case (Stray Dog, The French Connection, Memories of Murder); buddy-cop films are A8-7.

leaves.label: Crime Drama
leaves.defn: films about crime, its perpetrators and its effects, told as drama rather than suspense or gang epic (Vengeance Is Mine, Dog Day Afternoon, City of God).

leaves.label: Film Noir & Neo-Noir
leaves.defn: crime films in the noir manner — fatalism, low-key style, corrupt cities, the femme fatale: the American cycle of the 1940s–50s (Double Indemnity, The Big Sleep) and its later neo-noir and national forms (Chinatown, Pale Flower, Branded to Kill).

leaves.label: Pinky Violence
leaves.defn: Toei's 1970s cycle of women's revenge, delinquent-girl (sukeban) and women-in-prison films, with violence and eroticism (Female Prisoner #701: Scorpion).
leaves.see: A12-1 Pink Film; A2-1 Yakuza Film.
leaves.weak: no Wikidata item; attested in Toei's own cycle name and the pink-film literature

leaves.label: Heist Film
leaves.defn: films built on planning and pulling off a robbery, and on its unravelling (The Italian Job, Heat, Ocean's Eleven, Reservoir Dogs; noir heists such as The Asphalt Jungle and Rififi are Film Noir by F1).

leaves.label: Prison Film
leaves.defn: films set inside prisons and built on incarceration, its society and escape (A Man Escaped, Escape from Alcatraz, The Shawshank Redemption, A Prophet).

leaves.label: Poliziottesco
leaves.defn: the Italian crime cycle of the 1970s — vigilante police, kidnapping and urban violence (Almost Human, The Big Racket, Rome Armed to the Teeth).

leaves.label: Blaxploitation
leaves.defn: the American cycle of 1970s films with Black heroes for Black urban audiences, mostly crime and action (Shaft, Super Fly, Coffy, Foxy Brown).

leaves.label: Cine Quinqui
leaves.defn: the Spanish cycle of 1977–1985 about juvenile delinquents of the urban periphery, often played by non-actors (Deprisa, deprisa, Navajeros, El Pico).

leaves.label: Hood Film
leaves.defn: crime dramas of urban youth, gangs and the street, from the American hood films of the 1990s (Boyz n the Hood, Menace II Society) to the British road and estate films (Kidulthood, Blue Story).

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller
leaves.defn: suspense built on disturbed minds, obsession and manipulation (Cure, Gone Girl, Black Swan).

leaves.label: Mystery Film
leaves.defn: whodunits and puzzle films built on detection, including honkaku adaptations and Agatha Christie films (The Inugamis, Knives Out).

leaves.label: Survival & Death-Game Thriller
leaves.defn: films in which characters are forced into a lethal contest or a fight to survive an ordeal (Battle Royale, The Hunger Games, 127 Hours, Cast Away).

leaves.label: Erotic Thriller
leaves.defn: suspense driven by sexual desire, seduction and danger, the Hollywood cycle of the 1980s–90s and its heirs (Fatal Attraction, Basic Instinct, Body Heat, Decision to Leave).

leaves.label: Revenge Thriller
leaves.defn: suspense built on a protagonist's revenge, including rape-and-revenge and the Korean revenge cycle (Oldboy, Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance, I Saw the Devil, Ms .45).
leaves.weak: attested as 'rape and revenge' (Wikidata) and as a Korean cycle in criticism; no item for 'revenge thriller'

leaves.label: Political & Conspiracy Thriller
leaves.defn: suspense built on state power, political violence, cover-ups and paranoia (Z, The Parallax View, All the President's Men, The Lives of Others).
leaves.aliases: political thriller; paranoid thriller; conspiracy film

leaves.label: Spy Film
leaves.defn: films whose plot is driven by espionage, from the Bond cycle to Cold War realism (Dr. No, The Spy Who Came in from the Cold, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, Mission: Impossible) (F16).

leaves.label: Giallo
leaves.defn: the Italian thriller-horror cycle of the 1960s–70s: black-gloved killers, stylised murders and amateur sleuths (Blood and Black Lace, The Bird with the Crystal Plumage, Deep Red).

leaves.label: Suspense Thriller
leaves.defn: thrillers of an ordinary protagonist in danger — the wrong man, the stalker, the hostage, the trap — outside the narrower leaves (Rear Window, North by Northwest, Duel, Panic Room).

leaves.label: J-Horror
leaves.defn: the Japanese horror cycle of the late 1990s–2000s: vengeful onryō, curses carried by media and technology, slow dread (Ring, Ju-On, Pulse, Dark Water).

leaves.label: Kaidan Film
leaves.defn: kaidan eiga: ghost-story films drawn from Edo and folk tales (Ugetsu, Kwaidan, Onibaba, Kuroneko).
leaves.aliases: kaidan eiga; Japanese ghost story film

leaves.label: Supernatural Horror
leaves.defn: horror from ghosts, demons, possession and curses outside the named cycles (The Exorcist, Hereditary, House).

leaves.label: Body Horror
leaves.defn: horror of the body transformed, invaded or fused with machines (Tetsuo: The Iron Man).

leaves.label: Splatter & Gore Film
leaves.defn: horror built on graphic violence, mutilation and torture (Audition, Ichi the Killer, Tokyo Gore Police).
leaves.aliases: splatter film; ero guro; extreme cinema

leaves.label: Zombie Film
leaves.defn: horror of the walking dead (One Cut of the Dead, Versus).

leaves.label: Found-Footage Horror
leaves.defn: horror presented as recovered amateur or documentary footage (Noroi: The Curse). Found-footage films that are not horror go by genre (Chronicle, Cloverfield).

leaves.label: Slasher Film
leaves.defn: horror built on a killer stalking and murdering victims one by one (Evil Dead Trap).

leaves.label: Psychological Horror
leaves.defn: horror whose dread comes from disturbed minds, unreality and inescapable spaces rather than monsters or gore (Strange Circus, Haze, Exit 8).

leaves.label: Folk Horror
leaves.defn: horror rooted in rural isolation, pagan ritual and folklore (Witchfinder General, The Wicker Man, The Witch, Midsommar).

leaves.label: Vampire Film
leaves.defn: horror and its offshoots built on vampires (Dracula 1931, Let the Right One In, Thirst, Near Dark).

leaves.label: Haunted House Film
leaves.defn: horror of a haunted dwelling and its ghosts (The Haunting, The Innocents, The Shining, The Conjuring).

leaves.label: Gothic Horror
leaves.defn: horror of castles, curses and the literary monsters of the Gothic tradition: the Universal monster cycle, Hammer, the Corman–Poe cycle and Italian Gothic (Frankenstein, The Curse of Frankenstein, Black Sunday, Crimson Peak; Dracula films are A4-11).
leaves.aliases: Hammer horror; Universal monsters; Italian gothic

leaves.label: Creature Feature & Natural Horror
leaves.defn: horror of monsters, mutated beasts and nature turned killer, outside the giant kaiju (Jaws, The Birds, Tremors, Gremlins, An American Werewolf in London).
leaves.aliases: monster movie; natural horror; werewolf film; eco-horror
leaves.see: A5-1 Kaiju Film; A4-15 Science Fiction Horror.

leaves.label: Science Fiction Horror
leaves.defn: horror whose threat comes from science, space or aliens (Alien, The Thing, Invasion of the Body Snatchers, Event Horizon, The Fly).

leaves.label: Comedy Horror
leaves.defn: horror played mainly for laughs, outside a named cycle (The Evil Dead II, What We Do in the Shadows, Tucker & Dale vs. Evil) (F12).

leaves.label: Jiangshi Film
leaves.defn: the Hong Kong cycle of hopping-corpse films, horror played with kung fu and comedy (Mr. Vampire, Encounters of the Spooky Kind, Rigor Mortis).
leaves.see: A4-16 Comedy Horror; A8-4 Kung Fu Film.

leaves.label: Home Invasion Film
leaves.defn: horror and thrillers of a household besieged by intruders (The Strangers, Funny Games, Don't Breathe, You're Next).

leaves.label: Cannibal Film
leaves.defn: the Italian exploitation cycle of the late 1970s–early 80s set among jungle cannibals (Cannibal Holocaust, Cannibal Ferox).

leaves.label: Asian Horror
leaves.defn: the East and Southeast Asian supernatural horror cycles that followed J-horror — Thai, Korean, Indonesian, Malaysian, Taiwanese and Hong Kong ghost, possession and shamanic horror; as a named cycle it wins over the subgenre leaves (F2) (Shutter, A Tale of Two Sisters, Satan's Slaves, The Eye).
leaves.weak: attested through Korean horror and Thai horror; no item for the umbrella term

leaves.label: Kaiju Film
leaves.defn: kaiju eiga and giant-monster films: Godzilla, Mothra, Gamera and their Hollywood and Korean kin (Godzilla 1954, King Kong, The Host, Pacific Rim).

leaves.label: Tokusatsu Hero Film
leaves.defn: live-action special-effects films of costumed transforming heroes (Ultraman, Kamen Rider, Super Sentai).

leaves.label: Science Fiction Film
leaves.defn: speculative films of the future, technology, artificial minds and alien contact outside the narrower leaves (2001: A Space Odyssey, Arrival, Summer Time Machine Blues).

leaves.label: Cyberpunk
leaves.defn: high-tech, low-life science fiction of cybernetic bodies and urban decay, with its Japanese punk-industrial strand (Tetsuo, Burst City).

leaves.label: Disaster & Post-Apocalyptic Film
leaves.defn: films of catastrophe — natural, technological or speculative — and of collapse and survival after it (Airport, The Poseidon Adventure, Japan Sinks, Mad Max: Fury Road) (F26).

leaves.label: Space Opera & Space Adventure
leaves.defn: adventure on an interplanetary scale: starships, galactic empires and space westerns (Star Wars, Guardians of the Galaxy, Dune).

leaves.label: Dystopian Film
leaves.defn: films of oppressive future societies (Metropolis excepted as Expressionism; Brazil, Children of Men, Snowpiercer, The Hunger Games excepted as survival).

leaves.label: Alien Invasion & First Contact
leaves.defn: films of extraterrestrial invasion or contact (The War of the Worlds, Close Encounters of the Third Kind, Independence Day, District 9).

leaves.label: Time Travel Film
leaves.defn: films whose plot is built on travel in time or time loops (Back to the Future, 12 Monkeys, Primer, Groundhog Day excepted as comedy).

leaves.label: Fantasy Film
leaves.defn: live-action films of magic, myth and invented worlds outside the narrower leaves (Harry Potter, Pan's Labyrinth, The Great Yokai War).

leaves.label: Adventure Film
leaves.defn: journeys, quests and treasure hunts in exotic or perilous settings (Raiders of the Lost Ark, The Mummy 1999).

leaves.label: Superhero Film
leaves.defn: films of costumed or super-powered heroes — the Marvel and DC cycles and their kin — and live-action adaptations of power-based manga (Superman, The Dark Knight, Gantz, Death Note) (F15).
leaves.aliases: superhero film; comic-book film; live-action manga adaptation

leaves.label: High Fantasy
leaves.defn: epic fantasy of invented worlds, quests and sword-and-sorcery (The Lord of the Rings, Conan the Barbarian, The NeverEnding Story).

leaves.label: Fairy-Tale Film
leaves.defn: live-action films of fairy tales and their retellings (Beauty and the Beast 1946, The Princess Bride, Three Wishes for Cinderella).
leaves.weak: attested as a film form in the fairy-tale literature (Zipes); no item for 'fairy-tale film'

leaves.label: Swashbuckler
leaves.defn: adventure of sword-fighting heroes — pirates, musketeers, outlaws (The Adventures of Robin Hood, The Three Musketeers, Pirates of the Caribbean).

subs.label: Historical, Period & War
subs.axis: Axis: the era and what the past is used for.

leaves.label: Jidaigeki
leaves.defn: period drama set before the Meiji Restoration in which the past is the subject — manners, politics, family and fate rather than swordplay (Sansho the Bailiff, The Life of Oharu, Twilight Samurai).

leaves.label: Chanbara
leaves.defn: samurai swordplay films in which sword combat carries the drama (Seven Samurai, Yojimbo, Zatoichi, 13 Assassins).

leaves.label: War Film
leaves.defn: films about war and soldiers' experience of it (Fires on the Plain, The Burmese Harp, The Human Condition).

leaves.label: Historical Drama
leaves.defn: films whose past era defines them outside the narrower leaves: dramas of real events and of fictional lives in a recorded past, from the Meiji era to the twentieth century (The Story of the Last Chrysanthemum, Titanic, The Last Emperor); lives of real people are A7-8.

leaves.label: Atomic Bomb Film
leaves.defn: genbaku eiga: films about the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and the hibakusha (Children of Hiroshima, Black Rain).

leaves.label: Sword-and-Sandal Film
leaves.defn: epics of the ancient and biblical world, including the Italian peplum (Ben-Hur, Spartacus, The Ten Commandments, Hercules 1958, Gladiator).

leaves.label: Costume Drama
leaves.defn: dramas of manners in a period setting, often literary adaptations and heritage films (Barry Lyndon, The Age of Innocence, Pride & Prejudice, The Leopard).

leaves.label: Biographical Film
leaves.defn: films that tell a real person's life or career (Lawrence of Arabia, Gandhi, Amadeus, The Social Network) (F14).

leaves.label: Holocaust Film
leaves.defn: fiction films about the Nazi persecution and murder of the Jews (Schindler's List, The Pianist, Son of Saul, The Zone of Interest).
leaves.see: A7-3 War Film; A13-1 Documentary Film.

leaves.label: Partisan Film
leaves.defn: Yugoslav, Albanian and other Eastern-bloc films of the Second World War partisan resistance (The Battle of Neretva, Walter Defends Sarajevo, Red Poppies on the Wall; Come and See excepted as war).

leaves.label: Martial Arts Film
leaves.defn: films built on unarmed or weapons combat in modern or timeless settings outside chanbara, kung fu and wuxia (The Street Fighter, The Raid, Ong-Bak).

leaves.label: Action Film
leaves.defn: films carried by fights, chases, gunplay and stunts outside the narrower leaves (Die Hard, Mad Max: Fury Road, John Wick).

leaves.label: Wuxia
leaves.defn: Chinese films of martial-arts chivalry: wandering swordsmen and women of the jianghu with gravity-defying combat (Come Drink with Me, A Touch of Zen, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, Hero).
leaves.see: A8-4 Kung Fu Film; A7-2 Chanbara.

leaves.label: Kung Fu Film
leaves.defn: Hong Kong and Chinese unarmed martial-arts films, from Shaw Brothers and Bruce Lee to Jackie Chan and Ip Man (Enter the Dragon, The 36th Chamber of Shaolin, Drunken Master, Ip Man).
leaves.see: A8-3 Wuxia; A8-1 Martial Arts Film.

leaves.label: Heroic Bloodshed
leaves.defn: the Hong Kong gunplay cycle of the late 1980s–90s: brotherhood, honour and balletic shoot-outs (A Better Tomorrow, The Killer, Hard Boiled).

leaves.label: Hong Kong Action Cinema
leaves.defn: Hong Kong stunt-driven action outside kung fu, wuxia and heroic bloodshed: police action, girls-with-guns and the Milkyway crime-action films (Police Story, Project A, Exiled).

leaves.label: Buddy Cop Film
leaves.defn: action films of two mismatched police partners (48 Hrs., Lethal Weapon, Rush Hour, Hot Fuzz).

leaves.label: Romantic Drama
leaves.defn: love stories told as drama (Casablanca, In the Mood for Love, Love Letter).

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: love stories told for laughter (When Harry Met Sally..., Notting Hill).

leaves.label: Comedy Film
leaves.defn: films aimed first at laughter outside the narrower leaves (Groundhog Day, Tampopo).

leaves.label: Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: films that balance comedy with serious drama (Tokyo Sonata).

leaves.label: Black Comedy & Satire
leaves.defn: comedy of death, taboo and social satire (Dr. Strangelove, The Funeral, The Taste of Tea).

leaves.label: Screwball Comedy
leaves.defn: the fast-talking romantic comedies of the 1930s–40s, American above all, and their European kin, battle of the sexes and comedy of remarriage (It Happened One Night, Bringing Up Baby, His Girl Friday).

leaves.label: Slapstick Comedy
leaves.defn: physical comedy of pratfalls, chases and sight gags, from the silent clowns to Tati and Mr. Bean (The General, City Lights, Duck Soup, Playtime).

leaves.label: Parody & Spoof
leaves.defn: comedy that mocks a genre or a famous work (Airplane!, Young Frankenstein, Monty Python and the Holy Grail, Scary Movie).

leaves.label: Teen & Sex Comedy
leaves.defn: comedy of adolescence, parties and sexual initiation (Animal House, Fast Times at Ridgemont High, American Pie, Superbad).
leaves.aliases: teen comedy; sex comedy; gross-out comedy

leaves.label: Commedia all'italiana
leaves.defn: Italian comedy of 1958–1980 that satirised postwar society — Monicelli, Risi, Germi, Scola (Big Deal on Madonna Street, Divorce Italian Style, Il Sorpasso).

leaves.label: Action Comedy
leaves.defn: comedy carried by action set pieces outside the buddy-cop cycle (Beverly Hills Cop, The Nice Guys, Kung Fu Hustle).

leaves.label: Crime Comedy
leaves.defn: comedy of criminals, capers and botched crimes (The Ladykillers, A Fish Called Wanda, Snatch, The Big Lebowski).

leaves.label: Mockumentary
leaves.defn: fiction comedy in the form of a documentary (This Is Spinal Tap, Best in Show, Borat).

leaves.label: Bourekas Film
leaves.defn: the Israeli comedy and melodrama cycle of the 1960s–70s built on Mizrahi–Ashkenazi ethnic stereotypes (Sallah Shabati, Snooker, Charlie and a Half).

leaves.label: Stand-Up Comedy Film
leaves.defn: recorded stand-up comedy performances released as films or specials (Richard Pryor: Live in Concert, Eddie Murphy Raw, Nanette).

subs.label: Musical & Music
subs.axis: Axis: how music carries the film.

leaves.label: Musical & Music Film
leaves.defn: films carried by song and music: stage and screen musicals and films about musicians and bands (Singin' in the Rain, La La Land, Linda Linda Linda).

leaves.label: Dance Film
leaves.defn: films built on dance and dancers, competitions and the dance floor (The Red Shoes, Saturday Night Fever, Dirty Dancing, Step Up).

leaves.label: Rumberas Film
leaves.defn: the Mexican cabaret melodrama of the 1940s–50s built on rumba dancers and the nightclub (Aventurera, Victims of Sin).

subs.label: Erotic Film
subs.axis: Axis: the circuit it was made for.

leaves.label: Pink Film
leaves.defn: pinku eiga: independent Japanese softcore features made from the 1960s for the pink-film circuit, a training ground for directors (Daydream).

leaves.label: Roman Porno
leaves.defn: Nikkatsu's studio line of erotic features (1971–1988) under which Kumashiro, Tanaka and Sone made auteur films (Flower and Snake, A Woman Called Sada Abe).

leaves.label: Erotic Drama
leaves.defn: art-house and mainstream films whose subject is sexual obsession (In the Realm of the Senses, Last Tango in Paris, The Housemaid).

leaves.label: Sexploitation
leaves.defn: low-budget softcore features made for sex appeal outside Japan — nudie-cuties, Russ Meyer, Euro-softcore (Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!, Emmanuelle, Vixen!).

leaves.label: Pornographic Film (retired)
leaves.defn: Retired (S1). Hardcore pornography is classified in the Pleasure Taxonomies (EP II-K-1 Watching Pornography: theatrical, home-video and internet eras), not here; an explicit film made and received as cinema is placed by its genre (Caligula → A7-6). The code is not reused.
leaves.aliases: Golden Age of Porn; porno chic
leaves.see: EP II-K-1 Watching Pornography (Pleasure Taxonomies); A12-4 Sexploitation.

leaves.label: Documentary Film
leaves.defn: non-fiction films outside the narrower leaves: social, political, historical and portrait documentaries (Shoah, Hoop Dreams, The Act of Killing).

leaves.label: Concert & Music Documentary
leaves.defn: documentaries of musicians, concerts and festivals (Woodstock, Stop Making Sense, The Last Waltz, Summer of Soul).

leaves.label: Nature Documentary
leaves.defn: documentaries of wildlife and the natural world (Microcosmos, March of the Penguins, My Octopus Teacher).

leaves.label: Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité
leaves.defn: observational documentaries of the 1960s–70s with light cameras and synchronous sound (Primary, Salesman, Grey Gardens, Chronicle of a Summer).
leaves.aliases: cinéma vérité; observational documentary; direct cinema

leaves.label: True Crime Documentary
leaves.defn: documentaries investigating real crimes and miscarriages of justice (The Thin Blue Line, Paradise Lost, Capturing the Friedmans).

leaves.label: Essay Film
leaves.defn: personal, reflective non-fiction that argues and wanders (Night and Fog, Sans Soleil, F for Fake, The Gleaners and I).

leaves.label: City Symphony
leaves.defn: 1920s–30s documentaries that render a city's day as visual rhythm (Berlin: Symphony of a Metropolis, Man with a Movie Camera, Manhatta).

leaves.label: Mondo Film
leaves.defn: Italian-born shockumentaries of bizarre customs and violence, 1962 onward (Mondo Cane, Africa Addio, Faces of Death).

leaves.label: Ethnographic Film
leaves.defn: documentaries of peoples and cultures made from fieldwork (Nanook of the North, Moi, un noir, Dead Birds).

subs.label: Drama
subs.axis: Axis: the drama's subject (family, youth, society, the individual).

leaves.label: Shomingeki
leaves.defn: shomin-geki: dramas of ordinary lower-middle-class urban life, centred on the family and the workplace, the home genre of Ozu, Naruse and Kinoshita (Tokyo Story, Floating Clouds).

leaves.label: Family Drama
leaves.defn: dramas of families, parents and children outside the classic shomingeki (Kramer vs. Kramer, Shoplifters, A Separation).

leaves.label: Coming-of-Age Film
leaves.defn: youth, school and teen films about growing up (The 400 Blows excepted as New Wave; Stand by Me, Lady Bird, Kids Return).
leaves.aliases: seishun eiga; youth film; teen film

leaves.label: Social Drama
leaves.defn: dramas of social conditions, poverty, work, institutions and injustice (Ikiru, Parasite, I, Daniel Blake).

leaves.label: Character Study
leaves.defn: dramas centred on one person's inner life, grief, solitude or change (Taxi Driver, Drive My Car, Perfect Days).

leaves.label: Melodrama
leaves.defn: emotionally heightened dramas of suffering and sacrifice, especially the women's film (Sirk, haha-mono mother films, Imitation of Life, The Life of Oharu).
leaves.aliases: haha-mono; women's film; weepie; chick flick (drama)

leaves.label: Sports Film
leaves.defn: films built on a sport and its competition, comic or dramatic (Rocky, Raging Bull, Moneyball) (F19).

leaves.label: Animal Film
leaves.defn: live-action films centred on an animal and its bond with people (The Story of Hachikō, The Adventures of Milo and Otis).
src: Wikidata Q6619915 (list of films about animals)

leaves.label: Taiyōzoku Film
leaves.defn: the 'Sun Tribe' youth films of 1956 adapted from Ishihara Shintarō — affluent, amoral postwar youth (Season of the Sun, Crazed Fruit).
leaves.see: A14-3 Coming-of-Age Film; A1-1 Japanese New Wave.
leaves.weak: no Wikidata item; attested in Japanese film histories (taiyōzoku eiga)

leaves.label: Legal Drama
leaves.defn: dramas built on a trial, a lawyer's case or a jury (12 Angry Men, To Kill a Mockingbird, Anatomy of a Murder, Anatomy of a Fall) (F19).

leaves.label: Road Movie
leaves.defn: films whose structure is a journey on the road, comic or dramatic (Easy Rider excepted as New Hollywood; Thelma & Louise, Paris, Texas, Wild Strawberries, Y tu mamá también) (F19).

leaves.label: Banlieue Film
leaves.defn: French films of the multi-ethnic housing estates on the cities' edge, their youth, police and violence (La Haine, Girlhood, Divines, Les Misérables 2019).
leaves.see: A2-11 Hood Film; A14-4 Social Drama.

leaves.label: Christian Film
leaves.defn: films made by and for Christian audiences, of conversion and faith (The Passion of the Christ excepted as biblical epic; God's Not Dead, Fireproof).

leaves.label: Political Drama
leaves.defn: dramas of politics and power, of leaders, campaigns and activists, outside the thriller (Mr. Smith Goes to Washington, The Candidate, Milk excepted as biopic, Battle of Algiers excepted as Third Cinema).

subs.label: Animated Feature
subs.axis: Axis: technique and tradition (non-anime). Built at scale.

leaves.label: Hand-Drawn Animated Feature
leaves.defn: two-dimensional features animated by hand on cels or paper, or drawn digitally in 2D (Flash, Toon Boom, digital cut-out silhouettes), the Disney tradition and its rivals and the European, Soviet and Chinese studios (Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, The Lion King, The Snow Queen, The Triplets of Belleville).

leaves.label: Computer-Animated Feature
leaves.defn: features made with 3D computer animation, from Toy Story (1995) on: Pixar, DreamWorks, Disney and their peers (Shrek, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, Ne Zha).

leaves.label: Stop-Motion Feature
leaves.defn: features animated frame by frame with puppets, clay or cut-outs (The Nightmare Before Christmas, Coraline, Chicken Run, Fantastic Mr. Fox).

leaves.label: Adult Animated Feature
leaves.defn: animated features made for adults — satire, sex, politics, memoir — whatever the technique (Fritz the Cat, Persepolis, Anomalisa, Flee excepted as documentary).

leaves.label: Experimental Film
leaves.defn: avant-garde and underground films that work outside narrative convention (Dog Star Man, Wavelength, Terayama's Emperor Tomato Ketchup).

leaves.label: Surrealist Film
leaves.defn: films of the surrealist movement and its heirs, dream logic and provocation (L'Âge d'Or, The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie, Eraserhead, The Holy Mountain).

subs.label: Western
subs.axis: Axis: setting (the American frontier and its transpositions).

leaves.label: Western
leaves.defn: the classical western of the American frontier: gunfighters, cavalry, cattle drives and settlers (Stagecoach, The Searchers, Rio Bravo).

leaves.label: Spaghetti Western
leaves.defn: Italian westerns of 1964–1978 — Leone, Corbucci, Sollima — with mercenary heroes, operatic violence and Morricone scores (A Fistful of Dollars, The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, Django, Once Upon a Time in the West).

leaves.label: Revisionist Western
leaves.defn: westerns that question the genre's myths — violence, race, the frontier (The Wild Bunch, McCabe & Mrs. Miller, Little Big Man, Unforgiven).

leaves.label: Neo-Western
leaves.defn: films set in the modern American West that carry the western's codes (Lonely Are the Brave, No Country for Old Men, Hell or High Water, Brokeback Mountain excepted as romance) (F20).

leaves.label: Ostern
leaves.defn: Soviet and East German westerns and 'Eastern' adventures (White Sun of the Desert, The Sons of Great Bear).

subs.label: Popular Cinema Modes
subs.axis: Axis: the named popular-cinema mode — a production culture the field names as a genre of its own (F13).

leaves.label: Masala Film
leaves.defn: South Asian popular cinema that mixes action, romance, comedy, melodrama and song-and-dance in one star vehicle — the Hindi, Telugu, Tamil and other Indian industries, and the same mode in Bangladesh (Dhallywood) and Pakistan (Lollywood) (Sholay, Amar Akbar Anthony, Baahubali, RRR, Pushpa) (F13).
leaves.aliases: masala movie; Bollywood masala; mass film; Bollywood film; Hindi film; song-and-dance film
leaves.see: A1-17 Parallel Cinema; A11-1 Musical & Music Film.

leaves.label: Nollywood Film
leaves.defn: Nigerian popular film made in the Nollywood mode: the home-video melodramas of family, wealth, the occult and the city from Living in Bondage (1992), and the 'New Nollywood' cinema releases that grew from them (The Wedding Party, King of Boys) (F13).

leaves.label: Yeşilçam Film
leaves.defn: Turkish popular cinema of the Istanbul studios, c. 1950–1990: star melodramas, comedies and adventure films made fast for a mass audience (Hababam Sınıfı, Selvi Boylum Al Yazmalım, Tosun Paşa).

leaves.label: Children's Film
leaves.defn: live-action films made first for children (The Wizard of Oz excepted as fantasy; Mary Poppins excepted as musical; Matilda, Paddington, Kes excepted as drama).
leaves.see: A6-1 Fantasy Film; A14-8 Animal Film.

leaves.label: Christmas Film
leaves.defn: films built on Christmas, comic, romantic or dramatic (It's a Wonderful Life, Miracle on 34th Street, Home Alone, Elf) (F18).

fams.label: Short Film
fams.test: a film of 40 minutes or less (the Academy's line), fiction, animation, documentary or experimental; Japanese animated shorts go to E Anime.
