key: 1. Animated? → B1 Animated Short, by tradition and technique.
2. Non-fiction (actualities, documentary shorts)? → B3 Documentary & Actuality Short.
3. Avant-garde, outside narrative convention? → B4 Experimental Short.
4. Otherwise live-action fiction → B2 Live-Action Short.

leaves.label: Theatrical Cartoon
leaves.defn: studio cartoon shorts made for cinema programmes, the golden age of American animation and its kin (Disney's Silly Symphonies, Looney Tunes, Tom and Jerry, Fleischer's Betty Boop).

leaves.label: Auteur Animated Short
leaves.defn: independent and art animation shorts by individual animators and national studios — NFB, Soyuzmultfilm, Zagreb School (Neighbours, Hedgehog in the Fog, The Man Who Planted Trees).

leaves.label: Stop-Motion & Puppet Short
leaves.defn: shorts animated with puppets, clay or objects (A Grand Day Out, The Wrong Trousers, Dimensions of Dialogue).

leaves.label: Computer-Animated Short
leaves.defn: shorts made with 3D computer animation (Luxo Jr., Geri's Game, Bao).

leaves.label: Animated Television Special
leaves.defn: animated specials made for television broadcast, chiefly holiday specials (A Charlie Brown Christmas, How the Grinch Stole Christmas!, Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer).

subs.label: Live-Action Short
subs.axis: Axis: mode (trick film, silent comedy, narrative short).

leaves.label: Trick Film
leaves.defn: early fantasy shorts built on camera tricks and stage illusion, Méliès and his rivals (A Trip to the Moon, The Haunted Castle).

leaves.label: Silent Comedy Short
leaves.defn: one- and two-reel comedies of the silent clowns and the early sound comedy teams (One Week, The Immigrant, Laurel and Hardy's The Music Box).

leaves.label: Narrative Short Film
leaves.defn: live-action fiction shorts of every genre (La Jetée, The Red Balloon, Six Shooter).

leaves.label: Actuality Film
leaves.defn: the non-fiction views of early cinema, 1890s–1900s (Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory, The Arrival of a Train, Carmencita).

leaves.label: Documentary Short
leaves.defn: documentaries under 40 minutes (Night and Fog, Glass, The Silent World excepted as feature).

leaves.label: Avant-Garde Short
leaves.defn: experimental and avant-garde shorts — surrealist, abstract, structural and underground (Un Chien Andalou, Meshes of the Afternoon, Scorpio Rising, Window Water Baby Moving).

fams.label: Television Series
fams.test: a series made for television or streaming — scripted series and miniseries, and documentary series — anywhere, outside the named long-running serial traditions, anime and unscripted entertainment.
key: 0. Non-fiction (a documentary series)? → C8 Documentary Series (TV7).
1. Animated, and not anime? → C6 Animated Series (TV1).
2. Made first for children or tweens (live action)? → C7 Children's Series.

3. An East or Southeast Asian drama in a named tradition — K-drama romance, sageuk, makjang, Chinese costume drama, wuxia/xianxia drama, idol drama, asadora, taiga drama, Japanese trendy drama, lakorn, BL drama? → C2 (D3). Asian dramas outside those traditions (thrillers, medical, fantasy) go by genre below with 'Asian drama' as a filter.
4. Science fiction, fantasy, horror, the supernatural or superheroes? → C5 Genre Series.
5. Criminals, police, detectives, spies or a thriller plot? → C3 Crime & Thriller Series.
6. Laughter first? → C4 Comedy Series. Otherwise → C1 Drama Series, by subject.

subs.label: Drama Series
subs.axis: Axis: subject (family, medicine, law, politics, the past, youth).

leaves.label: Family Drama Series
leaves.defn: series about families and their generations (Six Feet Under, This Is Us, Succession, Reply 1988).

leaves.label: Medical Drama
leaves.defn: series set in hospitals and medical practice (ER, Grey's Anatomy, House, Hospital Playlist).

leaves.label: Legal Drama Series
leaves.defn: series about lawyers and the law's own world (L.A. Law, The Good Wife, Extraordinary Attorney Woo) (TV4).

leaves.label: Political Drama Series
leaves.defn: series of government, elections and power (The West Wing, House of Cards, Borgen).

leaves.label: Teen Drama
leaves.defn: series about adolescents and high school (Beverly Hills, 90210, Skins, Euphoria, Sex Education excepted as comedy).

leaves.label: Period Drama Series
leaves.defn: series set in a defining past, costume and historical drama (Downton Abbey, The Crown, Mad Men, Rome).
leaves.see: C2-2 Sageuk; C2-5 Chinese Costume Drama.

leaves.label: War Drama Series
leaves.defn: series about war and soldiers (Band of Brothers, The Pacific, Generation Kill).

leaves.label: Western Series
leaves.defn: series of the American frontier (Gunsmoke, Bonanza, Deadwood, Yellowstone as neo-western).

leaves.label: Docudrama Series
leaves.defn: dramatisations of real events and lives that are not crimes (Chernobyl, The Crown excepted as period, The Dropout, WeCrashed).

leaves.label: Workplace & Professional Drama
leaves.defn: series built on a profession or workplace outside medicine and law (The Newsroom, Mad Men excepted as period, The Bear, Misaeng).

leaves.label: Sports Drama Series
leaves.defn: series built on a sport and its teams (Friday Night Lights, Ted Lasso excepted as comedy).

leaves.label: Drama Series
leaves.defn: dramas of character and society outside the narrower leaves (The Leftovers, Normal People, The Crown excepted as period).
leaves.aliases: serial drama; prestige drama; miniseries; limited series

leaves.label: Anthology Drama Series
leaves.defn: series of self-contained plays or stories with changing casts (Play for Today, Armchair Theatre, Inside No. 9 excepted as comedy, The Twilight Zone excepted as SF).

leaves.label: Action & Adventure Series
leaves.defn: series carried by action, voyages, quests and treasure hunts, from literary adaptations to stunt-driven adventure (Relic Hunter, Knight Rider, MacGyver) (Treasure Island serials, Around the World in 80 Days, The Adventures of Robin Hood, Sharpe excepted as war).

leaves.label: Romantic Drama Series
leaves.defn: series whose main line is a love story, outside the Asian drama traditions (Outlander excepted as fantasy, Bridgerton, Normal People).

leaves.label: Erotic Drama Series
leaves.defn: series whose subject is sexual desire and display, including the Indian erotic web series of the streaming platforms (Gandii Baat, Mastram; Spartacus excepted as period).

leaves.label: Vertical Short Drama
leaves.defn: serials of one- to two-minute vertical episodes made for short-drama apps, mostly melodramatic romance and revenge (ReelShort, DramaBox).

subs.label: East & Southeast Asian Drama Traditions
subs.axis: Axis: the named tradition (D3: 'Asian drama' is a filter; Asian dramas outside these traditions are placed by genre).

leaves.label: K-Drama
leaves.defn: the Korean miniseries tradition of romance and melodrama — trendy, fated and rom-com love stories in 16–20 episodes (Winter Sonata, Guardian: The Lonely and Great God, Crash Landing on You, Coffee Prince).
leaves.aliases: Korean drama; Korean miniseries; K-drama romance

leaves.label: Sageuk
leaves.defn: Korean historical drama of the Joseon, Goryeo and Three Kingdoms courts (Dae Jang Geum, Moon Embracing the Sun, Mr. Sunshine, Kingdom).

leaves.label: Makjang
leaves.defn: Korean melodrama of outrageous twists — birth secrets, revenge, chaebol families, affairs — often in daily and weekend slots (The Penthouse, Temptation of Wife, The World of the Married).

leaves.label: Chinese Costume Drama
leaves.defn: guzhuang: Chinese historical and palace drama of the imperial past (Story of Yanxi Palace, Nirvana in Fire, Empresses in the Palace, Meteor Garden excepted as idol drama).

leaves.label: Wuxia & Xianxia Drama
leaves.defn: Chinese drama of martial heroes (wuxia), of immortal cultivation and celestial romance (xianxia), and of gods and demons (shenmo) (The Legend of the Condor Heroes, The Untamed, Eternal Love, Journey to the West).
leaves.aliases: wuxia drama; xianxia drama; shenmo drama

leaves.label: Idol & Modern Romance Drama
leaves.defn: Taiwanese and Chinese drama of modern romance: the idol drama of pop-idol casts from Meteor Garden (2001), and the modern Chinese campus, urban, workplace and fantasy romances that followed (It Started with a Kiss, Go Go Squid!, Hidden Love).
leaves.aliases: ouxiang ju; Taiwanese drama; C-drama romance

leaves.label: Asadora
leaves.defn: NHK's morning serial (renzoku terebi shōsetsu) of a woman's life across decades (Oshin, Amachan, Carnation).

leaves.label: Taiga Drama
leaves.defn: NHK's year-long historical drama of a figure of Japanese history (Sanada Maru, Ryōmaden, The 13 Lords of the Shogun).
leaves.see: C2-7 Asadora; C1-6 Period Drama Series.

leaves.label: Japanese Television Drama
leaves.defn: the Japanese drama series (dorama) of romance, school, work and everyday life in one-cour seasons, from the trendy dramas of Fuji TV's Monday 9 pm slot to the late-night and streaming manga adaptations (Tokyo Love Story, Long Vacation, Hana Yori Dango, Nigeru wa Haji da ga Yaku ni Tatsu).

leaves.label: Lakorn
leaves.defn: Thai television drama (lakhon), with its romance, revenge and slap-kiss conventions (Love Destiny, The Crown Princess, Girl from Nowhere excepted as thriller).

leaves.label: Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.defn: BL and GL series — romance between young men or between young women — from Thailand, the Philippines, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, China and the rest of East and Southeast Asia (SOTUS, 2gether, Bad Buddy, Cherry Magic!, GAP).
leaves.aliases: BL drama; Y series; danmei drama

leaves.label: Main-Melody Drama
leaves.defn: the Chinese state-endorsed drama of revolutionary history, Party leaders and national achievement (The Age of Awakening, Minning Town, Medal of the Republic, Mao Zedong).
leaves.see: C1-9 Docudrama Series; C1-7 War Drama Series.

leaves.label: Republican-Era Drama
leaves.defn: Chinese drama set in the Republic of China (1912–1949): romance, spy and family sagas of Shanghai and the warlord years (Winter Begonia, Siege in Fog, Romance in the Rain, The Disguiser).
leaves.see: C2-4 Chinese Costume Drama; C3-5 Spy & Espionage Series.
leaves.weak: no article under this label; attested through the Chinese television drama article

leaves.label: TVB Drama
leaves.defn: the Hong Kong television drama of TVB and its rivals, modern and costume, in 20–40-episode serials (The Greed of Man, War and Beauty, Triumph in the Skies, Line Walker).
leaves.aliases: Hong Kong television drama; TVB series
leaves.see: C2-4 Chinese Costume Drama; C2-5 Wuxia & Xianxia Drama.

subs.label: Crime & Thriller Series
subs.axis: Axis: milieu and source of suspense.

leaves.label: Police Procedural Series
leaves.defn: series of police investigations case by case (Hill Street Blues, NYPD Blue, Law & Order, Line of Duty, Signal).

leaves.label: Detective Series
leaves.defn: series of a detective solving mysteries, whodunits and cosy crime (Columbo, Poirot, Sherlock, Midsomer Murders).

leaves.label: Crime Drama Series
leaves.defn: series of fictional criminals and their world (The Sopranos, The Wire, Breaking Bad, Peaky Blinders) (TV4).

leaves.label: Nordic Noir
leaves.defn: Scandinavian crime series of bleak landscapes and slow investigations (The Killing, The Bridge, Wallander, Trapped).

leaves.label: Spy & Espionage Series
leaves.defn: series of intelligence agents (Mission: Impossible, The Americans, Homeland, Slow Horses, The Bureau).

leaves.label: Thriller Series
leaves.defn: suspense series of conspiracy, survival, revenge and psychological danger (24, Mr. Robot, Squid Game, Money Heist excepted as crime).

leaves.label: Psychological & Domestic Thriller Series
leaves.defn: suspense miniseries of secrets, marriages and threats at home (Doctor Foster, Liar, Fool Me Once, Big Little Lies).

leaves.label: True Crime Drama
leaves.defn: dramatised series of real criminal cases (Mindhunter, Dahmer, The Serpent).

subs.label: Comedy Series
subs.axis: Axis: comic form (multi-camera sitcom, single-camera, sketch, mockumentary).

leaves.label: Multi-Camera Sitcom
leaves.defn: studio sitcoms shot before an audience or laugh track (I Love Lucy, Cheers, Seinfeld, Friends, The Big Bang Theory).

leaves.label: Single-Camera Comedy
leaves.defn: film-style comedy series without laugh track (Curb Your Enthusiasm, Arrested Development, Fleabag, Atlanta).

leaves.label: Mockumentary Sitcom
leaves.defn: comedy in documentary form (The Office, Parks and Recreation, What We Do in the Shadows, Abbott Elementary).

leaves.label: Sketch Comedy
leaves.defn: series of comic sketches (Monty Python's Flying Circus, Saturday Night Live, Key & Peele).

leaves.label: Comedy-Drama Series
leaves.defn: series balancing comedy and drama (M*A*S*H, Gilmore Girls, Ted Lasso, The Bear excepted as workplace).

leaves.label: Stand-Up Comedy Special
leaves.defn: recorded stand-up shows and series of them (James Acaster: Repertoire, Nanette as special).

leaves.label: Satire & Political Comedy
leaves.defn: comedy that satirises politics and institutions (Yes Minister, The Thick of It, Veep).

subs.label: Genre Series
subs.axis: Axis: speculative premise (science fiction, fantasy, horror, superheroes).

leaves.label: Science Fiction Series
leaves.defn: series of the future, space and technology (Star Trek, Doctor Who, The Expanse, Black Mirror, Severance).

leaves.label: Fantasy Series
leaves.defn: series of magic and invented worlds (Game of Thrones, The Witcher, Outlander, Alchemy of Souls).

leaves.label: Horror Series
leaves.defn: series that aim first to frighten (The Walking Dead, American Horror Story, The Haunting of Hill House, Sweet Home).

leaves.label: Supernatural Drama
leaves.defn: series of ghosts, vampires, witches and the uncanny told as drama or adventure (Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Supernatural, Twin Peaks, Stranger Things).

leaves.label: Superhero Series
leaves.defn: series of costumed or super-powered heroes (Smallville, Daredevil, The Boys, WandaVision).

leaves.label: Tokusatsu Series
leaves.defn: the Japanese live-action special-effects hero series and their adaptations, for children and adults alike (Ultraman, Kamen Rider, Super Sentai, Power Rangers, Garo).
leaves.see: E2-6 Mecha & Tokusatsu Anime; C5-5 Superhero Series.

leaves.label: Animated Sitcom
leaves.defn: animated comedy series for adults and families (The Flintstones, The Simpsons, South Park, BoJack Horseman, Rick and Morty).

leaves.label: Adult Animated Series
leaves.defn: non-comedy animation for adults (Invincible, Primal, Love, Death & Robots, Blue Eye Samurai).

leaves.label: Animated Action-Adventure
leaves.defn: animated adventure series for all ages (Batman: The Animated Series, Avatar: The Last Airbender, Gravity Falls, The Legend of Vox Machina).

leaves.label: Children's Animated Series
leaves.defn: cartoon series made first for children (Looney Tunes, SpongeBob SquarePants, Bluey, Peppa Pig).

leaves.label: Preschool Series
leaves.defn: live-action and puppet series for young children (Sesame Street, Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, Teletubbies).

leaves.label: Children's & Tween Series
leaves.defn: live-action series for children and tweens (Lizzie McGuire, Hannah Montana, iCarly, Goosebumps).

leaves.label: Nordic Christmas Calendar
leaves.defn: the Scandinavian Advent serial of 24 daily episodes broadcast 1–24 December, whatever its genre (Jul i Skomakergata, The Julekalender, Sunes jul, Jul på Månetoppen).

leaves.label: Documentary Series
leaves.defn: non-fiction series of history, society, culture and science (The World at War, Cosmos, The Last Dance, Wild Wild Country).

leaves.label: True Crime Docuseries
leaves.defn: documentary series investigating real crimes (The Jinx, Making a Murderer, The Staircase, The Devil Next Door).

leaves.label: Nature Documentary Series
leaves.defn: series of wildlife and the natural world (Life on Earth, Planet Earth, Blue Planet II).

fams.label: Serial Drama Traditions
fams.test: a long-running serial in a named serial tradition, with continuing storylines broadcast daily or weekly for years or hundreds of episodes: soap opera, telenovela, dizi, Indian daily soap, teleserye, musalsal (TV2).
key: 1. Latin American or Iberian telenovela? → D1. 2. Anglophone soap opera? → D2. 3. Turkish dizi? → D3. 4. South Asian serial? → D4. 5. Arab musalsal? → D5. 6. Philippine teleserye? → D6.

leaves.label: Telenovela
leaves.defn: the Latin American serial of a single romance resolved in one run of 100–200 episodes, Mexican, Venezuelan and Colombian (Los ricos también lloran, Yo soy Betty, la fea, Café con aroma de mujer).

leaves.label: Brazilian Novela
leaves.defn: the Brazilian telenovela, above all TV Globo's prime-time novelas das nove (Roque Santeiro, Avenida Brasil, Escrava Isaura).

leaves.label: Narconovela
leaves.defn: the Colombian and Mexican telenovela of drug traffickers (El Patrón del Mal, La Reina del Sur, Sin senos no hay paraíso).

leaves.label: Youth Telenovela
leaves.defn: telenovelas for children and teens (Chiquititas, Rebelde Way, Rebelde, Violetta).

subs.label: Soap Opera
subs.axis: Axis: daypart and national industry (the field's own division).

leaves.label: American Daytime Soap Opera
leaves.defn: US daytime serials sponsored for the home audience (Guiding Light, General Hospital, Days of Our Lives, The Young and the Restless).

leaves.label: British & Irish Soap Opera
leaves.defn: British and Irish continuing dramas of a community (Coronation Street, EastEnders, Emmerdale, Fair City).

leaves.label: Australian & New Zealand Soap Opera
leaves.defn: Australian and New Zealand serials (Neighbours, Home and Away, Prisoner, Shortland Street).

leaves.label: Prime-Time Soap Opera
leaves.defn: evening serials of wealthy families, intrigue and cliffhangers (Peyton Place, Dallas, Dynasty, Melrose Place, Desperate Housewives).

leaves.label: European Soap Opera
leaves.defn: the continental European daily and weekly soaps and the European telenovelas outside Iberia (Lindenstraße, Gute Zeiten, schlechte Zeiten, Un posto al sole, Inimă de țigan).

leaves.label: Dizi
leaves.defn: the Turkish weekly serial of 120–150-minute episodes, romance, family honour and class (Aşk-ı Memnu, Fatmagül'ün Suçu Ne?, Kara Sevda).

leaves.label: Historical Dizi
leaves.defn: Turkish serials set before the founding of the Republic (1923), from the Seljuk and Ottoman court epics to late-Ottoman romances (Muhteşem Yüzyıl, Diriliş: Ertuğrul, Kurt Seyit ve Şura).

leaves.label: Indian Daily Soap
leaves.defn: the Hindi and regional daily serial of the joint family, above all the saas-bahu (mother-in-law and daughter-in-law) serial of the 2000s (Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii, Balika Vadhu, Anupamaa).

leaves.label: Indian Mythological Serial
leaves.defn: serials of the epics and the gods (Ramayan, Mahabharat, Devon Ke Dev...Mahadev).

leaves.label: Pakistani Drama Serial
leaves.defn: the Urdu prime-time drama serial of family and romance (Humsafar, Zindagi Gulzar Hai, Mere Paas Tum Ho).

leaves.label: Sri Lankan Teledrama
leaves.defn: the Sinhala television serial (teledrama), from the long-running family serials to the literary adaptations (Deweni Inima, Kopi Kade).

leaves.label: Ramadan Musalsal
leaves.defn: the Arab serial made for the Ramadan season, Syrian, Egyptian, Gulf and North African (Bab al-Hara, Al-Taghriba al-Filistiniya, Omar, Awled Moufida).

leaves.label: Arab Drama Serial
leaves.defn: Arab serials made outside the Ramadan season, including the long pan-Arab adaptations of Turkish dizi (Bride of Beirut, Al Hayba excepted as Ramadan).

leaves.label: Teleserye
leaves.defn: the Philippine prime-time serial (Pangako Sa 'Yo, Ang Probinsyano, Encantadia).

fams.label: Anime
fams.test: Japanese animation in any format (TV series, film, OVA, ONA, special); format is a filter, never a division (D4). Donghua and Korean animation selected through the anime database are placed here with their country as a filter.
key: 1. Explicit sexual content made for the adult market (hentai)? → not placed here: the Pleasure Taxonomies (S1). An adult-flagged drama, horror or art anime goes on by its genre (AN8).
2. Made first for young children (kodomo-muke), or a family literary adaptation? → E11 Children's & Family.
3. A magical girl who transforms to fight or to help? → E4 Magical Girl.
4. Giant robots, or speculative science (space, cyborgs, the future) that carries the story — not a device that only frames a school comedy, romance or idol show? → E2 Mecha & Science Fiction.
5. A sport or a competitive game carries it? → E7 Sports.
6. Aims first to frighten? → E9 Horror.

7. Transported or reborn into another world, or an invented fantasy world or yōkai spirit world at its centre? → E3 Fantasy & Isekai (a battle series in a fantasy world with a shōnen battle structure is E1, AN1).
8. Fights and powers carry it? → E1 Action & Battle.
9. A love story first? → E5 Romance & Romantic Comedy. Everyday life, healing calm, cute-girls, idols and bands? → E6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei.
10. Laughter first? → E10 Comedy. Otherwise → E8 Drama, Psychological & Mystery.

subs.label: Action & Battle
subs.axis: Axis: the fighting premise (shōnen battle, martial arts, samurai). Built at scale.

leaves.label: Shōnen Battle
leaves.defn: long-running action series of escalating fights, rivals, training arcs and power systems, the core of Weekly Shōnen Jump adaptations (Dragon Ball Z, Naruto, One Piece, Bleach, Jujutsu Kaisen, Demon Slayer).

leaves.label: Seinen Action
leaves.defn: violent action for adult audiences — mercenaries, hunters, gunfights, dark warriors (Hellsing, Black Lagoon, Gantz, Golgo 13; Berserk excepted as dark fantasy).

leaves.label: Samurai & Ninja Anime
leaves.defn: action in Japan's samurai and ninja past, including chanbara anime (Rurouni Kenshin, Samurai Champloo, Ninja Scroll, Sword of the Stranger).

leaves.label: Superhero Anime
leaves.defn: anime of costumed heroes and hero societies (My Hero Academia, One-Punch Man, Tiger & Bunny).

leaves.label: Action Anime
leaves.defn: action series and films outside shōnen battle, seinen action and the narrower leaves — light-novel and game-based action, school battle series (Absolute Duo, Akame ga Kill! excepted as dark fantasy).

leaves.label: Wuxia & Xianxia Animation
leaves.defn: animation of martial heroes and of immortal cultivation, Chinese (donghua) above all, and Japanese works in the same genre, (Soul Land, Battle Through the Heavens, Link Click excepted as drama).

leaves.label: Delinquent Anime
leaves.defn: anime of yankī delinquents and gang fights (Tokyo Revengers, Great Teacher Onizuka excepted as comedy-drama, Crows-type brawlers).

leaves.label: Martial Arts Anime
leaves.defn: anime built on hand-to-hand fighting and tournaments outside shōnen battle power systems (Baki, Kengan Ashura, Fist of the North Star).

subs.label: Mecha & Science Fiction
subs.axis: Axis: real-robot, super-robot, cyberpunk, space opera. Built at scale.

leaves.label: Super Robot
leaves.defn: giant robots as invincible heroes with signature attacks (Mazinger Z, Getter Robo, Gurren Lagann).

leaves.label: Real Robot
leaves.defn: mecha as mass-produced military machines in realistic wars (Mobile Suit Gundam, Macross, Code Geass, Neon Genesis Evangelion).

leaves.label: Cyberpunk Anime
leaves.defn: high-tech, low-life futures of cyborgs, networks and megacities (Akira, Ghost in the Shell, Serial Experiments Lain, Psycho-Pass).

leaves.label: Space Opera Anime
leaves.defn: adventure and war among the stars (Space Battleship Yamato, Legend of the Galactic Heroes, Cowboy Bebop, Space Brothers excepted as drama).

leaves.label: Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
leaves.defn: anime of giant monsters and of the tokusatsu hero franchises (Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters, SSSS.Gridman, Godzilla Singular Point).
leaves.see: A5-1 Kaiju Film; A5-2 Tokusatsu Hero Film.

leaves.label: Science Fiction Anime
leaves.defn: speculative anime outside mecha, cyberpunk and space opera: time travel, post-apocalypse, aliens, technology (Steins;Gate, Dr. Stone, Planetes, Attack on Titan excepted as dark fantasy).

subs.label: Fantasy & Isekai
subs.axis: Axis: the invented world. Built at scale.

leaves.label: Isekai
leaves.defn: stories of people transported to or reborn in another world (Re:Zero, Mushoku Tensei, KonoSuba, That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime, Sword Art Online).

leaves.label: Fantasy Adventure
leaves.defn: quests and journeys through invented worlds and magic (Spirited Away, Frieren, Made in Abyss, Magi).

leaves.label: Dark Fantasy
leaves.defn: grim fantasy of monsters, war and cruelty (Attack on Titan, Claymore, Devilman Crybaby, Vinland Saga excepted as historical).

leaves.label: Shenmo Animation
leaves.defn: Chinese animation of gods and demons from the classical shenmo novels and myth (Ne Zha, Monkey King: Hero Is Back, Havoc in Heaven).
leaves.aliases: gods and demons fiction; Chinese mythological animation

leaves.label: Supernatural & Yōkai Anime
leaves.defn: the spirit world among us — yōkai, gods, exorcists, ghosts — told as adventure or quiet wonder (Natsume's Book of Friends, Mushishi, Noragami, Mononoke).

leaves.label: Magical Girl
leaves.defn: mahō shōjo: girls who gain magic to help others, from Sally the Witch and Minky Momo to Cardcaptor Sakura.
src: Wikidata Q752321 (magical girl anime and manga)

leaves.label: Magical Girl Warrior
leaves.defn: magical girls who transform to fight evil in teams, and their dark deconstructions (Sailor Moon, Pretty Cure, Puella Magi Madoka Magica).
leaves.aliases: sentai magical girl; dark magical girl
src: Wikidata Q752321 (magical girl anime and manga)

subs.label: Romance & Romantic Comedy
subs.axis: Axis: tone and demographic (shōjo, josei, harem). Built at scale.

leaves.label: Shōjo Romance
leaves.defn: romance written for girls, of first love and feelings (Fruits Basket, Kimi ni Todoke, Ouran High School Host Club, Nana excepted as josei).

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: love stories told for laughter, often school rom-coms (Toradora!, Kaguya-sama: Love Is War, Horimiya).

leaves.label: Harem
leaves.defn: one protagonist surrounded by several romantic interests (Love Hina, The Quintessential Quintuplets, Tenchi Muyo!).

leaves.label: Boys' Love
leaves.defn: romance between men (BL, yaoi) (Given, Sasaki and Miyano, Doukyuusei).

leaves.label: Yuri
leaves.defn: romance between women (Bloom Into You, Citrus, Revolutionary Girl Utena excepted as drama).

leaves.label: Romantic Drama Anime
leaves.defn: love stories told as drama, including josei romance (Your Name excepted as fantasy; Nana, Honey and Clover, Clannad, The Garden of Words).

leaves.label: Iyashikei
leaves.defn: 'healing' anime of calm, beauty and small pleasures (Aria, Yuru Camp, Non Non Biyori, Barakamon).
leaves.see: E6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things.

leaves.label: Cute Girls Doing Cute Things
leaves.defn: moe slice-of-life of girls' clubs and daily routines (K-On!, Lucky Star, Azumanga Daioh, Nichijou excepted as gag).

leaves.label: Slice of Life Anime
leaves.defn: everyday school, work and family life outside the narrower leaves (Shirobako, Silver Spoon, Spy × Family excepted as comedy).

leaves.label: Idol Anime
leaves.defn: anime of idol groups and their rise (Love Live!, The Idolmaster, Uta no Prince-sama, Oshi no Ko excepted as drama).

leaves.label: Music Anime
leaves.defn: anime of musicians, bands and performance (Your Lie in April, Bocchi the Rock!, Beck, Nodame Cantabile).

leaves.label: Performing Arts Anime
leaves.defn: anime of theatre, revue, rakugo, recitation and circus (Kageki Shoujo!!, Kaleido Star, Akane-banashi, Revue Starlight).
leaves.see: E6-4 Idol Anime; E6-5 Music Anime.

leaves.label: Cooking & Gourmet Anime
leaves.defn: anime built on food, cooking and eating (Food Wars!, Sweetness and Lightning, Restaurant to Another World).

leaves.label: Sports Anime
leaves.defn: spokon: anime of a sport, a team and its competitions — volleyball, basketball, baseball, football, boxing, cycling, swimming (Slam Dunk, Haikyu!!, Hajime no Ippo, Ashita no Joe, Blue Lock).

leaves.label: Game Anime
leaves.defn: anime of competitive games — go, shogi, karuta, mahjong, card battles (Hikaru no Go, Chihayafuru, March Comes in Like a Lion excepted as drama, Yu-Gi-Oh!).
leaves.aliases: card battle anime; board game anime

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller Anime
leaves.defn: suspense of minds in conflict, manipulation and identity (Death Note, Monster, Perfect Blue, Paranoia Agent, The Promised Neverland).

leaves.label: Mystery & Detective Anime
leaves.defn: anime of detection and puzzles (Case Closed, Hyouka, Odd Taxi, Erased).

leaves.label: Drama Anime
leaves.defn: dramas of grief, growing up, family and society (Anohana, Violet Evergarden, A Silent Voice, March Comes in Like a Lion, Wolf Children).
leaves.see: E5-6 Romantic Drama Anime; E6-3 Slice of Life Anime.

leaves.label: Historical & War Anime
leaves.defn: anime in which a historical era or a war is the subject (Grave of the Fireflies, In This Corner of the World, The Rose of Versailles, Vinland Saga).

leaves.label: Death Game & Survival Anime
leaves.defn: anime of lethal games and forced survival contests (Danganronpa, Darwin's Game, Kaiji, Btooom!, Future Diary).

leaves.label: Art & Experimental Anime
leaves.defn: independent and avant-garde Japanese animation made outside genre — Kuri, Yamamura, Furukawa, Aihara (Cat Soup, Mt. Head, Belladonna of Sadness excepted as drama).

leaves.label: Crime & Gangster Anime
leaves.defn: anime of thieves, gangsters and the underworld (Lupin III, Baccano!, 91 Days, Great Pretender).

subs.label: Horror
subs.axis: Axis: source of fear. Built at scale.

leaves.label: Horror Anime
leaves.defn: anime that aims first to frighten — curses, ghosts, killers, cosmic dread (Another, Higurashi: When They Cry, Shiki, Junji Ito Collection).
leaves.see: E3-3 Dark Fantasy; E8-1 Psychological Thriller Anime.

subs.label: Comedy
subs.axis: Axis: comic mode. Built at scale.

leaves.label: Gag & Parody Anime
leaves.defn: comedy first: gags, absurdity, parody and surreal humour (Gintama, Nichijou, The Disastrous Life of Saiki K., Pop Team Epic).

leaves.label: Ecchi
leaves.defn: comedy and fan service built on sexual innuendo without explicit content (High School DxD, Prison School, Kill la Kill excepted as battle).

leaves.label: Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: situation and character comedy outside gag and ecchi (Spy × Family, Grand Blue, The Devil Is a Part-Timer!).

leaves.label: Kodomo-muke
leaves.defn: anime made for young children, including the long family series (Doraemon, Anpanman, Crayon Shin-chan, Pokémon, Chibi Maruko-chan).

leaves.label: Early Japanese Animation
leaves.defn: Japanese animation before the television era (to 1962): the silent and early sound shorts of Shimokawa, Kitayama, Kōuchi, Ōfuji and Masaoka the wartime features and the first postwar shorts (Namakura Gatana, Momotaro's Divine Sea Warriors, Kumo no Ito); Toei's feature films from Hakujaden (1958) go by genre.

leaves.label: World Masterpiece Theater
leaves.defn: Nippon Animation's series of family adaptations of Western classics and their kin (Heidi, Girl of the Alps, Anne of Green Gables, A Dog of Flanders).

subs.label: Adult Anime
subs.axis: Axis: none (one leaf); is_adult titles of the anime database.

leaves.label: Hentai (retired)
leaves.defn: Retired (S1). Explicit hentai made to arouse is classified in the Pleasure Taxonomies (EP II-K-12 Drawn & Animated Erotic Media), not here; an adult-flagged anime made as drama, horror or art is placed by its genre (AN8), and ecchi stays E10-2. The code is not reused.
leaves.see: EP II-K-12 Drawn & Animated Erotic Media (Pleasure Taxonomies); E10-2 Ecchi.

fams.label: Asian Drama (retired)
fams.test: Retired by ruling D3: East and Southeast Asian drama series are placed in C Television Series (C2) and 'Asian drama' is a filter. The code F is not reused.

fams.label: Unscripted Formats
fams.test: unscripted entertainment television: the formats licensed across borders (≥3 versions in ≥2 countries, national versions as variants), the East Asian variety shows of the drama database, and the domestic unscripted programmes of the series selection (talk, variety, reality, court and instructional shows).
key: 1. Contestants compete for a prize or title? → G1 Competition Formats.
2. Real people filmed in arranged situations (dating, makeover, swaps, docusoap)? → G2 Factual Entertainment Formats.
3. Hosts, guests, games and talk in a studio or on location? → G3 Variety & Talk.

leaves.label: Talent Show
leaves.defn: singing, dancing and variety talent contests judged by panel and public (Idols, Got Talent, The Voice, The X Factor, Dancing with the Stars).

leaves.label: Reality Competition
leaves.defn: contestants live together or travel and are eliminated (Survivor, Big Brother, The Amazing Race, Fort Boyard).

leaves.label: Cooking Competition
leaves.defn: contests of cooks and bakers (MasterChef, Hell's Kitchen, The Great British Bake Off, Top Chef).

leaves.label: Game Show
leaves.defn: quiz and game formats played in a studio (Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, Wheel of Fortune, The Price Is Right, The Chase).

leaves.label: Business Pitch Show
leaves.defn: entrepreneurs pitch to investors (Dragons' Den, Shark Tank, The Apprentice).

leaves.label: Dating Show
leaves.defn: formats of courtship and matchmaking (The Dating Game, The Bachelor, Love Island, Married at First Sight).

leaves.label: Docusoap & Social Experiment
leaves.defn: real people followed or placed in arranged situations, including occupational and paranormal-investigation reality (Wife Swap, The Real Housewives, Deadliest Catch, Dirty Jobs, Ghost Hunters, Jackass).
leaves.aliases: docusoap; social experiment; survival reality; bridal docusoap; shopping docusoap

leaves.label: Makeover Show
leaves.defn: transformations of people, homes and businesses (Extreme Makeover, Queer Eye, Kitchen Nightmares, Grand Designs).
leaves.aliases: makeover television; lifestyle show; home renovation show; house flipping

leaves.label: Hidden Camera & Prank Show
leaves.defn: real people caught in staged situations, pranks and stunts filmed on hidden or open camera (Candid Camera, Punk'd, Impractical Jokers, Jackass).

leaves.label: Variety Show
leaves.defn: entertainment programmes of games, missions, music and comedy led by a fixed cast or host, and broadcasts of concerts and stage performances — including the Korean and Japanese real-variety shows (Running Man, Infinite Challenge, 2 Days & 1 Night, The Ed Sullivan Show, Austin City Limits).

leaves.label: Panel Show
leaves.defn: comedy panel games of a host, team captains and guests (QI, Have I Got News for You, Would I Lie to You?, Never Mind the Buzzcocks).

leaves.label: Talk Show
leaves.defn: host-led conversation programmes, late-night and daytime (The Tonight Show, Late Show with David Letterman, The Daily Show, Wetten, dass..?).

leaves.label: Court Show
leaves.defn: arbitration of real small-claims disputes before a television judge (The People's Court, Judge Judy, Judge Rinder).

leaves.label: Instructional & Lifestyle Show
leaves.defn: programmes that teach a craft, cooking, painting or home skill (The French Chef, The Joy of Painting, Good Eats, This Old House).
leaves.see: G1-3 Cooking Competition; G2-3 Makeover Show.

leaves.label: Web Show
leaves.defn: unscripted online video series of a host or channel (Good Mythical Morning, Hot Ones, Everything Wrong With, PewDiePie); scripted web series go by genre in C.

familyKey: 1. Is it Japanese animation (anime), in any format — TV series, film, OVA, ONA, special? → E Anime; format is a filter (D4). Animation from elsewhere is placed by its form below (a feature → A15 Animated Feature).
2. Is it an unscripted format licensed across countries (talent competition, dating, cooking, game show, docusoap)? → G Unscripted Formats.
3. Is it a long-running serial in a named serial tradition — telenovela, dizi, Indian daily soap, soap opera? → D Serial Drama Traditions.

4. Any other scripted series or miniseries, from anywhere — including the East and Southeast Asian drama traditions (K-drama, Chinese costume drama, asadora, taiga drama, lakorn)? → C Television Series (D3: Asian drama is a filter, not a family).
5. A film of 40 minutes or less? → B Short Film. Otherwise → A Feature Film (the Academy's 40-minute line).
precedence: A film with a home in a named genre cycle (chanbara, kaidan, J-horror, yakuza, film noir, pink film, Roman Porno, pinky violence, kaiju, tokusatsu, Taiyōzoku) goes to that cycle, even when a movement's reference sources list it as a member. A movement leaf keeps the attested members with no cycle home; every attested member carries the movement as a tag (D1).
A named cycle with its own canon (J-horror, kaiju eiga, yakuza eiga, pink film) beats the general genre leaf (supernatural horror, monster film, gangster film, sexploitation).
A film whose story turns on ghosts or the supernatural is horror (kaidan eiga) even when set in the Edo period; period setting alone does not make jidaigeki win.
A jidaigeki whose drama is carried by sword combat is chanbara; a period film of manners, politics or family is jidaigeki.
A film built on a giant monster (kaiju) is Kaiju Film whether or not a costumed hero appears; a costumed transforming hero with no giant monster at its centre is Tokusatsu Hero Film.
Criminals or police and their world at the centre → Crime; suspense built on a threat to an ordinary protagonist, a conspiracy or a puzzle → Thriller & Mystery.
A love story as the main line → Romance; aimed at laughter first → Comedy; otherwise Drama, divided by its subject.

A fantastical or science-fiction device that only frames a love story or a youth drama (a time slip, a letter from the future) does not make the film fantasy or science fiction: it is placed by the story it frames (A9, A14-3).
When a film named as a leaf example would be sent elsewhere by the key, the key wins and the example is replaced; examples never override the key.
Japanese animation is always E Anime, never an animated-feature leaf, whatever list it was selected from.
A war fought in Japan's pre-1868 past is jidaigeki or chanbara, not War Film (Ran, Kagemusha).

A genre cycle wins over Comedy when the cycle's premise drives the plot (Zom 100 → Zombie Film; Shaun of the Dead → Zombie Film). Comedy keeps films whose premise is only a backdrop for gags; a horror film played mainly for laughs with no cycle home is Comedy Horror.

A South Asian popular star vehicle that mixes an action strand with romance, comedy, melodrama and song-and-dance is Masala Film, before the general crime, action, fantasy and historical leaves (Sholay, Baahubali, Pushpa). Without an action strand, a family or romance musical goes by its main line with Masala Film as see-also (Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge → Romantic Drama). A film built on one narrow premise keeps that leaf with Masala Film as see-also (heist, spy, superhero, sport, revenge: Dhoom, Pathaan, Krrish, Dangal). A Nigerian film made in the Nollywood mode is Nollywood Film unless a named genre cycle claims it. Films outside those modes (parallel cinema, art-house, realist thrillers) are placed by genre like any other film.

A film that tells a real person's life or career is Biographical Film whatever the person's field (musicians, athletes, criminals), unless it is mainly a war film, a sports contest or a named cycle; a dramatised single real event is placed by its genre (a heist → Heist Film; a battle → War Film).

A film whose protagonist has a costumed or super-powered heroic identity is Superhero Film, before Action, Science Fiction and Fantasy; a superhero parody stays there too. Japanese transforming heroes are Tokusatsu (F5).
Espionage as the plot's engine makes a Spy Film, before Action and Political Thriller (James Bond, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy).
Every animated feature that is not Japanese animation is Animated Feature (A15), placed by technique, whatever its genre; animated documentaries are Documentary (key step 1). Genre is a see-also.

A live-action film made first for children (not a family-friendly fantasy or adventure, which keep their genre) is Children's Film; a film built on Christmas is Christmas Film, before Comedy, Romance and Drama.

A film whose structure is a journey is Road Movie, a film built on a sport and its competition is Sports Film, and a film built on a trial is Legal Drama, whether comic or dramatic, unless a named cycle claims it.

A war film is about the war and the soldiers' experience of it; a horror, action or thriller film that merely uses a war as its setting goes by its own genre (Sisu → Action Film; Overlord → Science Fiction Horror).

When a film's defining trait is named by a narrow leaf that the key reaches only later (Crime Comedy, Action Comedy, Parody & Spoof, Black Comedy & Satire, Sports Film, Dance Film, Spy Film, Road Movie), that leaf wins over the broader sub-family reached first: The Olsen Gang → Crime Comedy, a Karl May spoof → Parody & Spoof, a fencing biopic → Sports Film; a war satire (The Great Dictator, Jojo Rabbit) → Black Comedy & Satire; a spy comedy → Parody & Spoof when it mocks the genre (Johnny English, Spy), otherwise Action Comedy.

Subgenre leaves (vampire, zombie, slasher, haunted house, creature feature, found footage) are not named cycles for F1/D1: an attested movement member that is also a vampire film stays in the movement (Nosferatu → German Expressionism). Named cycles are the period- and industry-bound leaves (giallo, J-horror, poliziottesco, spaghetti western, Ostern, blaxploitation, erotic thriller ...); revisionist and neo-Western are subgenres; a later foreign remake or homage of a cycle film goes by its own genre, with the cycle as see-also (The Grudge 2019).

An original love story in a period setting is Romantic Drama (The English Patient, Portrait of a Lady on Fire); Costume Drama takes the drama of manners and society, above all literary adaptations (Austen, James, Wharton, Forster: A Room with a View, The Age of Innocence). A period comedy goes by its comic mode.

A comedy whose fantastical or speculative premise only carries the gags is Comedy (Groundhog Day, Multiplicity, Bedazzled, Ivan Vasilyevich Changes His Profession), with the genre as see-also; a science-fiction action comedy is Action Comedy (Men in Black). A live-action/animation hybrid is Animated Feature only when animation carries most of the film (Who Framed Roger Rabbit yes, Space Jam yes, Enchanted no).

A star vehicle carried by fights, chases and stunts is Action even when its hero is a cop or a criminal (Die Hard, Speed, Cobra); Crime takes films whose subject is the crime, its world or its investigation. Disaster films are A5-5 whether the catastrophe is speculative or real (Airport, The Towering Inferno, Titanic excepted as romance).

A children's television film (Disney Channel and Nickelodeon originals, Halloweentown) is Children's Film whatever its premise; theatrical family fantasy and science fiction keep their genre (F18). A feature assembled from television episodes is excluded as a compilation (the episodes belong to their series); an animated television special under 40 minutes is B1-5.

A film set on the American frontier (or a transposition of its codes to another frontier — the Australian bushranger film, Aferim!) is a Western leaf before Action, Historical Drama and Comedy; a contemporary crime film in the West is Neo-Western only when the frontier code carries it (Hell or High Water, No Country for Old Men).

A series whose episodes are built on escalating fights, rivals and power systems (shōnen battle) is E1 even when set in a fantasy world (Fullmetal Alchemist, Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen); an isekai or a fantasy whose world and journey carry it stays E3 (Re:Zero, Frieren).
All seasons, films, OVAs and specials of one franchise share the leaf of its main series, unless a spin-off belongs to another genre outright (a gag spin-off → E10).
Shōnen, seinen, shōjo and josei are tags on every title (MAL/AniList demographic); they divide leaves only where the field names a demographic genre (shōjo romance, josei).

A series whose premise is a pretext for gags or parody (gag manga, a genre parody) is E10 whatever its setting or club (Detroit Metal City, Dragon Half, KonoSuba excepted as isekai, since its world carries the story).
A children's franchise (Pokémon, Digimon, Doraemon) stays in E11 across its entries (AN2), including films made for its grown-up fans.

A setting, sport, band or speculative frame that is only a backdrop does not decide the leaf: the sport must drive the plot for E7 (Blue Box → romance), a fantasy world must carry the story for E3 (a villainess romance in a fantasy court → romance). Toy-line battle shows for children (Beyblade, Bakugan) are E11; one-off comedy specials and chibi extras of a franchise are E10.

Explicit hentai is classified in the Pleasure Taxonomies (S1; E12-1 retired); an adult-flagged art film or erotic drama (Cleopatra 1970, Shoujo Tsubaki) is placed by its genre. A gag series about everyday life is E10 (comedy first, AN5); a gentle everyday series without gag structure is E6.

AN1 holds for science-fiction and samurai settings too: a series built on escalating fights and power systems is E1 (Kaiju No. 8, Jigokuraku); a death game or gambling series whose engine is the game, not the fights, is E8-6 (Kakegurui, Juuni Taisen excepted as battle). Ecchi series whose fan service carries them stay E10-2 even with fights (High School DxD).

A magical-girl or robot frame on a romance or comedy does not make E4 or E2 (AN7); a magical-girl parody is E10. A historical war epic whose era and campaigns are the subject is E8-4 even with constant battles (Kingdom, Vinland Saga). Comedy shorts, bloopers and chibi extras of a franchise are E10; side stories in the franchise's own genre stay with it (AN2).
Non-Japanese animation in the anime database
Donghua and Korean animation selected through the anime database are placed by the same key, with country as a filter; animation from elsewhere selected as film is A15.
Every animated series that is not anime is C6, whatever its genre (The Simpsons → Animated Sitcom; Arcane → Animated Action-Adventure).

A long-running serial in a named serial tradition (telenovela, dizi, daily soap, soap opera, teleserye, musalsal) is D, not C, even when it is also a crime or historical story; a limited or seasonal series with a closed arc is C.

An Asian drama in a named tradition of C2 stays there whatever its genre mix (a sageuk with zombies, Kingdom, is Sageuk; a xianxia romance is Wuxia & Xianxia Drama); a Korean thriller or a Japanese medical drama with no tradition home goes by genre.

A series centred on crime, police, lawyers defending criminals or spies is C3, even when its prestige makes it 'drama' (The Sopranos, The Wire, Breaking Bad); a legal series about the law firm's own life is Legal Drama.
Daily comedies, crime comedies and true events

A daily or long-running comedy is a sitcom (C4), not a serial tradition, even with thousands of episodes (Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah). A comedy about criminals goes by laughter first (C4). A dramatised real crime is True Crime Drama (C3-7); a dramatised real event that is not a crime is Docudrama Series (C1-9).
A documentary series is C8; a talk, chat or variety programme that is not a cross-border format goes to G3 (variety and talk) as a programme of its own.

A comedy whose fantastical premise only carries the gags is Comedy (C4), not Genre Series (The Addams Family, Wonderfalls); a supernatural or speculative frame on a medical, crime or family series does not make it C5 unless the frame carries the plot. A children's cartoon with an adult following stays Children's Animated Series. News magazines and current-affairs programmes are not series of this tab: exclude them.
Comedy first; thrillers; long-running continuing dramas

A sitcom with a science-fiction, fantasy or horror premise is Comedy (C4) when laughter comes first (Red Dwarf, The League of Gentlemen); comic detectives stay in C3 with C4-5 as see-also. A domestic or psychological thriller miniseries is C3-8. A long-running continuing drama of a workplace (Casualty, Holby City, The Bill) goes by genre (C1-2, C3-1), not D. An Arab 30-episode Ramadan series is D5-1 whatever its genre.
Spin-offs and revivals share their parent's leaf unless they change genre outright.
Ramadan comedies, dizi genres, Arab serials

TV6 wins over TV9 for Ramadan comedies: a Ramadan sitcom or sketch show is C4; only Ramadan drama is D5-1. A Turkish weekly serial in the dizi format stays D3 whatever its genre (crime, action, romantic comedy); only a case-of-the-week police show is C3-1. D3-2 is any dizi set before 1923.

A biographical or religious series of a pre-modern life (prophets, saints, Leonardo) is Period Drama (C1-6); a modern life is Docudrama (C1-9). Series about young adults past school age (college, aspirants, first jobs) go by genre (C1-12, C4-5), not Teen Drama. A remake of a series shares its original's leaf unless it changes genre (TV5).

A streaming serial of 60 or more episodes in a named serial tradition is D; a short web series of the same subject is C. A Nordic Advent serial is C7-3 whatever its genre. A short mythological web series is C5-2 with D4-2 as see-also.
Stage recordings, specials and visual albums

A filmed stage production goes by its stage genre (a musical → A11-1, a stand-up show → A10-12, a play → its genre). A special of a television series that is not a compilation (the South Park streaming specials) is placed with its series → route:FT-C; a music or variety television special is excluded as television. A visual album or long-form music video is Musical Film (A11-1) as a feature, Live-Action Short (B2-3) at 40 minutes or less.

Dinosaurs, giant sharks and other natural monsters are Creature Feature (A4-14) when the film aims to frighten, Science Fiction (A5-3) when it is adventure; only giant monsters of the kaiju tradition are A5-1. A recent homage to a cycle (Malignant, MaXXXine) goes by its own genre with the cycle as see-also (F23). Revenge horror stays horror (A4) when it aims to frighten; a revenge story without horror is A3-5.

A talk, variety, reality, court, instructional or web show is placed in G directly, whether or not it is a licensed format (G2-2 for occupational and paranormal reality, G3-4 for court shows, G3-5 for how-to shows); professional wrestling is G3-1. A documentary series with reenactments is C8 when talking heads and archive carry it, C1-9 when dramatised scenes do. A disaster miniseries is Action & Adventure (C1-15). A US re-edit or dub of an anime is anime (route:FT-E). A defence-lawyer series is Legal Drama (C1-3) when the cases change each week, Crime Drama (C3-3) when a season follows one crime; a lawyer dramedy stays C1-3 with C4-5 as see-also. A 2000s–2010s network serial of secrets among the rich (Revenge, Gossip Girl) is Prime-Time Soap Opera (D2-4); a teen mystery (Pretty Little Liars) is Thriller (C3-6).
Streaming originals in a serial tradition; sports

A streaming original of a closed season (8–20 episodes) from a serial-tradition country (a Netflix or BluTV Turkish series, a streaming telenovela) goes by genre in C; the broadcast weekly or daily serial is D. A remake that leaves its original's tradition goes by its own form (a 60-episode Turkish broadcast remake of Doctor Foster is D3-1). An anthology of crime or suspense stories is C1-16 Anthology with the genre as see-also. Live sports coverage is not a series of this tab: exclude it.

A Chinese drama of the Party, the revolution or national achievement is Main-Melody Drama (C2-12) whatever its genre; one set in 1912–1949 is Republican-Era Drama (C2-13); a modern Chinese romance of any kind is C2-6. A censored danmei adaptation goes by its setting (The Untamed → C2-5) with C2-11 as see-also; a modern-day one is C2-11. A costume drama goes to C2-5 when martial heroes or a fantasy world carry the story, otherwise C2-4.

A foreign remake keeps its original's leaf only when it keeps its form; it goes by its own setting when moved (a US remake of a Nordic series is C3-1, not C3-4). A spin-off that moves to another workplace goes by its own profession. A streaming or 2020s series of rich-family secrets with a closed season is C (C1-1 or C3-8) with D2-4 as see-also; the D2-4 rule of TV13 holds only for network serials of 2000–2019 and long-running streaming serials (TV12).
Japanese and Hong Kong drama; tokusatsu

Every Japanese drama of romance, school, work, family or everyday life is C2-9; Japanese crime, mystery, medical, legal and speculative dramas go by genre with C2-9 as see-also. A Hong Kong drama is C2-14 unless it is wuxia (C2-5); Hong Kong BL is C2-11. A tokusatsu series is C5-6 whatever its audience (Power Rangers included); a tokusatsu parody comedy is C4. A foreign remake of an Asian drama made inside another tradition goes to the remaking tradition (a Japanese remake of a K-drama is C2-9) with the original's leaf as see-also. A New Year or one-off special is route:FT-A; a re-edit or complete edition of a series is excluded as a duplicate.

A Korean weekend or daily family drama is Makjang (C2-3) only when birth secrets, revenge or chaebol schemes drive it; a gentle family drama is C1-1 with C2-3 as see-also. Sageuk (C2-2) ends with the Korean Empire (1910); a drama of the colonial period or later is Period Drama (C1-6) with C2-2 as see-also. A Korean drama goes by genre (C3, C5) only when its genre plot carries it and the love line is secondary; otherwise it is K-Drama (C2-1). A Korean prosecutor or judge drama is Legal Drama (C1-3) unless it follows one crime (C3-3). A one- or two-part drama special is route:FT-A.
Thai and Philippine drama; versions and segments

A Thai drama of romance, youth or revenge is Lakorn (C2-10); a Thai thriller, horror or fantasy series that its genre carries goes by genre with C2-10 as see-also. Any Asian BL or GL series is C2-11 whatever its genre or form; a straight main couple with BL side couples stays in the tradition (C2-10) with C2-11 as see-also. A Philippine broadcast serial is D6-1; a Philippine streaming series goes by genre. Uncut, director's-cut and special-edition versions, anthology segments listed as titles, and bonus or making-of specials are excluded as duplicates or supplements of their series.

A comedy about police that is neither buddy-cop (A8-7) nor spoof is Comedy (A10-1), or Action Comedy (A10-9) when action set-pieces carry it. A past setting 'defines' a film (key step 8) only when the era's events or manners are its subject; a family drama or comedy merely set in the past goes by its genre with A7-4 as see-also (F24).

A hidden-camera, prank or stunt show is G2-4. A transformation story (house, body, business) is G2-3; a show that teaches the craft is G3-5. Recaps, re-edits with pop-up facts and behind-the-scenes companions of a format are excluded as supplements (TV19). A model or talent search judged on performance is G1-1; one built on living together and elimination tasks is G1-2.
Generals, real disasters and narrow-leaf ties

A biopic whose story is a military campaign is War Film (A7-3) with A7-8 as see-also; a soldier's life beyond the war is A7-8. A real disaster told as a social drama of the people in it (a mine rescue) goes by that drama with A5-5 as see-also; A5-5 takes the disaster spectacle. When two narrow leaves tie (sport and road), the one the film's climax belongs to wins.
Manner movies, recap specials and behind-the-scenes supplements of an anime are excluded as supplements of their series; a promotional short with its own story is placed by genre.

Explicit works made to arouse (hardcore pornography, hentai) are classified in the Pleasure Taxonomies, not here; an explicit work made and received as art or mainstream cinema is placed by its genre (In the Realm of the Senses, Caligula). Non-explicit erotic genres and cycles with their own canon stay here (pink film, Roman Porno, erotic drama, sexploitation, erotic thriller, ecchi; shunga in VA-B2-17). Segments of the adult trade with no canon (amateur and creator content, adult magazines, glamour and pin-up photography, late-night cable softcore) are the Pleasure Taxonomies'. Retired here: A12-5, E12-1.
modifiers: Country of origin — a filter (Wikidata P495 first, as in the selection rule; a co-production counts in each of its countries, D8). National cinemas are never divisions; national cycles and movements defined by what the films are (J-horror, Japanese New Wave) are leaves.
Decade and period of release — a filter.
Director, studio, writer — tags; studio-branded cycles are leaves only where the field names them as a genre (Nikkatsu Roman Porno).
Setting — jidaigeki (pre-1868) or gendaigeki (contemporary) as a filter on every Japanese film; a leaf (Jidaigeki) exists only for the period drama genre.
Release format — theatrical, V-cinema (direct-to-video), TV movie, streaming: a filter.
Movement — a tag on every attested member of a named movement (Japanese New Wave), including members placed in a genre cycle (D1).
Format — for anime: TV series, film, OVA, ONA, special (D4). For series: miniseries, limited, ongoing.
Asian drama — the drama database's scope (Korea, China, Japan, Taiwan, Thailand, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Singapore) as a filter on Television Series (D3).
Source material (manga, novel, true story) — a tag.
Language, rating, runtime, platform — tags.
Audience counts (Letterboxd, IMDb, MAL, MDL) — kept internal (licensing); never shown.
Theme — LGBTQ+, disability, faith, sport fandom and similar subjects are tags on any film; they become leaves only as named genres or movements (New Queer Cinema, Christian Film).
Era of production — silent era, pre-Code Hollywood, the studio era, the Golden Age of a national cinema: filters, not leaves.
Series format — miniseries, limited, anthology, ongoing, web series: a filter on Television Series.
Network and platform — HBO, BBC, Netflix, TVB, Globo: tags.
Country of origin — Wikidata P495 (D8); a co-production counts in each country. A filter on every leaf of both families ("British crime drama" = C3 leaves filtered by GB), never a node.
Critical tags — prestige drama, cult film, arthouse, blockbuster: tags, not genres.

What this release holds

This is the first full release of both tabs, built from the pilot's method after your rulings D1–D8 and the accepted F11–F12. Codes are provisional; they freeze at the first frozen release.

Film & Television33236,182 titlesFeature films 17,187 · shorts 820 · television series 11,686 · serial traditions 367 · anime 5,531 · unscripted formats 591.

Every gathered row has one disposition. Film routes and exclusions: 383 routed between families (mostly Japanese animation in the film list → Anime, and anime found in the TV list), 130 excluded with a reason (TV specials, compilations, recaps, duplicates and supplements).

How it was built

  1. Leaves first. Global feature-film leaves (movements, genres, cycles, popular modes), the anime leaves by D4, the television leaves with the Asian drama traditions in C2 by D3, the serial traditions, and the unscripted formats; Visual Art leaves region by region from the gathered pool (tradition-led) and from the artists' attested movements and period styles (artist-led).
  2. Rules propose, reviewers decide. Each title got a rule proposal from its TMDB keywords, overview and Wikidata genre; fresh reviewers then placed batches of about 220 against the leaf list and the precedence sentences (82 film batches, 32 television, 23 Asian drama, 26 anime, 2 unscripted). Recurring seams became new leaves and sentences (F13–F31, AN1–AN11, TV1–TV20, P11–P16), and sweeps re-placed earlier batches when a leaf arrived late.
  3. Hand corrections live in seeds/classify/*_overrides.csv; sweeps in taxonomy/*/review/sweep_*.csv.

Audits

Blind placement test

A fresh rater saw only the keys and the leaf definitions and placed a held-out sample drawn from every family. Film & Television, round 1: 103 of 125 (film 51/60, tv 24/30, anime 19/25, unscripted 9/10); after the fixes, on a new sample, round 2: 107 of 125 (film 51/60, tv 28/30, anime 19/25, unscripted 9/10). Visual Art, round 1: 78 of 100 (tradition row 45/50, architecture style 6/10, artist 27/40); round 2: 75 of 100 (tradition row 47/50, architecture style 8/10, artist 20/40).

The film misses sit on the seams the reviewers also reported: a general's biopic against War Film, comic police films, a period setting that does or does not "define" a family drama, Asian anime comedies against gag anime, and supplements (manner movies, behind-the-scenes cuts). Fixes made: F30, F31, AN11, TV20, Hood Film widened beyond the United States, and overrides for the items where the rater was right.

The Visual Art misses split by kind of row. Tradition rows and architecture styles hold well (the rater agreed on 92 of 100 in round 1 and 2 together for traditions, 14 of 20 for styles); the misses are culture rows that a slice made a kind of one tradition while the rater kept them as place tags (now P14). Artists are the weak spot (27 of 40, then 20 of 40): most artists have no attested movement, and the rater and the period rules disagree on the boundary leaves (academic against modern, modern against contemporary, a photographer or designer with no period leaf) and on artists whose recorded medium is wrong (a railroad photographer recorded as a painter). Fixes made: P15 and P16 (period leaves by birth year for every medium), corrected artists, and the photography, design and poster leaves added after the probes.

Census

Film & Television leaves with no title in this release: A1-34, A12-1, A12-2, E1-8, E3-6 (Pink Film and Roman Porno: the selection has no pink-circuit or Nikkatsu titles; Korean New Wave: its one candidate keeps its neo-noir leaf and carries the movement tag). Visual Art leaves with no kind yet: 148 — attested traditions whose sub-types and makers are not in the gathered evidence. Leaves whose attestation is still weak carry a yellow note on their card: 79 in Visual Art, 6 in Film & Television.

Decisions taken (2026-10-28)

You left these calls to me. They are applied in this release and recorded here so they can be reversed later.

R1 New Hollywood against genre cycles. D1 holds: a Hollywood blockbuster or horror classic by an attested New Hollywood director (Jaws, The Exorcist) keeps its genre leaf and carries the movement as a tag. The movement leaf keeps its members with no genre home.
R2 The inclusion rule. §2.3 stands. One exception: a tradition that fails only because the source does not record it (not because the objects are absent) is admitted. On that ground Gobelins Tapestry and Beauvais Tapestry are leaves. The other 29 below-rule traditions (Dala horse, rosemaling, Quimper, santons, Erzgebirge, Fair Isle, Nottingham alabaster, tartan, Shaker furniture …) stay out and are listed in taxonomy/visual_art/review/gapsweep_europe_below_rule.csv and probefix_below_rule.csv for a later evidence pass.
R3 Medieval illumination. Stays split by P1: the illustrated book as a book (Western illumination schools) is Book Arts C2; a manuscript painting tradition named as painting (Byzantine, Armenian, Persian, Mughal) is Painting A1. The Gothic and Ghent-Bruges artist cells keep their illuminators.
R4 North American settler folk art (Amish quilts, fraktur, decoys, weathervanes, hooked rugs, tramp art) stays as leaves in its media; settler and colonial origin is a filter (P7), not a sub-family.
R5 Intangible-heritage rows with no objects. The line stands: a named craft tradition is a leaf when attested (telepuk, tekat, Daluang); a garment, mat type or performance is excluded (P10).
R6 Artist fallbacks. Period-style leaves are the home for artists with no attested movement (P15, P16). Splitting Modern Art and Contemporary Art further by country is left to the next artist pass.
R7 Movement against medium. Conceptual, Fluxus, mail art, minimal and kinetic artists follow their movement (installation, new media, sculpture), since those movements define the medium.
R8 Scope edges. Fashion designers belong to the Possession taxonomy: those found so far are excluded (Chanel, Doucet), and the rest are left to the next artist pass; manga, Franco-Belgian and American comics stay in Drawings & Prints until a comics tab exists; filmed stage productions go by stage genre (F28); vertical micro-dramas keep their leaf (C1-17); BL and GL share one leaf (C2-11).
R9 Animated television specials. The 40-minute line holds; longer specials (Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer) are animated features with B1-5 as see-also.
R10 Weak attestations. Accepted for this release; the yellow notes stay on the cards until a better source is found.

Your open items

  • Black Rain (Imamura, 1989) is added to the film selection and placed in Atomic Bomb Film. The Japan 1980s top-up took films that were all above the main bar, so it added nothing below it; other near misses there: Godzilla 1985, Sweet Home, Mermaid Legend.
  • Difret was fourth in its Ethiopia 2010s cell (the top-up takes three after Lamb); added by hand.
  • Japanese animated films: matched to the anime list through MAL synonyms and Wikidata MAL IDs; 12 remain unmatched, 5 turned out to be live action and are placed as films.
  • Aboriginal artists are attached to Western Desert Painting (art centres as kinds), Bark Painting, the Hermannsburg School and Contemporary Indigenous Australian Art.
  • Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi was not in the TV selection (2,269 IMDb votes, below the 2,500 bar). It is the defining saas-bahu serial and the example of Indian Daily Soap (D4-1), so it is added by hand and placed there.
  • Korean anime: the country top-up now includes South Korea (+9 titles, Pucca among them).
  • Licensing: audience counts stay in the repository; the page carries titles, years, makers, IDs and notes only.
